units.label: Verse 1
units.deva:
सर्व-वेदान्त-सिद्धान्त-गोचरं तमगोचरम् ।
गोविन्दं परमानन्दं सद्-गुरुं प्रणतोऽस्म्यहम् ॥
units.iast:
sarva-vedānta-siddhānta-gocaraṃ tamagocaram |
govindaṃ paramānandaṃ sad-guruṃ praṇato'smyaham ||
units.translation: I bow to Govinda, supreme bliss and the true teacher, within the scope of all Vedānta doctrine, yet beyond every ordinary reach.

gloss.en: within the range of all Vedānta conclusions

units.editionTranslation: I bow to Govinda, whose nature is Bliss Supreme, who is the Sadguru, who can be known only from the import of all Vedanta, and who is beyond the reach of speech and mind.

units.label: Verse 2
units.deva:
जन्तूनां नरजन्म दुर्लभमतः पुंस्त्वं ततो विप्रता
तस्माद्वैदिकधर्ममार्गपरता विद्वत्त्वमस्मात्परम् ।
आत्मानात्म-विवेचनं स्वनुभवो ब्रह्मात्मना संस्थितिः
मुक्तिर् नो शत-जन्म-कोटि-सुकृतैः पुण्यैर् विना लभ्यते ॥
units.iast:
jantūnāṃ narajanma durlabhamataḥ puṃstvaṃ tato vipratā
tasmādvaidikadharmamārgaparatā vidvattvamasmātparam |
ātmānātma-vivecanaṃ svanubhavo brahmātmanā saṃsthitiḥ
muktir no śata-janma-koṭi-sukṛtaiḥ puṇyair vinā labhyate ||
units.translation: Among beings, human birth is hard to obtain; harder still is manhood; then Brāhmaṇa status; then commitment to the Vedic dharma path; then learning. Higher still are discrimination between Self and not-Self, direct experience, and abiding as Brahman. Liberation is not gained without merits accumulated through a hundred crore births.

gloss.en: commitment to the Vedic dharma path
by merits from a hundred crore births

units.editionTranslation: For all beings a human birth is difficult to obtain, more so is a male body; rarer than that is Brahmanahood; rarer still is the attachment to the path of Vedic religion; higher than this is erudition in the scriptures; discrimination between the Self and not-Self, Realisation, and continuing in a state of identity with Brahman – these come next in order. (This kind of) Mukti (Liberation) is not to be attained except through the well-earned merits of a hundred crore of births.

units.label: Verse 3
units.deva:
दुर्लभं त्रयम् एवैतद्देवानुग्रहहेतुकम् ।
मनुष्यत्वं मुमुक्षुत्वं महापुरुषसंश्रयः ॥
units.iast:
durlabhaṃ trayam evaitaddevānugrahahetukam |
manuṣyatvaṃ mumukṣutvaṃ mahāpuruṣasaṃśrayaḥ ||
units.translation: These three are indeed rare and come from divine grace: human birth, desire for liberation, and refuge with a great sage.
units.editionTranslation: These are three things which are rare indeed and are due to the grace of God – namely, a human birth, the longing for Liberation, and the protecting care of a perfected sage.

units.label: Verse 4
units.deva:
लब्ध्वा कथंचिन् नरजन्म दुर्लभं
तत्रापि पुंस्त्वं श्रुतिपारदर्शनम् ।
यस्त्व् आत्म-मुक्तौ न यतेत मूढधीः
स ह्य् आत्म-हा स्वं विनिहन्त्यसद्ग्रहात् ॥
units.iast:
labdhvā kathaṃcin narajanma durlabhaṃ
tatrāpi puṃstvaṃ śrutipāradarśanam |
yastv ātma-muktau na yateta mūḍhadhīḥ
sa hy ātma-hā svaṃ vinihantyasadgrahāt ||
units.translation: Having somehow obtained rare human birth, and even manhood and mastery of śruti, the dull-minded person who does not strive for freedom of the Self is a self-killer: he destroys himself by grasping what is unreal.
units.editionTranslation: The man who, having by some means obtained a human birth, with a male body and mastery of the Vedas to boot, is foolish enough not to exert himself for self-liberation, verily commits suicide, for he kills himself by clinging to things unreal.

units.label: Verse 5
units.deva:
इतः को न्वस्ति मूढात्मा यस् तु स्वार्थे प्रमाद्यति ।
दुर्लभं मानुषं देहं प्राप्य तत्रापि पौरुषम् ॥
units.iast:
itaḥ ko nvasti mūḍhātmā yas tu svārthe pramādyati |
durlabhaṃ mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ prāpya tatrāpi pauruṣam ||
units.translation: Who is more foolish than one who neglects his own aim, having gained a rare human body and even manhood?
units.editionTranslation: What greater fool is there than the man who having obtained a rare human body, and a masculine body too, neglects to achieve the real end of this life ?

units.label: Verse 6
units.deva:
वदन्तु शास्त्राणि यजन्तु देवान्
कुर्वन्तु कर्माणि भजन्तु देवताः ।
आत्मैक्यबोधेन विनापि मुक्तिः
न सिध्यति ब्रह्मशतान्तरेऽपि ॥
units.iast:
vadantu śāstrāṇi yajantu devān
kurvantu karmāṇi bhajantu devatāḥ |
ātmaikyabodhena vināpi muktiḥ
na sidhyati brahmaśatāntare'pi ||
units.translation: Let them recite the śāstras, sacrifice to the gods, perform rites, and worship the deities; without knowledge of the Self’s oneness, liberation is not achieved, even in a hundred lifetimes of Brahmā.

gloss.en: by knowledge of the Self’s oneness
in a hundred lifetimes of Brahmā

units.editionTranslation: Let people quote the Scriptures and sacrifice to the gods, let them perform rituals and worship the deities, but there is no Liberation without the realisation of one’s identity with the Atman, no, not even in the lifetime of a hundred Brahmas put together.

units.label: Verse 7
units.deva:
अमृतत्वस्य नाशास्ति वित्तेनेत्य् एव हि श्रुतिः ।
ब्रवीति कर्मणो मुक्तेरहेतुत्वं स्फुटं यतः ॥
units.iast:
amṛtatvasya nāśāsti vittenety eva hi śrutiḥ |
bravīti karmaṇo mukterahetutvaṃ sphuṭaṃ yataḥ ||
units.translation: Śruti indeed declares: there is no hope of immortality through wealth. It clearly says that action is not the cause of liberation.
units.editionTranslation: There is no hope of immortality by means of riches – such indeed is the declaration of the Vedas. Hence it is clear that works cannot be the cause of Liberation.

units.label: Verse 8
units.deva:
अतो विमुक्त्यै प्रयतेत् विद्वान्
संन्यस्तबाह्यार्थसुखस्पृहः सन् ।
सन्तं महान्तं समुपेत्य देशिकं
तेनोपदिष्टार्थसमाहितात्मा ॥
units.iast:
ato vimuktyai prayatet vidvān
saṃnyastabāhyārthasukhaspṛhaḥ san |
santaṃ mahāntaṃ samupetya deśikaṃ
tenopadiṣṭārthasamāhitātmā ||
units.translation: Therefore a learned person should strive for liberation, having given up desire for pleasure from outer things. Having approached a good, great teacher, one should steady the mind on the meaning taught by him.

gloss.en: having given up desire for pleasure from outer things

units.editionTranslation: Therefore the man of learning should strive his best for Liberation, having renounced his desire for pleasures from external objects, duly approaching a good and generous preceptor, and fixing his mind on the truth inculcated by him.

units.label: Verse 9
units.deva:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं मग्नं संसारवारिधौ ।
योगारूढत्वमासाद्य सम्यग्दर्शननिष्ठया ॥
units.iast:
uddharedātmanātmānaṃ magnaṃ saṃsāravāridhau |
yogārūḍhatvamāsādya samyagdarśananiṣṭhayā ||
units.translation: One should lift oneself by oneself, sunk in the ocean of saṃsāra, by steadfastness in right vision, having attained the state of being established in yoga.

gloss.en: the state of being established in yoga

units.editionTranslation: Having attained the Yogarudha state, one should recover oneself, immersed in the sea of birth and death by means of devotion to right discrimination.

units.label: Verse 10
units.deva:
संन्यस्य सर्वकर्माणि भवबन्धविमुक्तये ।
यत्यतां पण्डितैर् धीरैर् आत्माभ्यास उपस्थितैः ॥
units.iast:
saṃnyasya sarvakarmāṇi bhavabandhavimuktaye |
yatyatāṃ paṇḍitair dhīrair ātmābhyāsa upasthitaiḥ ||
units.translation: Having renounced all actions for release from the bond of existence, let learned and steady people strive, engaged in the practice of the Self.

gloss.en: for release from the bond of existence
in the practice of the Self

units.editionTranslation: Let the wise and erudite man, having commenced the practice of the realisation of the Atman give up all works and try to cut loose the bonds of birth and death.

units.label: Verse 11
units.deva:
चित्तस्य शुद्धये कर्म न तु वस्तूपलब्धये ।
वस्तुसिद्धिर्विचारेण न किंचित् कर्मकोटिभिः ॥
units.iast:
cittasya śuddhaye karma na tu vastūpalabdhaye |
vastusiddhirvicāreṇa na kiṃcit karmakoṭibhiḥ ||
units.translation: Action is for purification of the mind, not for grasping Reality. Reality is established by inquiry, and not by ten million actions.
units.editionTranslation: Work leads to purification of the mind, not to perception of the Reality. The realisation of Truth is brought about by discrimination and not in the least by ten million of acts.

units.label: Verse 12
units.deva:
सम्यग्विचारतः सिद्धा रज्जुतत्त्वावधारणा ।
भ्रान्तोदितमहासर्पभयदुःखविनाशिनी ॥
units.iast:
samyagvicārataḥ siddhā rajjutattvāvadhāraṇā |
bhrāntoditamahāsarpabhayaduḥkhavināśinī ||
units.translation: By proper inquiry, the truth of the rope is established, destroying the fear and pain of the great snake that arose through delusion.

gloss.en: certainty about the truth of the rope

units.editionTranslation: By adequate reasoning the conviction of the reality about the rope is gained, which puts an end to the great fear and misery caused by the snake worked up in the deluded mind.

units.label: Verse 13
units.deva:
अर्थस्य निश्चयो दृष्टो विचारेण हितोक्तितः ।
न स्नानेन न दानेन प्राणायमशतेन वा ॥
units.iast:
arthasya niścayo dṛṣṭo vicāreṇa hitoktitaḥ |
na snānena na dānena prāṇāyamaśatena vā ||
units.translation: The truth is settled by inquiry based on beneficial teaching, not by bathing, giving, or a hundred breath-control practices.
units.editionTranslation: The conviction of the Truth is seen to proceed from reasoning upon the salutary counsel of the wise, and not by bathing in the sacred waters, nor by gifts, nor by a hundred Pranayamas (control of the vital force).

units.label: Verse 14
units.deva:
अधिकारिणमाशास्ते फलसिद्धिर्विशेषतः ।
उपाया देशकालाद्याः सन्त्यस्मिन्सहकारिणः ॥
units.iast:
adhikāriṇamāśāste phalasiddhirviśeṣataḥ |
upāyā deśakālādyāḥ santyasminsahakāriṇaḥ ||
units.translation: Success depends chiefly on the qualified person. Means such as place and time are helpers here.
units.editionTranslation: Success depends essentially on a qualified aspirant; time, place and other such means are but auxiliaries in this regard.

units.label: Verse 15
units.deva:
अतो विचारः कर्तव्यो जिज्ञासोर् आत्मवस्तुनः ।
समासाद्य दयासिन्धुं गुरुं ब्रह्मविदुत्तमम् ॥
units.iast:
ato vicāraḥ kartavyo jijñāsor ātmavastunaḥ |
samāsādya dayāsindhuṃ guruṃ brahmaviduttamam ||
units.translation: Therefore, the seeker after the reality of the Self should inquire, having approached a compassionate teacher, the best knower of Brahman.

gloss.en: of the reality of the Self

units.editionTranslation: Hence the seeker after the Reality of the Atman should take to reasoning, after duly approaching the Guru – who should be the best of the knowers of Brahman, and an ocean of mercy.

units.label: Verse 16
units.deva:
मेधावी पुरुषो विद्वानुहापोहविचक्षणः ।
अधिकार्यात्मविद्यायामुक्तलक्षणलक्षितः ॥
units.iast:
medhāvī puruṣo vidvānuhāpohavicakṣaṇaḥ |
adhikāryātmavidyāyāmuktalakṣaṇalakṣitaḥ ||
units.translation: The intelligent, learned person, skilled in reasoning for and against, and marked by the stated qualities, is qualified for Self-knowledge.

gloss.en: skilled in reasoning for and against

units.editionTranslation: An intelligent and learned man skilled in arguing in favour of the Scriptures and in refuting counter-arguments against them – one who has got the above characteristics is the fit recipient of the knowledge of the Atman.

units.label: Verse 17
units.deva:
विवेकिनो विरक्तस्य शमादिगुणशालिनः ।
मुमुक्षोर् एव हि ब्रह्मजिज्ञासायोग्यता मता ॥
units.iast:
vivekino viraktasya śamādiguṇaśālinaḥ |
mumukṣor eva hi brahmajijñāsāyogyatā matā ||
units.translation: Only the discriminating, dispassionate seeker, endowed with calm and the other qualities and longing for liberation, is considered qualified to inquire into Brahman.

gloss.en: endowed with calm and the other qualities

units.editionTranslation: The man who discriminates between the Real and the unreal, whose mind is turned away from the unreal, who possesses calmness and the allied virtues, and who is longing for Liberation, is alone considered qualified to enquire after Brahman.

units.label: Verse 18
units.deva:
साधनान्यत्र चत्वारि कथितानि मनीषिभिः ।
येषु सत्स्व् एव सन्निष्ठा यदभावे न सिध्यति ॥
units.iast:
sādhanānyatra catvāri kathitāni manīṣibhiḥ |
yeṣu satsv eva sanniṣṭhā yadabhāve na sidhyati ||
units.translation: Sages have stated four means here. When they are present, commitment is firm; without them, it does not succeed.
units.editionTranslation: Regarding this, sages have spoken of four means of attainment, which alone being present, the devotion to Brahman succeeds, and in the absence of which, it fails.

units.label: Verse 19
units.deva:
आदौ नित्यानित्यवस्तुविवेकः परिगम्यते ।
इहामुत्रफलभोगविरागस्तदनन्तरम्

शमादिषट्कसम्पत्तिर्मुमुक्षुत्वमिति स्फुटम् ॥
units.iast:
ādau nityānityavastuvivekaḥ parigamyate |
ihāmutraphalabhogavirāgastadanantaram

śamādiṣaṭkasampattirmumukṣutvamiti sphuṭam ||
units.translation: First is stated discrimination between eternal and non-eternal things; next is dispassion toward enjoying results here and hereafter; then the six qualities beginning with calmness, and clearly, desire for liberation.

gloss.en: discrimination between eternal and non-eternal things
endowment of six qualities beginning with calmness

units.editionTranslation: First is enumerated discrimination between the Real and the unreal; next comes aversion to the enjoyment of fruits (of one’s actions) here and hereafter; (next is) the group of six attributes, viz. calmness and the rest; and (last) is clearly the yearning for Liberation.

units.label: Verse 20
units.deva:
ब्रह्म सत्यं जगन्मिथ्येत्य् एवंरूपो विनिश्चयः ।
सोऽयं नित्यानित्यवस्तुविवेकः समुदाहृतः ॥
units.iast:
brahma satyaṃ jaganmithyety evaṃrūpo viniścayaḥ |
so'yaṃ nityānityavastuvivekaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ ||
units.translation: The firm conviction “Brahman alone is real; the world is unreal” is called discrimination between eternal and non-eternal things.

gloss.en: discrimination between eternal and non-eternal things

units.editionTranslation: A firm conviction of the mind to the effect that Brahman is real and the universe unreal, is designated as discrimination (Viveka) between the Real and the unreal.

units.label: Verse 21
units.deva:
तद्वैराग्यं जिहासा या दर्शनश्रवणादिभिः ।
देहादिब्रह्मपर्यन्ते ह्यनित्ये भोगवस्तुनि ॥
units.iast:
tadvairāgyaṃ jihāsā yā darśanaśravaṇādibhiḥ |
dehādibrahmaparyante hyanitye bhogavastuni ||
units.translation: That dispassion is indeed the desire to give up, through seeing, hearing, and the like, the impermanent object of enjoyment extending from the body up to Brahmā.

gloss.en: through seeing, hearing, and the like

units.editionTranslation: Vairagya or renunciation is the desire to give up all transitory enjoyments (ranging) from those of an (animate) body to those of Brahmahood (having already known their defects) from observation, instruction and so forth.

units.label: Verse 22
units.deva:
विरज्य विषयव्राताद्दोषदृष्ट्या मुहुर्मुहुः ।
स्वलक्ष्ये नियतावस्था मनसः शम उच्यते ॥
units.iast:
virajya viṣayavrātāddoṣadṛṣṭyā muhurmuhuḥ |
svalakṣye niyatāvasthā manasaḥ śama ucyate ||
units.translation: After becoming dispassionate from the multitude of sense objects by seeing their faults again and again, the mind’s steady abiding in its own aim is called śama (calm).

gloss.en: from the multitude of sense objects

units.editionTranslation: The resting of the mind steadfastly on its Goal (viz. Brahman) after having detached itself from manifold sense-objects by continually observing their defects, is called Shama or calmness.

units.label: Verse 23
units.deva:
विषयेभ्यः परावर्त्य स्थापनं स्वस्वगोलके ।
उभयेषामिन्द्रियाणां स दमः परिकीर्तितः

बाह्यानालम्बनं वृत्तेरेषोपरतिरुत्तमा ॥
units.iast:
viṣayebhyaḥ parāvartya sthāpanaṃ svasvagolake |
ubhayeṣāmindriyāṇāṃ sa damaḥ parikīrtitaḥ

bāhyānālambanaṃ vṛttereṣoparatiruttamā ||
units.translation: Turning both kinds of sense faculties away from sense objects and placing them in their respective spheres is called dama (self-restraint). The mind’s non-reliance on external things is the highest uparati (withdrawal).
units.editionTranslation: Turning both kinds of sense-organs away from sense-objects and placing them in their respective centres, is called Dama or self-control. The best Uparati or self-withdrawal consists in the mind-function ceasing to be affected by external objects.

units.label: Verse 24
units.deva:
सहनं सर्वदुःखानामप्रतीकारपूर्वकम् ।
चिन्ताविलापरहितं सा तितिक्षा निगद्यते ॥
units.iast:
sahanaṃ sarvaduḥkhānāmapratīkārapūrvakam |
cintāvilāparahitaṃ sā titikṣā nigadyate ||
units.translation: Enduring all suffering without counteracting it, free from worry and lamentation, is called titikṣā (forbearance).
units.editionTranslation: The bearing of all afflictions without caring to redress them, being free (at the same time) from anxiety or lament on their score, is called Titiksha or forbearance.

units.label: Verse 25
units.deva:
शास्त्रस्य गुरुवाक्यस्य सत्यबुद्ध्यवधारणम् ।
सा श्रद्धा कथिता सद्भिर्यया वस्तूपलभ्यते ॥
units.iast:
śāstrasya guruvākyasya satyabuddhyavadhāraṇam |
sā śraddhā kathitā sadbhiryayā vastūpalabhyate ||
units.translation: A firm conviction that scripture and the teacher’s words are true is called śraddhā (trust) by the wise; through it, reality is realized.

gloss.en: with the conviction that they are true

units.editionTranslation: Acceptance by firm judgment as true of what the Scriptures and the Guru instruct, is called by sages Shraddha or faith, by means of which the Reality is perceived.

units.label: Verse 26
units.deva:
सर्वदा स्थापनं बुद्धेः शुद्धे ब्रह्मणि सर्वदा ।
तत्समाधानमित्युक्तं न तु चित्तस्य लालनम् ॥
units.iast:
sarvadā sthāpanaṃ buddheḥ śuddhe brahmaṇi sarvadā |
tatsamādhānamityuktaṃ na tu cittasya lālanam ||
units.translation: Always keeping the intellect fixed in pure Brahman, at all times, is called samādhāna; it is not indulging the mind.
units.editionTranslation: Not the mere indulgence of thought (in curiosity) but the constant concentration of the intellect (or the affirming faculty) on the ever-pure Brahman, is what is called Samadhana or self-settledness.

units.label: Verse 27
units.deva:
अहंकारादिदेहान्तान् बन्धानज्ञानकल्पितान् ।
स्वस्वरूपावबोधेन मोक्तुमिच्छा मुमुक्षुता ॥
units.iast:
ahaṃkārādidehāntān bandhānajñānakalpitān |
svasvarūpāvabodhena moktumicchā mumukṣutā ||
units.translation: The desire to free oneself, through knowing one’s true nature, from bonds imagined by ignorance that extend from ego to body is mumukṣutā (yearning for liberation).
units.editionTranslation: Mumukshuta or yearning for Freedom is the desire to free oneself, by realising one’s true nature, from all bondages from that of egoism to that of the body – bondages superimposed by Ignorance.

units.label: Verse 28
units.deva:
मन्दमध्यमरूपापि वैराग्येण शमादिना ।
प्रसादेन गुरोः सेयं प्रवृद्धा सूयते फलम् ॥
units.iast:
mandamadhyamarūpāpi vairāgyeṇa śamādinā |
prasādena guroḥ seyaṃ pravṛddhā sūyate phalam ||
units.translation: Even when weak or moderate in degree, this yearning, strengthened by dispassion and practices such as śama, and by the guru’s grace, bears fruit.

gloss.en: through śama and the other practices

units.editionTranslation: Even though torpid or mediocre, this yearning for Freedom, through the grace of the Guru, may bear fruit (being developed) by means of Vairagya (renunciation), Shama (calmness), and so on.

units.label: Verse 29
units.deva:
वैराग्यं च मुमुक्षुत्वं तीव्रं यस्य तु विद्यते ।
तस्मिन्नेवार्थवन्तः स्युः फलवन्तः शमादयः ॥
units.iast:
vairāgyaṃ ca mumukṣutvaṃ tīvraṃ yasya tu vidyate |
tasminnevārthavantaḥ syuḥ phalavantaḥ śamādayaḥ ||
units.translation: Indeed, only for the person in whom dispassion and yearning for liberation are intense do śama and the other practices have meaning and bear fruit.
units.editionTranslation: In his case, verily, whose renunciation and yearning for Freedom are intense, calmness and the other practices have (really) their meaning and bear fruit.

units.label: Verse 30
units.deva:
एतयोर् मन्दता यत्र विरक्तत्वमुमुक्षयोः ।
मरौ सलीलवत्तत्र शमादेर्भानमात्रता ॥
units.iast:
etayor mandatā yatra viraktatvamumukṣayoḥ |
marau salīlavattatra śamāderbhānamātratā ||
units.translation: Where dispassion and yearning for liberation are weak, śama and the other practices are merely apparent, like water in a desert.

gloss.en: in dispassion and yearning for liberation
of śama and the other practices

units.editionTranslation: Where (however) this renunciation and yearning for Freedom are torpid, there calmness and the other practices are as mere appearances, like water in a desert.

units.label: Verse 31
units.deva:
मोक्षकारणसामग्र्यां भक्तिर् एव गरीयसी ।
स्वस्वरूपानुसन्धानं भक्तिरित्यभिधीयते ॥
units.iast:
mokṣakāraṇasāmagryāṃ bhaktir eva garīyasī |
svasvarūpānusandhānaṃ bhaktirityabhidhīyate ||
units.translation: Among all the means for liberation, devotion alone is highest. Inquiry into one’s own true nature is called devotion.

gloss.en: among the complete set of means for liberation
inquiry into one’s own true nature

units.editionTranslation: Among things conducive to Liberation, devotion (Bhakti) holds the supreme place. The seeking after one’s real nature is designated as devotion.

units.label: Verse 32
units.deva:
स्वात्मतत्त्वानुसन्धानं भक्तिरित्यपरे जगुः ।
उक्तसाधनसंपन्नस्तत्त्वजिज्ञासुरात्मनः

उपसीदेद्गुरुं प्राज्ञं यस्माद्बन्धविमोक्षणम् ॥
units.iast:
svātmatattvānusandhānaṃ bhaktirityapare jaguḥ |
uktasādhanasaṃpannastattvajijñāsurātmanaḥ

upasīdedguruṃ prājñaṃ yasmādbandhavimokṣaṇam ||
units.translation: Others say that inquiry into the truth of one’s own Self is devotion. A seeker who has the qualifications just stated and wants to know the truth of the Self should approach a wise teacher, from whom release from bondage comes.

gloss.en: inquiry into the truth of one’s own Self
endowed with the qualifications just stated

units.editionTranslation: Others maintain that the inquiry into the truth of one’s own self is devotion. The inquirer about the truth of the Atman who is possessed of the above-mentioned means of attainment should approach a wise preceptor, who confers emancipation from bondage.

units.label: Verse 33
units.deva:
श्रोत्रियोऽवृजिनोऽकामहतो यो ब्रह्मवित्तमः ।
ब्रह्मण्य् उपरतः शान्तो निरिन्धन इवानलः

अहेतुकदयासिन्धुर्बन्धुरानमतां सताम् ॥
units.iast:
śrotriyo'vṛjino'kāmahato yo brahmavittamaḥ |
brahmaṇy uparataḥ śānto nirindhana ivānalaḥ

ahetukadayāsindhurbandhurānamatāṃ satām ||
units.translation: A teacher is learned in the Veda, free from sin, untouched by desire, foremost among knowers of Brahman, at rest in Brahman, and peaceful like a fire without fuel; an ocean of causeless compassion and a friend to virtuous people who bow to him.
units.editionTranslation: Who is versed in the Vedas, sinless, unsmitten by desire and a knower of Brahman par excellence, who has withdrawn himself into Brahman; who is calm, like fire that has consumed its fuel, who is a boundless reservoir of mercy that knows no reason, and a friend of all good people who prostrate themselves before him.

units.label: Verse 34
units.deva:
तमाराध्य गुरुं भक्त्या प्रह्वप्रश्रयसेवनैः ।
प्रसन्नं तमनुप्राप्य पृच्छेज्ज्ञातव्यमात्मनः ॥
units.iast:
tamārādhya guruṃ bhaktyā prahvapraśrayasevanaiḥ |
prasannaṃ tamanuprāpya pṛcchejjñātavyamātmanaḥ ||
units.translation: Having honored that teacher with devotion, bowing, humility, and service, and approaching him when he is pleased, one should ask what is to be known about the Self.
units.editionTranslation: Worshipping that Guru with devotion, and approaching him, when he is pleased with prostration, humility and service, (he) should ask him what he has got to know:

units.label: Verse 35
units.deva:
स्वामिन् नमस्ते नतलोकबन्धो
कारुण्यसिन्धो पतितं भवाब्धौ ।
मामुद्धरात्मीयकटाक्षदृष्ट्या
ऋज्व्यातिकारुण्यसुधाभिवृष्ट्या ॥
units.iast:
svāmin namaste natalokabandho
kāruṇyasindho patitaṃ bhavābdhau |
māmuddharātmīyakaṭākṣadṛṣṭyā
ṛjvyātikāruṇyasudhābhivṛṣṭyā ||
units.translation: O Master, salutations to you, friend of those who bow, ocean of compassion. Lift me, fallen in the ocean of existence, with your own gracious sidelong glance, direct and showering the nectar of supreme compassion.

gloss.en: O friend of those who bow
with your own gracious sidelong glance
showering the nectar of supreme compassion

units.editionTranslation: O Master, O friend of those that bow to thee, thou ocean of mercy, I bow to thee; save me, fallen as I am into this sea of birth and death, with a straightforward glance of thine eye, which sheds nectar-like grace supreme.

units.label: Verse 36
units.deva:
दुर्वारसंसारदवाग्नितप्तं
दोधूयमानं दुरदृष्टवातैः ।
भीतं प्रपन्नं परिपाहि मृत्योः
शरण्यमन्यद्यदहं न जाने ॥
units.iast:
durvārasaṃsāradavāgnitaptaṃ
dodhūyamānaṃ duradṛṣṭavātaiḥ |
bhītaṃ prapannaṃ paripāhi mṛtyoḥ
śaraṇyamanyadyadahaṃ na jāne ||
units.translation: Protect me from death: I am scorched by the hard-to-resist forest fire of worldly existence, shaken by the winds of misfortune, frightened, and seeking refuge in you. I know no other shelter.
units.editionTranslation: Save me from death, afflicted as I am by the unquenchable fire of this world-forest, and shaken violently by the winds of an untoward lot, terrified and (so) seeking refuge in thee, for I do not know of any other man with whom to seek shelter.

units.label: Verse 37
units.deva:
शान्ता महान्तो निवसन्ति सन्तो
वसन्तवल्लोकहितं चरन्तः ।
तीर्णाः स्वयं भीमभवार्णवं जनान्
अहेतुना अन्यान् अपि तारयन्तः ॥
units.iast:
śāntā mahānto nivasanti santo
vasantavallokahitaṃ carantaḥ |
tīrṇāḥ svayaṃ bhīmabhavārṇavaṃ janān
ahetunā anyān api tārayantaḥ ||
units.translation: Peaceful, great saints live in the world, working for its welfare like spring. Having crossed the dreadful ocean of becoming themselves, they ferry other people across it too, without motive.
units.editionTranslation: There are good souls, calm and magnanimous, who do good to others as does the spring, and who, having themselves crossed this dreadful ocean of birth and death, help others also to cross the same, without any motive whatsoever.

units.label: Verse 38
units.deva:
अयं स्वभावः स्वत एव यत्पर-
श्रमापनोदप्रवणं महात्मनाम् ।
सुधांशुरेष स्वयमर्ककर्कश-
प्रभाभितप्तामवति क्षितिं किल ॥
units.iast:
ayaṃ svabhāvaḥ svata eva yatpara-
śramāpanodapravaṇaṃ mahātmanām |
sudhāṃśureṣa svayamarkakarkaśa-
prabhābhitaptāmavati kṣitiṃ kila ||
units.translation: This is the nature of great souls: they are naturally inclined to relieve others’ suffering. The moon itself indeed protects the earth scorched by the sun’s harsh rays.

gloss.en: scorched by the sun’s harsh rays

units.editionTranslation: It is the very nature of the magnanimous to move of their own accord towards removing others’ troubles. Here, for instance, is the moon who, as everybody knows, voluntarily saves the earth parched by the flaming rays of the sun.

units.label: Verse 39
units.deva:
ब्रह्मानन्दरसानुभूतिकलितैः पूर्तैः सुशीतैर् युतैः
युष्मद्वाक्कलशोज्झितैः श्रुतिसुखैर् वाक्यामृतैः सेचय ।
संतप्तं भवतापदावदहनज्वालाभिरेनं प्रभो
धन्यास्ते भवदीक्षणक्षणगतेः पात्रीकृताः स्वीकृताः ॥
units.iast:
brahmānandarasānubhūtikalitaiḥ pūrtaiḥ suśītair yutaiḥ
yuṣmadvākkalaśojjhitaiḥ śrutisukhair vākyāmṛtaiḥ secaya |
saṃtaptaṃ bhavatāpadāvadahanajvālābhirenaṃ prabho
dhanyāste bhavadīkṣaṇakṣaṇagateḥ pātrīkṛtāḥ svīkṛtāḥ ||
units.translation: O Lord, sprinkle me—scorched by the flames of worldly affliction—with nectar-like words from your speech, filled with the taste of Brahman-bliss, complete, very cool, and pleasant to hear. Blessed are those made worthy and accepted as your own when your glance falls on them even for a moment.

gloss.en: filled with the taste of experiencing Brahman-bliss
poured from the vessel of your speech
by the flames of worldly affliction

units.editionTranslation: O Lord, with thy nectar-like speech, sweetened by the enjoyment of the elixir-like bliss of Brahman, pure, cooling to a degree, issuing in streams from thy lips as from a pitcher, and delightful to the ear – do thou sprinkle me who am tormented by worldly afflictions as by the tongues of a forest-fire. Blessed are those on whom even a passing glance of thy eye lights, accepting them as thine own.

units.label: Verse 40
units.deva:
कथं तरेयं भवसिन्धुमेतं
का वा गतिर्मे कतमोऽस्त्य् उपायः ।
जाने न किञ्चित्कृपयाव मां प्रभो
संसारदुःखक्षतिमातनुष्व ॥
units.iast:
kathaṃ tareyaṃ bhavasindhumetaṃ
kā vā gatirme katamo'sty upāyaḥ |
jāne na kiñcitkṛpayāva māṃ prabho
saṃsāraduḥkhakṣatimātanuṣva ||
units.translation: How can I cross this ocean of existence? What is my path, and what means are there? I know nothing. Out of compassion, protect me, O Lord, and bring an end to the suffering of saṃsāra.
units.editionTranslation: How to cross this ocean of phenomenal existence, what is to be my fate, and which of the means should I adopt – as to these I know nothing. Condescend to save me, O Lord, and describe at length how to put an end to the misery of this relative existence.

units.label: Verse 41
units.deva:
तथा वदन्तं शरणागतं स्वं
संसारदावानलतापतप्तम् ।
निरीक्ष्य कारुण्यरसार्द्रदृष्ट्या
दद्यादभीतिं सहसा महात्मा ॥
units.iast:
tathā vadantaṃ śaraṇāgataṃ svaṃ
saṃsāradāvānalatāpataptam |
nirīkṣya kāruṇyarasārdradṛṣṭyā
dadyād abhītiṃ sahasā mahātmā ||
units.translation: Seeing his own [disciple] speaking thus, having sought refuge and scorched by the heat of saṃsāra’s forest fire, the great soul should at once grant fearlessness with a glance softened by compassion.

gloss.en: scorched by the heat of saṃsāra’s forest fire
with a glance softened by compassion

units.editionTranslation: As he speaks thus, tormented by the afflictions of the world – which is like a forest on fire – and seeking his protection, the saint eyes him with a glance softened with pity and spontaneously bids him give up all fear.

units.label: Verse 42
units.deva:
विद्वान् स तस्मा उपसत्तिमीयुषे
मुमुक्षवे साधु यथोक्तकारिणे ।
प्रशान्तचित्ताय शमान्विताय
तत्त्वोपदेशं कृपयैव कुर्यात् ॥
units.iast:
vidvān sa tasmā upasattim īyuṣe
mumukṣave sādhu yathoktakāriṇe |
praśāntacittāya śamānvitāya
tattvopadeśaṃ kṛpayaiva kuryāt ||
units.translation: The wise teacher should, out of compassion, teach the truth to the seeker of liberation who has approached for instruction, acts as taught, has a peaceful mind, and is endowed with calm.

gloss.en: to one who acts as instructed
to one whose mind is peaceful

units.editionTranslation: To him who has sought his protection, thirsting for Liberation, who duly obeys the injunctions of the Scriptures, who is of a serene mind, and endowed with calmness – (to such a one) the sage proceeds to inculcate the truth out of sheer grace.

units.label: Verse 43
units.deva:
मा भैष्ट विद्वंस्तव नास्त्य् अपायः
संसारसिन्धोस्तरणेऽस्त्य् उपायः ।
येनैव याता यतयोऽस्य पारं
तम् एव मार्गं तव निर्दिशामि ॥
units.iast:
mā bhaiṣṭa vidvaṃs tava nāsty apāyaḥ
saṃsārasindhos taraṇe 'sty upāyaḥ |
yenaiva yātā yatayo 'sya pāraṃ
tam eva mārgaṃ tava nirdiśāmi ||
units.translation: Do not fear, wise one; no danger threatens you. There is a means to cross the ocean of saṃsāra. I will point out to you that very path by which the ascetics reached its far shore.
units.editionTranslation: Fear not, O learned one, there is no death for thee; there is a means of crossing this sea of relative existence; that very way by which sages have gone beyond it, I shall inculcate to thee.

units.label: Verse 44
units.deva:
अस्त्य् उपायो महान् कश्चित्संसारभयनाशनः ।
तेन तीर्त्वा भवाम्भोधिं परमानन्दमाप्स्यसि ॥
units.iast:
asty upāyo mahān kaścit saṃsārabhayanāśanaḥ |
tena tīrtvā bhavāmbhodhiṃ paramānandam āpsyasi ||
units.translation: There is a great means that destroys the fear of saṃsāra. By crossing the ocean of existence through it, you will attain supreme bliss.
units.editionTranslation: There is a sovereign means which puts an end to the fear of relative existence; through that thou wilt cross the sea of Samsara and attain the supreme bliss.

units.label: Verse 45
units.deva:
वेदान्तार्थविचारेण जायते ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।
तेनात्यन्तिकसंसारदुःखनाशो भवत्यनु ॥
units.iast:
vedāntārthavicāreṇa jāyate jñānam uttamam |
tenātyantika-saṃsāra-duḥkhanāśo bhavaty anu ||
units.translation: Inquiry into the meaning of Vedānta gives rise to the highest knowledge; through that, the suffering of saṃsāra is completely destroyed as a result.

gloss.en: by inquiry into the meaning of Vedānta

units.editionTranslation: Reasoning on the meaning of the Vedanta leads to efficient knowledge, which is immediately followed by the total annihilation of the misery born of relative existence.

units.label: Verse 46
units.deva:
श्रद्धाभक्तिध्यानयोगाम्मुमुक्षोः
मुक्तेर्हेतून्वक्ति साक्षाच्छ्रुतेर्गीः ।
यो वा एतेष्व् एव तिष्ठत्यमुष्य
मोक्षोऽविद्याकल्पिताद्देहबन्धात् ॥
units.iast:
śraddhābhaktidhyānayogāṃ mumukṣoḥ
mukter hetūn vakti sākṣāc chruter gīḥ |
yo vā eteṣv eva tiṣṭhaty amuṣya
mokṣo 'vidyākalpitād dehabandhāt ||
units.translation: For a seeker of liberation, Śruti directly declares faith, devotion, and meditative practice to be the means of liberation. Whoever remains firm in these is freed from the bodily bondage imagined by ignorance.

gloss.en: from what is imagined by ignorance

units.editionTranslation: Faith (Shraddha), devotion and the Yoga of meditation – these are mentioned by the Shruti as the immediate factors of Liberation in the case of a seeker; whoever abides in these gets Liberation from the bondage of the body, which is the conjuring of Ignorance.

units.label: Verse 47
units.deva:
अज्ञानयोगात्परमात्मनस्तव
ह्यनात्मबन्धस्तत एव संसृतिः ।
तयोर् विवेकोदितबोधवह्निः
अज्ञानकार्यं प्रदहेत्समूलम् ॥
units.iast:
ajñānayogāt paramātmanas tava
hyanātmabandhas tata eva saṃsṛtiḥ |
tayoḥ vivekoditabodhavahniḥ
ajñānakāryaṃ pradahet samūlam ||
units.translation: By association with ignorance, you—the Supreme Self—are bound to the not-Self; from that alone comes the cycle of rebirth. The fire of knowledge arising from discernment between the two should burn up the effects of ignorance, root and all.

gloss.en: the fire of knowledge arisen from discernment

units.editionTranslation: It is verily through the touch of Ignorance that thou who art the Supreme Self findest thyself under the bondage of the non-Self, whence alone proceeds the round of births and deaths. The fire of knowledge, kindled by the discrimination between these two, burns up the effects of Ignorance together with their root.

units.label: Verse 48
units.deva:
शिष्य उवाच
कृपया श्रूयतां स्वामिन् प्रश्नोऽयं क्रियते मया ।
यदुत्तरमहं श्रुत्वा कृतार्थः स्यां भवन्मुखात् ॥
units.iast:
śiṣya uvāca
kṛpayā śrūyatāṃ svāmin praśno 'yaṃ kriyate mayā |
yad uttaram ahaṃ śrutvā kṛtārthaḥ syāṃ bhavanmukhāt ||
units.translation: The disciple said: O Master, kindly hear the question I am asking. Having heard the answer from your own lips, may I have my purpose fulfilled.

gloss.en: let it be heard; please hear

units.editionTranslation: Condescend to listen, O Master, to the question I am putting (to thee). I shall be gratified to hear a reply to the same from thy lips.

units.label: Verse 49
units.deva:
को नाम बन्धः कथम् एष आगतः
कथं प्रतिष्ठास्य कथं विमोक्षः ।
कोऽसावनात्मा परमः क आत्मा
तयोर् विवेकः कथम् एतदुच्यताम् ॥
units.iast:
ko nāma bandhaḥ katham eṣa āgataḥ
kathaṃ pratiṣṭhāsya kathaṃ vimokṣaḥ |
ko 'sāv anātmā paramaḥ ka ātmā
tayoḥ vivekaḥ katham etad ucyatām ||
units.translation: What exactly is bondage? How did it arise? How does it persist, and how is release from it possible? What is the not-Self, and what is the Supreme Self? How are the two distinguished? Please explain all this.
units.editionTranslation: What is bondage, forsooth ? How has it come (upon the Self) ? How does it continue to exist ? How is one freed from it ? What is this non-Self ? And who is the Supreme Self ? And how can one discriminate between them ? -- Do tell me about all these.

units.label: Verse 50
units.deva:
श्रीगुरुवाच
धन्योऽसि कृतकृत्योऽसि पावितं ते कुलं त्वया ।
यदविद्याबन्धमुक्त्या ब्रह्मीभवितुमिच्छसि ॥
units.iast:
śrīguruvāca
dhanyo 'si kṛtakṛtyo 'si pāvitaṃ te kulaṃ tvayā |
yad avidyābandhamuktyā brahmībhavitum icchasi ||
units.translation: The revered teacher said: You are blessed; you have fulfilled your purpose, and your family line has been purified through you, since you seek to become Brahman by release from ignorance’s bondage.

gloss.en: one who has fulfilled the purpose

units.editionTranslation: The Guru replied: Blessed art thou ! Thou hast achieved thy life’s end and hast sanctified thy family, that thou wishest to attain Brahmanhood by getting free from the bondage of Ignorance !

units.label: Verse 51
units.deva:
ऋणमोचनकर्तारः पितुः सन्ति सुतादयः ।
बन्धमोचनकर्ता तु स्वस्मादन्यो न कश्चन ॥
units.iast:
ṛṇamocanakartāraḥ pituḥ santi sutādayaḥ |
bandhamocanakartā tu svasmād anyo na kaścana ||
units.translation: Sons and others can clear a father’s debts, but no one other than oneself can remove one’s bondage.
units.editionTranslation: A father has got his sons and others to free him from his debts, but he has got none but himself to remove his bondage.

units.label: Verse 52
units.deva:
मस्तकन्यस्तभारादेर्दुःखमन्यैर् निवार्यते ।
क्षुधादिकृतदुःखं तु विना स्वेन न केनचित् ॥
units.iast:
mastakanyastabhārāder duḥkham anyair nivāryate |
kṣudhādikṛtaduḥkhaṃ tu vinā svena na kenacit ||
units.translation: Others can remove the pain of a load placed on the head, but no one can remove the pain caused by hunger and the like without the person himself.

gloss.en: from a load placed on the head and the like
pain caused by hunger and the like

units.editionTranslation: Trouble such as that caused by a load on the head can be removed by others, but none but one’s own self can put a stop to the pain which is caused by hunger and the like.

units.label: Verse 53
units.deva:
पथ्यमौषधसेवा च क्रियते येन रोगिणा ।
आरोग्यसिद्धिर्दृष्टास्य नान्यानुष्ठितकर्मणा ॥
units.iast:
pathyamauṣadhasevā ca kriyate yena rogiṇā |
ārogyasiddhir dṛṣṭāsya nānyānuṣṭhitakarmaṇā ||
units.translation: A patient who follows a proper diet and takes medicine is seen to recover; recovery does not come through actions performed by someone else.

gloss.en: by an action performed by another

units.editionTranslation: The patient who takes (the proper) diet and medicine is alone seen to recover completely – not through work done by others.

units.label: Verse 54
units.deva:
वस्तुस्वरूपं स्फुटबोधचक्षुषा
स्वेनैव वेद्यं न तु पण्डितेन ।
चन्द्रस्वरूपं निजचक्षुषैव
ज्ञातव्यमन्यैर् अवगम्यते किम् ॥
units.iast:
vastusvarūpaṃ sphuṭabodhacakṣuṣā
svenaiva vedyaṃ na tu paṇḍitena |
candrasvarūpaṃ nijacakṣuṣaiva
jñātavyam anyair avagamyate kim ||
units.translation: A thing’s true nature must be known by oneself, through the eye of clear understanding, not by a scholar. The moon’s nature must be known with one’s own eyes; can it be understood by someone else?
units.editionTranslation: The true nature of things is to be known personally, through the eye of clear illumination, and not through a sage: what the moon exactly is, is to be known with one’s own eyes; can others make him know it ?

units.label: Verse 55
units.deva:
अविद्याकामकर्मादिपाशबन्धं विमोचितुम् ।
कः शक्नुयाद्विनात्मानं कल्पकोटिशतैर् अपि ॥
units.iast:
avidyākāmakarmādipāśabandhaṃ vimocitum |
kaḥ śaknuyād vinātmānaṃ kalpakoṭiśatair api ||
units.translation: Who, other than oneself, could free a person from the bondage-noose of ignorance, desire, action, and the rest—even over hundreds of crores of cosmic cycles?

gloss.en: over hundreds of crores of cosmic cycles

units.editionTranslation: Who but one’s own self can get rid of the bondage caused by the fetters of Ignorance, desire, action and the like, aye even in a hundred crore of cycles ?

units.label: Verse 56
units.deva:
न योगेन न सांख्येन कर्मणा नो न विद्यया ।
ब्रह्मात्मैकत्वबोधेन मोक्षः सिध्यति नान्यथा ॥
units.iast:
na yogena na sāṃkhyena karmaṇā no na vidyayā |
brahmātmaikatvabodhena mokṣaḥ sidhyati nānyathā ||
units.translation: Liberation is not achieved by Yoga, Sāṃkhya, action, or learning; it is achieved through knowledge of the oneness of Brahman and the Self, and not otherwise.

gloss.en: through knowledge of the oneness of Brahman and the Self

units.editionTranslation: Neither by Yoga, nor by Sankhya, nor by work, nor by learning, but by the realisation of one's identity with Brahman is Liberation possible, and by no other means.

units.label: Verse 57
units.deva:
वीणाया रूपसौन्दर्यं तन्त्रीवादनसौष्ठवम् ।
प्रजारञ्जनमात्रं तन् न साम्राज्याय कल्पते ॥
units.iast:
vīṇāyā rūpasaundaryaṃ tantrīvādanasauṣṭhavam |
prajārañjanamātraṃ tan na sāmrājyāya kalpate ||
units.translation: The beauty of a vīṇā’s shape and the skill of playing its strings merely delight people; they do not qualify one for sovereignty.
units.editionTranslation: The beauty of a guitar’s form and the skill of playing on its chords serve merely to please a few persons; they do not suffice to confer sovereignty.

units.label: Verse 58
units.deva:
वाग्वैखरी शब्दझरी शास्त्रव्याख्यानकौशलम् ।
वैदुष्यं विदुषां तद्वद्भुक्तये न तु मुक्तये ॥
units.iast:
vāgvaikharī śabdajharī śāstravyākhyānakauśalam |
vaiduṣyaṃ viduṣāṃ tadvad bhuktaye na tu muktaye ||
units.translation: Eloquent speech, a stream of words, skill in explaining scripture, and scholarship serve the learned for enjoyment, not liberation.
units.editionTranslation: Loud speech consisting of a shower of words, the skill in expounding the Scriptures, and likewise erudition - these merely bring on a little personal enjoyment to the scholar, but are no good for Liberation.

units.label: Verse 59
units.deva:
अविज्ञाते परे तत्त्वे शास्त्राधीतिस्तु निष्फला ।
विज्ञातेऽपि परे तत्त्वे शास्त्राधीतिस्तु निष्फला ॥
units.iast:
avijñāte pare tattve śāstrādhītis tu niṣphalā |
vijñāte 'pi pare tattve śāstrādhītis tu niṣphalā ||
units.translation: Study of scripture is fruitless when the highest truth is unknown; even when the highest truth is known, study of scripture is fruitless.
units.editionTranslation: The study of the Scriptures is useless so long as the highest Truth is unknown, and it is equally useless when the highest Truth has already been known.

units.label: Verse 60
units.deva:
शब्दजालं महारण्यं चित्तभ्रमणकारणम् ।
अतः प्रयत्नाज्ज्ञातव्यं तत्त्वज्ञैस्तत्त्वम् आत्मनः ॥
units.iast:
śabdajālaṃ mahāraṇyaṃ cittabhramaṇakāraṇam |
ataḥ prayatnāj jñātavyaṃ tattvajñais tattvam ātmanaḥ ||
units.translation: The web of words is a vast forest that causes the mind to wander. Therefore, the discerning should make an effort to know the truth of the Self.
units.editionTranslation: The Scriptures consisting of many words are a dense forest which merely causes the mind to ramble. Hence men of wisdom should earnestly set about knowing the true nature of the Self.

units.label: Verse 61
units.deva:
अज्ञानसर्पदष्टस्य ब्रह्मज्ञानौषधं विना ।
किमु वेदैश्च शास्त्रैश्च किमु मन्त्रैः किमौषधैः ॥
units.iast:
ajñānasarpadaṣṭasya brahmajñānauṣadhaṃ vinā |
kimu vedaiś ca śāstraiś ca kimu mantraiḥ kim auṣadhaiḥ ||
units.translation: For one bitten by the snake of ignorance, what use are the Vedas, scriptures, mantras, or medicines without the remedy of Brahman-knowledge?

gloss.en: for one bitten by the snake of ignorance

units.editionTranslation: For one who has been bitten by the serpent of Ignorance, the only remedy is the knowledge of Brahman. Of what avail are the Vedas and (other) Scriptures, Mantras (sacred formulae) and medicines to such a one ?

units.label: Verse 62
units.deva:
न गच्छति विना पानं व्याधिरौषधशब्दतः ।
विनापरोक्षानुभवं ब्रह्मशब्दैर् न मुच्यते ॥
units.iast:
na gacchati vinā pānaṃ vyādhir auṣadhaśabdāt |
vināparokṣānubhavaṃ brahmaśabdair na mucyate ||
units.translation: Illness does not go away through the word “medicine” without taking medicine; without direct experience, one is not freed by words about Brahman.
units.editionTranslation: A disease does not leave off if one simply utter the name of the medicine, without taking it; (similarly) without direct realisation one cannot be liberated by the mere utterance of the word Brahman.

units.label: Verse 63
units.deva:
अकृत्वा दृश्यविलयमज्ञात्वा तत्त्वम् आत्मनः ।
ब्रह्मशब्दैः कुतो मुक्तिरुक्तिमात्रफलैर् नृणाम् ॥
units.iast:
akṛtvā dṛśyavilayam ajñātvā tattvam ātmanaḥ |
brahmaśabdaiḥ kuto muktir uktimātraphalair nṛṇām ||
units.translation: Without dissolving what is seen and knowing the truth of the Self, how could people be liberated through words about Brahman whose only fruit is utterance?
units.editionTranslation: Without causing the objective universe to vanish and without knowing the truth of the Self, how is one to achieve Liberation by the mere utterance of the word Brahman ? -- It would result merely in an effort of speech.

units.label: Verse 64
units.deva:
अकृत्वा शत्रुसंहारमगत्वाखिलभूश्रियम् ।
राजाहमिति शब्दान्नो राजा भवितुमर्हति ॥
units.iast:
akṛtvā śatrusaṃhāram agatvā akhilabhūśriyam |
rājāham iti śabdānno rājā bhavitum arhati ||
units.translation: Without destroying enemies and attaining the wealth of the entire earth, a person cannot become king simply by saying, “I am king.”

gloss.en: the wealth of the entire earth

units.editionTranslation: Without killing one’s enemies, and possessing oneself of the splendour of the entire surrounding region, one cannot claim to be an emperor by merely saying, ‘I am an emperor’.

units.label: Verse 65
units.deva:
आप्तोक्तिं खननं तथोपरिशिलाद्युत्कर्षणं स्वीकृतिं
निक्षेपः समपेक्षते नहि बहिः शब्दैस्तु निर्गच्छति ।
तद्वद्ब्रह्मविदोपदेशमननध्यानादिभिर्लभ्यते
मायाकार्यतिरोहितं स्वममलं तत्त्वं न दुर्युक्तिभिः ॥
units.iast:
āptoktiṃ khananaṃ tathopariśilādyutkarṣaṇaṃ svīkṛtiṃ
nikṣepaḥ samapekṣate na hi bahiḥ śabdais tu nirgacchati |
tadvad brahmavidopadeśa-mananadhyānādibhir labhyate
māyākāryatirohitaṃ svam amalaṃ tattvaṃ na duryuktibhiḥ ||
units.translation: A hidden deposit requires a trustworthy person’s directions, digging, removing the stones and such above it, and taking it up; it does not emerge through words spoken from outside. In the same way, one attains one’s own pure reality, hidden by Maya’s effects, through a knower of Brahman’s teaching, reflection, meditation, and the like—not through faulty reasoning.

gloss.en: removing the stones and such above
the teaching of a knower of Brahman

units.editionTranslation: As a treasure hidden underground requires (for its extraction) competent instruction, excavation, the removal of stones and other such things lying above it and (finally) grasping, but never comes out by being (merely) called out by name, so the transparent Truth of the self, which is hidden by Maya and its effects, is to be attained through the instructions of a knower of Brahman, followed by reflection, meditation and so forth, but not through perverted arguments.

units.label: Verse 66
units.deva:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन भवबन्धविमुक्तये ।
स्वैर् एव यत्नः कर्तव्यो रोगादाव् इव पण्डितैः ॥
units.iast:
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena bhavabandhavimuktaye |
svair eva yatnaḥ kartavyo rogādāv iva paṇḍitaiḥ ||
units.translation: Therefore the wise must make every effort themselves to be free from the bondage of existence, just as they would in the case of illness and the like.

gloss.en: for release from the bondage of existence

units.editionTranslation: Therefore the wise should, as in the case of disease and the like, personally strive by all the means in their power to be free from the bondage of repeated births and deaths.

units.label: Verse 67
units.deva:
यस्त्वयाद्य कृतः प्रश्नो वरीयाञ्छास्त्रविन्मतः ।
सूत्रप्रायो निगूढार्थो ज्ञातव्यश्च मुमुक्षुभिः ॥
units.iast:
yas tvayādya kṛtaḥ praśno varīyāñchāstravinmataḥ |
sūtraprāyo nigūḍhārtho jñātavyaś ca mumukṣubhiḥ ||
units.translation: The question you asked today is excellent and approved by those who know the scriptures; it is concise like a sūtra, rich in hidden meaning, and worth knowing for seekers of liberation.

gloss.en: approved by those who know scripture

units.editionTranslation: The question that thou hast asked today is excellent, approved by those versed in the Scriptures, aphoristic, pregnant with meaning and fit to be known by the seekers after Liberation.

units.label: Verse 68
units.deva:
शृणुष्वावहितो विद्वन्यन्मया समुदीर्यते ।
तदेतच्छ्रवणात्सद्यो भवबन्धाद्विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
units.iast:
śṛṇuṣvāvahito vidvan yan mayā samudīryate |
tad etac chravaṇāt sadyo bhavabandhād vimokṣyase ||
units.translation: Listen attentively, learned one, to what I am saying. By hearing this, you will be freed at once from the bondage of existence.
units.editionTranslation: Listen attentively, O learned one, to what I am going to say. By listening to it thou shalt be instantly free from the bondage of Samsara.

units.label: Verse 69
units.deva:
मोक्षस्य हेतुः प्रथमो निगद्यते
वैराग्यमत्यन्तमनित्यवस्तुषु ।
ततः शमश्चापि दमस्तितिक्षा
न्यासः प्रसक्ताखिलकर्मणां भृशम् ॥
units.iast:
mokṣasya hetuḥ prathamo nigadyate
vairāgyam atyantam anityavastuṣu |
tataḥ śamaś cāpi damaḥ titikṣā
nyāsaḥ prasaktākhilakarmaṇāṃ bhṛśam ||
units.translation: The first cause of liberation is declared to be complete dispassion toward impermanent things. After that come calmness, restraint, forbearance, and thorough renunciation of all actions undertaken.
units.editionTranslation: The first step to Liberation is the extreme aversion to all perishable things, then follow calmness, self-control, forbearance, and the utter relinquishment of all work enjoined in the Scriptures.

units.label: Verse 70
units.deva:
ततः श्रुतिस् तन्मननं सतत्त्व-
ध्यानं चिरं नित्यनिरन्तरं मुनेः ।
ततोऽविकल्पं परमेत्य विद्वान्
इहैव निर्वाणसुखं समृच्छति ॥
units.iast:
tataḥ śrutis tan mananaṃ satattva-
dhyānaṃ ciraṃ nityanirantaraṃ muneḥ |
tato 'vikalpaṃ param etya vidvān
ihaiva nirvāṇasukhaṃ samṛcchati ||
units.translation: Then come hearing, reflection on that teaching, and the sage’s long, uninterrupted meditation on reality. Having reached the supreme state free of distinctions, the wise one attains the bliss of nirvāṇa here itself.
units.editionTranslation: Then come hearing, reflection on that, and long, constant and unbroken meditation on the Truth for the Muni. After that the learned seeker attains the supreme Nirvikalpa state and realises the bliss of Nirvana even in this life.

units.label: Verse 71
units.deva:
यद्बोद्धव्यं तवेदानीमात्मानात्मविवेचनम् ।
तदुच्यते मया सम्यक् श्रुत्वात्मन्यवधारय ॥
units.iast:
yadboddhavyaṃ tavedānīm ātmānātmavivecanam |
taducyate mayā samyak śrutvātmanyavadhāraya ||
units.translation: What you must now understand is discrimination between the Self and the non-Self. I shall explain it fully; listen and grasp it firmly within yourself.

gloss.en: discrimination between the Self and the non-Self

units.editionTranslation: Now I am going to tell thee fully about what thou oughtst to know – the discrimination between the Self and the non-Self. Listen to it and decide about it in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 72
units.deva:
मज्जास्थिमेदःपलरक्तचर्म-
त्वगाह्वयैर्धातुभिरेभिरन्वितम् ।
पादोरुवक्षोभुजपृष्ठमस्तकैः
अङ्गैरुपाङ्गैरुपयुक्तमेतत् ॥
units.iast:
majjāsthimedaḥpalaraktacarma-
tvagāhvayair dhātubhirebhiranvitam |
pādoruvakṣobhujapṛṣṭhamastakaiḥ
aṅgairupāṅgairupayuktametat ||
units.translation: This body is made up of seven constituents—marrow, bone, fat, flesh, blood, skin, and cuticle—and comprises these limbs and their parts: feet, thighs, chest, arms, back, and head.

gloss.en: by what is called the cuticle
by feet, thighs, chest, arms, back, and head

units.editionTranslation: Composed of the seven ingredients, viz. marrow, bones, fat, flesh, blood, skin and cuticle, and consisting of the following limbs and their parts – legs, thighs, the chest, arms, the back and the head:

units.label: Verse 73
units.deva:
अहंममेति प्रथितं शरीरं
मोहास्पदं स्थूलमितीर्यते बुधैः ।
नभोनभस्वद्दहनाम्बुभूमयः
सूक्ष्माणि भूतानि भवन्ति तानि ॥
units.iast:
ahaṃmametiprathitaṃ śarīraṃ
mohāspadaṃ sthūlamitīryate budhaiḥ |
nabhonabhasvaddahanāmbubhūmayaḥ
sūkṣmāṇi bhūtāni bhavanti tāni ||
units.translation: This body, known through the ideas “I” and “mine” and serving as a basis for delusion, is called the gross body by the wise. Space, air, fire, water, and earth are those subtle elements.
units.editionTranslation: This body, reputed to be the abode of the delusion of ‘I and mine’, is designated by sages as the gross body. The sky, air, fire, water and earth are subtle elements. They –

units.label: Verse 74
units.deva:
परस्परांशैर्मिलितानि भूत्वा
स्थूलानि च स्थूलशरीरहेतवः ।
मात्रास्तदीया विषया भवन्ति
शब्दादयः पञ्च सुखाय भोक्तुः ॥
units.iast:
parasparāṃśair militāni bhūtvā
sthūlāni ca sthūlaśarīrahetavaḥ |
mātrāstadīyā viṣayā bhavanti
śabdādayaḥ pañca sukhāya bhoktuḥ ||
units.translation: Joined with portions of one another, the elements become gross and cause the gross body to form. Their subtle essences become the five sense-objects—sound and the rest—for the experiencer’s pleasure.
units.editionTranslation: Being united with parts of one another and becoming gross, (they) form the gross body. And their subtle essences form sense-objects – the group of five such as sound, which conduce to the happiness of the experiencer, the individual soul.

units.label: Verse 75
units.deva:
य एषु मूढा विषयेषु बद्धा
रागोरुपाशेन सुदुर्दमेन ।
आयान्ति निर्यान्त्यध ऊर्ध्वमुच्चैः
स्वकर्मदूतेन जवेन नीताः ॥
units.iast:
ya eṣu mūḍhā viṣayeṣu baddhā
rāgorupāśena sudurdamena |
āyānti niryāntyadha ūrdhvamuccaiḥ
svakarmadūtena javena nītāḥ ||
units.translation: Those fools bound to these sense-objects by attachment’s great noose, very hard to break, come and go—down below and high above—swiftly driven by the messenger of their own actions.

gloss.en: by the great noose of attachment
by the messenger of their own actions

units.editionTranslation: Those fools who are tied to these sense-objects by the stout cord of attachment, so very difficult to snap, come and depart, up and down, carried amain by the powerful emissary of their past action.

units.label: Verse 76
units.deva:
शब्दादिभिः पञ्चभिर् एव पञ्च
पञ्चत्वमापुः स्वगुणेन बद्धाः ।
कुरङ्गमातङ्गपतङ्गमीन-
भृङ्गा नरः पञ्चभिरञ्चितः किम् ॥
units.iast:
śabdādibhiḥ pañcabhir eva pañca
pañcatvamāpuḥ svaguṇena baddhāḥ |
kuraṅgamātaṅgapataṅgamīna-
bhṛṅgā naraḥ pañcabhirañcitaḥ kim ||
units.translation: The deer, elephant, moth, fish, and bee—these five—have met their end, each bound by its own tendency to one of the five sense-objects, beginning with sound. What, then, of a person beset by all five?
units.editionTranslation: The deer, the elephant, the moth, the fish and the black-bee – these five have died, being tied to one or other of the five senses, viz. sound etc., through their own attachment. What then is in store for man who is attached to all these five.

units.label: Verse 77
units.deva:
दोषेण तीव्रो विषयः कृष्णसर्पविषाद् अपि ।
विषं निहन्ति भोक्तारं द्रष्टारं चक्षुषाप्ययम् ॥
units.iast:
doṣeṇa tīvro viṣayaḥ kṛṣṇasarpaviṣād api |
viṣaṃ nihanti bhoktāraṃ draṣṭāraṃ cakṣuṣāpyayam ||
units.translation: A sense-object is more deadly in its harmful effect than even the venom of a black snake. Poison kills the one who consumes it, but this kills even the one who sees it with the eye.
units.editionTranslation: Sense-objects are even more virulent in their evil effects than the poison of the cobra. Poison kills one who takes it, but those others kill one who even looks at them through the eyes.

units.label: Verse 78
units.deva:
विषयाशामहापाशाद्यो विमुक्तः सुदुस्त्यजात् ।
स एव कल्पते मुक्त्यै नान्यः षट्शास्त्रवेद्य् अपि ॥
units.iast:
viṣayāśāmahāpāśādyo vimuktaḥ sudustyajāt |
sa eva kalpate muktyai nānyaḥ ṣaṭśāstravedy api ||
units.translation: He alone is fit for liberation who is free from the great noose of desire for sense-objects, so hard to give up; no one else, even if learned in the six śāstras.

gloss.en: from the great noose of desire for sense-objects
from what is very hard to give up

units.editionTranslation: He who is free from the terrible snare of the hankering after sense-objects, so very difficult to get rid of, is alone fit for Liberation, and none else – even though he be versed in all the six Shastras.

units.label: Verse 79
units.deva:
आपातवैराग्यवतो मुमुक्षून्
भवाब्धिपारं प्रतियातुमुद्यतान् ।
आशाग्रहो मज्जयतेऽन्तराले
निगृह्य कण्ठे विनिवर्त्य वेगात् ॥
units.iast:
āpātavairāgyavato mumukṣūn
bhavābdhipāraṃ pratiyātumudyatān |
āśāgraho majjayate 'ntarāle
nigṛhya kaṇṭhe vinivartya vegāt ||
units.translation: The shark of desire seizes by the throat those seekers for liberation whose dispassion is only superficial and who are striving to reach the far shore of the ocean of worldly existence; it forcefully turns them back and drowns them midway.

gloss.en: the far shore of the ocean of becoming

units.editionTranslation: The shark of hankering catches by the throat those seekers after Liberation who have got only an apparent dispassion (Vairagya) and are trying to cross the ocean of samsara (relative existence), and violently snatching them away, drowns them half-way.

units.label: Verse 80
units.deva:
विषयाख्यग्रहो येन सुविरक्त्यसिना हतः ।
स गच्छति भवाम्भोधेः पारं प्रत्यूहवर्जितः ॥
units.iast:
viṣayākhyagraho yena suviraktyasinā hataḥ |
sa gacchati bhavāmbhodheḥ pāraṃ pratyūhavarjitaḥ ||
units.translation: He who has slain the shark called “sense-objects” with the sword of strong dispassion reaches the far shore of the ocean of becoming, free from obstacles.

gloss.en: with the sword of strong dispassion

units.editionTranslation: He who has killed the shark known as sense-object with the sword of mature dispassion, crosses the ocean of Samsara, free from all obstacles.

units.label: Verse 81
units.deva:
विषमविषयमार्गैर् गच्छतोऽनच्छबुद्धेः
प्रतिपदमभियातो मृत्युरप्येष विद्धि ।
हितसुजनगुरुक्त्या गच्छतः स्वस्य युक्त्या
प्रभवति फलसिद्धिः सत्यम् इत्य् एव विद्धि ॥
units.iast:
viṣamaviṣayamārgair gacchato 'nacchabuddheḥ
pratipadamabhiyāto mṛtyurapyeṣa viddhi |
hitasujanaguruktyā gacchataḥ svasya yuktyā
prabhavati phalasiddhiḥ satyam ity eva viddhi ||
units.translation: Know this to be true: death pursues at every step the dull-minded person who walks the dangerous paths of sense-objects. The one who walks by the counsel of well-wishing teachers and by their own reasoning succeeds in attaining the goal.

gloss.en: by the counsel of well-wishing teachers

units.editionTranslation: Know that death quickly overtakes the stupid man who walks along the dreadful ways of sense-pleasure; whereas one who walks in accordance with the instructions of a well-wishing and worthy Guru, as also with his own reasoning, achieves his end – know this to be true.

units.label: Verse 82
units.deva:
मोक्षस्य कांक्षा यदि वै तवास्ति
त्यजातिदूराद्विषयान्विषं यथा ।
पीयूषवत्तोषदयाक्षमार्जव-
प्रशान्तिदान्तीर्भज नित्यमादरात् ॥
units.iast:
mokṣasya kāṃkṣā yadi vai tavāsti
tyajātidūrādviṣayānviṣaṃ yathā |
pīyūṣavattoṣadayākṣamārjava-
praśāntidāntīrbhaja nityamādarāt ||
units.translation: If you truly long for liberation, leave sense-objects far away, as you would poison. Always carefully cultivate, as if they were nectar, contentment, compassion, forgiveness, straightforwardness, calmness, and self-restraint.
units.editionTranslation: If indeed thou hast a craving for Liberation, shun sense-objects from a good distance as thou wouldst do poison, and always cultivate carefully the nectar-like virtues of contentment, compassion, forgiveness, straight-forwardness, calmness and self-control.

units.label: Verse 83
units.deva:
अनुक्षणं यत्परिहृत्य कृत्यं
अनाद्यविद्याकृतबन्धमोक्षणम् ।
देहः परार्थोऽयममुष्य पोषणे
यः सज्जते स स्वमनेन हन्ति ॥
units.iast:
anukṣaṇaṃ yatparihṛtya kṛtyaṃ
anādyavidyākṛtabandhamokṣaṇam |
dehaḥ parārtho 'yam amuṣya poṣaṇe
yaḥ sajjate sa svam anena hanti ||
units.translation: Whoever sets aside the task to be done at every moment—the release from bondage caused by beginningless ignorance—and becomes attached to nourishing this body, which is for another’s use, kills himself by it.

gloss.en: release from bondage caused by beginningless ignorance

units.editionTranslation: Whoever leaves aside what should always be attempted, viz. emancipation from the bondage of Ignorance without beginning, and passionately seeks to nourish this body, which is an object for others to enjoy, commits suicide thereby.

units.label: Verse 84
units.deva:
शरीरपोषणार्थी सन् य आत्मानं दिदृक्षति ।
ग्राहं दारुधिया धृत्वा नदि तर्तुं स गच्छति ॥
units.iast:
śarīrapoṣaṇārthī san ya ātmānaṃ didṛkṣati |
grāhaṃ dārudhiyā dhṛtvā nadi tartuṃ sa gacchati ||
units.translation: One intent on nourishing the body who wants to see the Self is like someone who grasps a crocodile, mistaking it for a log, and sets out to cross a river.
units.editionTranslation: Whoever seeks to realise the Self by devoting himself to the nourishment of the body, proceeds to cross a river by catching hold of a crocodile, mistaking it for a log.

units.label: Verse 85
units.deva:
मोह एव महामृत्युर्मुमुक्षोर्वपुरादिषु ।
मोहो विनिर्जितो येन स मुक्तिपदमर्हति ॥
units.iast:
moha eva mahāmṛtyurmumukṣorvapurādiṣu |
moho vinirjito yena sa muktipadamarhati ||
units.translation: For a seeker of liberation, delusion about the body and such things is indeed a great death. Whoever has thoroughly conquered delusion is worthy of the state of liberation.

gloss.en: about the body and such things

units.editionTranslation: So for a seeker after Liberation the infatuation over things like the body is a dire death. He who has thoroughly conquered this deserves the state of Freedom.

units.label: Verse 86
units.deva:
मोहं जहि महामृत्युं देहदारसुतादिषु ।
यं जित्वा मुनयो यान्ति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
units.iast:
mohaṃ jahi mahāmṛtyuṃ dehadārasutādiṣu |
yaṃ jitvā munayo yānti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ||
units.translation: Conquer delusion about the body, spouse, children, and the like—the great death. Having conquered it, sages reach that supreme state of Viṣṇu.

gloss.en: about the body, spouse, children, and the like

units.editionTranslation: Conquer the dire death of infatuation over thy body, wife, children etc., -- conquering which the sages reach that Supreme State of Vishnu.

units.label: Verse 87
units.deva:
त्वङ्मांसरुधिरस्नायुमेदोमज्जास्थिसंकुलम् ।
पूर्णं मूत्रपुरीषाभ्यां स्थूलं निन्द्यमिदं वपुः ॥
units.iast:
tvaṅmāṃsarudhirasnāyumedomajjāsthisaṃkulam |
pūrṇaṃ mūtrapurīṣābhyāṃ sthūlaṃ nindyamidaṃ vapuḥ ||
units.translation: This gross body, packed with skin, flesh, blood, sinews, fat, marrow, and bone, is full of urine and feces and is contemptible.
units.editionTranslation: This gross body is to be deprecated, for it consists of the skin, flesh, blood, arteries and veins, fat, marrow and bones, and is full of other offensive things.

units.label: Verse 88
units.deva:
पञ्चीकृतेभ्यो भूतेभ्यः स्थूलेभ्यः पूर्वकर्मणा ।
समुत्पन्नमिदं स्थूलं भोगायतनम् आत्मनः

अवस्था जागरस्तस्य स्थूलार्थानुभवो यतः ॥
units.iast:
pañcīkṛtebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ sthūlebhyaḥ pūrvakarmaṇā |
samutpannamidaṃ sthūlaṃ bhogāyatanam ātmanaḥ

avasthā jāgarastasya sthūlārthānubhavo yataḥ ||
units.translation: By past action, this gross body arises from the gross elements formed by fivefold combination; it is the field of experience for the self. Its state is waking, because gross objects are experienced in it.

gloss.en: from elements formed by fivefold combination

units.editionTranslation: The gross body is produced by one’s past actions out of the gross elements formed by the union of the subtle elements with each other, and is the medium of experience for the soul. That is its waking state in which it perceives gross objects.

units.label: Verse 89
units.deva:
बाह्येन्द्रियैः स्थूलपदार्थसेवां
स्रक्चन्दनस्त्र्यादिविचित्ररूपाम् ।
करोति जीवः स्वयमेतद् आत्मना
तस्मात्प्रशस्तिर्वपुषोऽस्य जागरे ॥
units.iast:
bāhyendriyaiḥ sthūlapadārthasevāṃ
srakcandanastryādivicitrarūpām |
karoti jīvaḥ svayam etad ātmanā
tasmātpraśastirvapuṣo 'sya jāgare ||
units.translation: Through the external senses, the living being itself engages with gross objects in varied forms—garlands, sandal paste, women, and the like—taking this body as its self. Therefore this body is esteemed in the waking state.

gloss.en: taking this body as the self

units.editionTranslation: Identifying itself with this form, the individual soul, though separate, enjoys gross objects, such as garlands and sandal-paste, by means of the external organs. Hence this body has its fullest play in the waking state.

units.label: Verse 90
units.deva:
सर्वापि बाह्यसंसारः पुरुषस्य यदाश्रयः ।
विद्धि देहमिदं स्थूलं गृहवद्गृहमेधिनः ॥
units.iast:
sarvāpi bāhyasaṃsāraḥ puruṣasya yadāśrayaḥ |
viddhi dehamidaṃ sthūlaṃ gṛhavadgṛhamedhinaḥ ||
units.translation: Know this gross body, on which all of a person's external dealings depend, to be like a house for its householder.
units.editionTranslation: Know this gross body to be like a house to the householder, on which rests man’s entire dealing with the external world.

units.label: Verse 91
units.deva:
स्थूलस्य संभवजरामरणानि धर्माः
स्थौल्यादयो बहुविधाः शिशुताद्यवस्थाः ।
वर्णाश्रमादिनियमा बहुधामयाः स्युः
पूजावमानबहुमानमुखा विशेषाः ॥
units.iast:
sthūlasya saṃbhavajarāmaraṇāni dharmāḥ
sthaulyādayo bahuvidhāḥ śiśutādyavasthāḥ |
varṇāśramādiniyamā bahudhāmayāḥ syuḥ
pūjāvamānabahumānamukhā viśeṣāḥ ||
units.translation: Birth, aging, and death are properties of the gross body, along with many conditions such as corpulence and childhood. It is subject to rules about social class and life-stage, many diseases, and varied treatment—reverence, insult, and high honor.

gloss.en: rules about social class, life-stage, and the rest

units.editionTranslation: Birth, decay and death are the various characteristics of the gross body, as also stoutness etc., childhood etc., are its different conditions; it has got various restrictions regarding castes and orders of life; it is subject to various diseases, and meets with different kinds of treatment, such as worship, insult and high honours.

units.label: Verse 92
units.deva:
बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि श्रवणं त्वगक्षि
घ्राणं च जिव्हा विषयावबोधनात् ।
वाक्पाणिपादा गुदमप्युपस्थः
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि प्रवणेन कर्मसु ॥
units.iast:
buddhīndriyāṇi śravaṇaṃ tvagakṣi
ghrāṇaṃ ca jivhā viṣayāvabodhanāt |
vākpāṇipādā gudamapyupasthaḥ
karmendriyāṇi pravaṇena karmasu ||
units.translation: The five organs of knowledge are hearing, skin, eye, nose, and tongue, because they make objects known. Speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are organs of action, being directed toward action.
units.editionTranslation: The ears, skin, eyes, nose and tongue are organs of knowledge, for they help us to cognise objects; the vocal organs, hands, legs, etc., are organs of action, owing to their tendency to work.

units.label: Verses 93–94
units.deva:
निगद्यतेऽन्तःकरणं मनोधीः
अहंकृतिश्चित्तमिति स्ववृत्तिभिः ।
मनस्तु संकल्पविकल्पनादिभिः
बुद्धिः पदार्थाध्यवसायधर्मतः ॥

अत्राभिमानादहमित्यहंकृतिः ।
स्वार्थानुसन्धानगुणेन चित्तम् ॥
units.iast:
nigadyate 'ntaḥkaraṇaṃ manodhīḥ
ahaṃkṛtiścittamiti svavṛttibhiḥ |
manastu saṃkalpavikalpanādibhiḥ
buddhiḥ padārthādhyavasāyadharmataḥ ||

atrābhimānādahamityahaṃkṛtiḥ |
svārthānusandhānaguṇena cittam ||
units.translation: The inner organ is called mind, intellect, ego, and citta according to its functions: mind from thinking and weighing alternatives, intellect from determining the nature of things. Here, ego arises from the notion “I,” and citta from its function of pursuing one’s own concern.

gloss.en: by forming and weighing alternatives, and the like
because its nature is to determine the meaning of things
by the function of pursuing its own concern

units.editionTranslation: The inner organ (Antahkarana) is called Manas, Buddhi, ego or Chitta, according to their respective functions: Manas, from its considering the pros and cons of a thing; Buddhi, from its property of determining the truth of objects; the ego, from its identification with this body as one’s own self; and Chitta, from its function of remembering things it is interested in.

units.label: Verse 95
units.deva:
प्राणापानव्यानोदानसमाना भवत्यसौ प्राणः ।
स्वयम् एव वृत्तिभेदाद्विकृतिभेदात्सुवर्णसलिलादिवत् ॥
units.iast:
prāṇāpānavyānodānasamānā bhavatyasau prāṇaḥ |
svayam eva vṛttibhedādvikṛtibhedātsuvarṇasalilādivat ||
units.translation: The one vital force itself becomes prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna, and samāna because its functions and transformations differ, as with gold, water, and the like.

gloss.en: prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna, and samāna

units.editionTranslation: One and the same Prana (vital force) becomes Prana, Apana, Vyana, Udana and Samana according to their diversity of functions and modifications, like gold, water, etc.

units.label: Verse 96
units.deva:
वागादि पञ्च श्रवणादि पञ्च
प्राणादि पञ्चाभ्रमुखानि पञ्च ।
बुद्ध्याद्यविद्यापि च कामकर्मणी
पुर्यष्टकं सूक्ष्मशरीरमाहुः ॥
units.iast:
vāgādi pañca śravaṇādi pañca
prāṇādi pañcābhramukhāni pañca |
buddhyādyavidyāpi ca kāmakarmaṇī
puryaṣṭakaṃ sūkṣmaśarīramāhuḥ ||
units.translation: The five organs beginning with speech, the five beginning with hearing, the five vital breaths beginning with prāṇa, the five elements beginning with space, and buddhi and the rest together with ignorance, desire, and action—these eight groups, they say, make up the subtle body.
units.editionTranslation: The five organs of action such as speech, the five organs of knowledge such as the ear, the group of five Pranas, the five elements ending with the ether, together with Buddhi and the rest as also Nescience, desire and action – these eight "cities" make up what is called the subtle body.

units.label: Verse 97
units.deva:
इदं शरीरं शृणु सूक्ष्मसंज्ञितं
लिङ्गं त्वपञ्चीकृतसंभवम् ।
सवासनं कर्मफलानुभावकं
स्वाज्ञानतोऽनादिरुपाधिर् आत्मनः ॥
units.iast:
idaṃ śarīraṃ śṛṇu sūkṣmasaṃjñitaṃ
liṅgaṃ tvapañcīkṛtasaṃbhavam |
savāsanaṃ karmaphalānubhāvakaṃ
svājñānato'nādirupādhir ātmanaḥ ||
units.translation: Listen: this body, called the subtle or liṅga body, arises from elements before their fivefold combination, carries latent impressions, and experiences the fruits of action. Due to its own ignorance, it is a beginningless limiting adjunct of the Self.

gloss.en: arisen from elements not yet fivefold-combined

units.editionTranslation: Listen – this subtle body, called also the Linga body, is produced out of the elements before their subdividing and combining with each other, is possessed of latent impressions and causes the soul to experience the fruits of its past actions. It is a beginningless superimposition on the soul brought on by its own ignorance.

units.label: Verses 98–99
units.deva:
स्वप्नो भवत्यस्य विभक्त्यवस्था
स्वमात्रशेषेण विभाति यत्र ।
स्वप्ने तु बुद्धिः स्वयम् एव जाग्रत्
कालीननानाविधवासनाभिः ॥

कर्त्रादिभावं प्रतिपद्य राजते
यत्र स्वयं भाति ह्ययं परात्मा ।
धीमात्रकोपाधिरशेषसाक्षी
न लिप्यते तत्कृतकर्मलेशैः

यस्मादसङ्गस्तत एव कर्मभिः
न लिप्यते किंचिद् उपाधिना कृतैः ॥
units.iast:
svapno bhavatyasya vibhaktyavasthā
svamātraśeṣeṇa vibhāti yatra |
svapne tu buddhiḥ svayam eva jāgrat
kālīnanānāvidhavāsanābhiḥ ||

kartrādibhāvaṃ pratipadya rājate
yatra svayaṃ bhāti hyayaṃ parātmā |
dhīmātrakopādhiraśeṣasākṣī
na lipyate tatkṛtakarmaleśaiḥ

yasmādasaṅgastata eva karmabhiḥ
na lipyate kiṃcid upādhinā kṛtaiḥ ||
units.translation: 98. Dream is this [subtle body’s] distinct state, in which it shines with only its own inner residue remaining. In dream, the intellect itself appears awake through the many impressions formed during waking. 99. There it appears as an agent and in other roles; the supreme Self shines there as the witness of all, with intellect alone as its limiting adjunct. It is unstained by even a trace of action performed by that adjunct; being unattached, it is not touched at all by actions performed by any adjunct.

gloss.en: through many kinds of latent impressions
the state of an agent and the like
with intellect alone as limiting adjunct
by even traces of actions done by that

units.editionTranslation: Dream is a state of the soul distinct from the waking state, where it shines by itself. In dreams Buddhi, by itself, takes on the role of the agent and the like, owing to various latent impressions of the waking state, while the supreme Atman shines in Its own glory – with Buddhi as Its only superimposition, the witness of everything, and is not touched by the least work that Buddhi does. As It is wholly unattached, It is not touched by any work that Its superimpositions may perform.

units.label: Verse 100
units.deva:
सर्वव्यापृतिकरणं लिङ्गमिदं स्याच्चिद् आत्मनः पुंसः ।
वास्यादिकम् इव तक्ष्णस्तेनैवात्मा भवत्यसङ्गोऽयम् ॥
units.iast:
sarvavyāpṛtikaraṇaṃ liṅgamidaṃ syāccid ātmanaḥ puṃsaḥ |
vāsyādikam iva takṣṇastenaivātmā bhavatyasaṅgo'yam ||
units.translation: This liṅga body is the instrument of all activity for a person’s conscious Self, like an adze and other tools for a carpenter. Therefore this Self is unattached.
units.editionTranslation: This subtle body is the instrument for all activities of the Atman, who is Knowledge Absolute, like the adze and other tools of a carpenter. Therefore this Atman is perfectly unattached.

units.label: Verse 101
units.deva:
अन्धत्वमन्दत्वपटुत्वधर्माः
सौगुण्यवैगुण्यवशाद्धि चक्षुषः ।
बाधिर्यमूकत्वमुखास्तथैव
श्रोत्रादिधर्मा न तु वेत्तुर् आत्मनः ॥
units.iast:
andhatvamandatvapaṭutvadharmāḥ
sauguṇyavaiguṇyavaśāddhi cakṣuṣaḥ |
bādhiryamūkatvamukhāstathaiva
śrotrādidharmā na tu vettur ātmanaḥ ||
units.translation: Blindness, dimness, and sharpness are properties of the eye, depending on its good or poor condition. Likewise, deafness, muteness, and the like belong to the ear and other senses, never to the knower, the Self.

gloss.en: depending on good or poor condition

units.editionTranslation: Blindness, weakness and sharpness are conditions of the eye, due merely to its fitness or defectiveness; so are deafness, dumbness, etc., of the ear and so forth – but never of the Atman, the Knower.

units.label: Verse 102
units.deva:
उच्छ्वासनिःश्वासविजृम्भणक्षुत्
प्रस्यन्दनाद्युत्क्रमणादिकाः क्रियाः ।
प्राणादिकर्माणि वदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः
प्राणस्य धर्मावशनापिपासे ॥
units.iast:
ucchvāsaniḥśvāsavijṛmbhaṇakṣut
prasyandanādyutkramaṇādikāḥ kriyāḥ |
prāṇādikarmāṇi vadanti tajjñāḥ
prāṇasya dharmāvaśanāpipāse ||
units.translation: Experts call breathing in and out, yawning, sneezing, secretion, and leaving the body the functions of prāṇa and the other vital airs. Hunger and thirst are qualities of prāṇa itself.

gloss.en: functions of prāṇa and the rest

units.editionTranslation: Inhalation and exhalation, yawning, sneezing, secretion, leaving this body, etc., are called by experts functions of Prana and the rest, while hunger and thirst are characteristics of Prana proper.

units.label: Verse 103
units.deva:
अन्तःकरणमेतेषु चक्षुरादिषु वर्ष्मणि ।
अहमित्यभिमानेन तिष्ठत्याभासतेजसा ॥
units.iast:
antaḥkaraṇameteṣu cakṣurādiṣu varṣmaṇi |
ahamityabhimānena tiṣṭhatyābhāsatejasā ||
units.translation: The inner organ, lit by reflected consciousness, resides in the eye and other senses and in the body, identifying with them through the notion “I.”
units.editionTranslation: The inner organ (mind) has its seat in the organs such as the eye, as well as in the body, identifying with them and endued with a reflection of the Atman.

units.label: Verse 104
units.deva:
अहंकारः स विज्ञेयः कर्ता भोक्ताभिमान्ययम् ।
सत्त्वादिगुणयोगेन चावस्थात्रयमश्नुते ॥
units.iast:
ahaṃkāraḥ sa vijñeyaḥ kartā bhoktābhimānyayam |
sattvādiguṇayogena cāvasthātrayamaśnute ||
units.translation: Know this as ego: it identifies itself as the doer and experiencer, and, through association with the qualities beginning with sattva, undergoes the three states.

gloss.en: through association with qualities beginning with sattva

units.editionTranslation: Know that it is egoism which, identifying itself with the body, becomes the doer or experiencer, and in conjunction with the Gunas such as the Sattva, assumes the three different states.

units.label: Verse 105
units.deva:
विषयाणामानुकूल्ये सुखी दुःखी विपर्यये ।
सुखं दुःखं च तद्धर्मः सदानन्दस्य नात्मनः ॥
units.iast:
viṣayāṇāmānukūlye sukhī duḥkhī viparyaye |
sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca taddharmaḥ sadānandasya nātmanaḥ ||
units.translation: When sense-objects are favorable, one is happy; when they are the opposite, one is unhappy. Happiness and unhappiness are properties of that [ego], not of the ever-blissful Self.
units.editionTranslation: When sense-objects are favourable it becomes happy, and it becomes miserable when the case is contrary. So happiness and misery are characteristics of egoism, and not of the ever-blissful Atman.

units.label: Verse 106
units.deva:
आत्मार्थत्वेन हि प्रेयान्विषयो न स्वतः प्रियः ।
स्वत एव हि सर्वेषामात्मा प्रियतमो यतः

तत आत्मा सदानन्दो नास्य दुःखं कदाचन ॥
units.iast:
ātmārthatvena hi preyānviṣayo na svataḥ priyaḥ |
svata eva hi sarveṣāmātmā priyatamo yataḥ

tata ātmā sadānando nāsya duḥkhaṃ kadācana ||
units.translation: A sense-object is dearer for the sake of the Self, not dear in itself. The Self alone is dearest of all to everyone; therefore the Self is ever-blissful and never suffers.

gloss.en: for the sake of the Self

units.editionTranslation: Sense-objects are pleasurable only as dependent on the Atman manifesting through them, and not independently, because the Atman is by Its very nature the most beloved of all. Therefore the Atman is ever blissful, and never suffers misery.

units.label: Verse 107
units.deva:
यत्सुषुप्तौ निर्विषय आत्मानन्दोऽनुभूयते ।
श्रुतिः प्रत्यक्षमैतिह्यमनुमानं च जाग्रति ॥
units.iast:
yatsuṣuptau nirviṣaya ātmānando'nubhūyate |
śrutiḥ pratyakṣamaitihyamanumānaṃ ca jāgrati ||
units.translation: The Self’s bliss, free from sense-objects, is experienced in deep sleep. Scripture, direct perception, tradition, and inference attest to this in the waking state.
units.editionTranslation: That in profound sleep we experience the bliss of the Atman independent of sense-objects, is clearly attested by the Shruti, direct perception, tradition and inference.

units.label: Verse 108
units.deva:
अव्यक्तनाम्नी परमेशशक्तिः
अनाद्यविद्या त्रिगुणात्मिका परा ।
कार्यानुमेया सुधियैव माया
यया जगत्सर्वमिदं प्रसूयते ॥
units.iast:
avyaktanāmnī parameśaśaktiḥ
anādyavidyā triguṇātmikā parā |
kāryānumeyā sudhiyaiva māyā
yayā jagatsarvamidaṃ prasūyate ||
units.translation: Called the Unmanifest, Māyā is the Supreme Lord’s power: beginningless ignorance, composed of the three guṇas and higher than its effects. The wise infer it from its effects alone; through it this whole world is brought forth.

gloss.en: to be inferred from its effects

units.editionTranslation: Avidya (Nescience) or Maya, called also the Undifferentiated, is the power of the Lord. She is without beginning, is made up of the three Gunas and is superior to the effects (as their cause). She is to be inferred by one of clear intellect only from the effects She produces. It is She who brings forth this whole universe.

units.label: Verse 109
units.deva:
सन्नाप्यसन्नाप्युभयात्मिका नो
भिन्नाप्यभिन्नाप्युभयात्मिका नो ।
साङ्गाप्यनङ्गा ह्युभयात्मिका नो
महाद्भुतानिर्वचनीयरूपा ॥
units.iast:
sannāpyasannāpyubhayātmikā no
bhinnāpyabhinnāpyubhayātmikā no |
sāṅgāpyanaṅgā hyubhayātmikā no
mahādbhutānirvacanīyarūpā ||
units.translation: It is neither existent nor nonexistent, nor both; neither distinct nor nondistinct, nor both; neither with parts nor partless, nor both. Its nature is wondrous and impossible to describe.
units.editionTranslation: She is neither existent nor non-existent nor partaking of both characters; neither same nor different nor both; neither composed of parts nor an indivisible whole nor both. She is most wonderful and cannot be described in words.

units.label: Verse 110
units.deva:
शुद्धाद्वयब्रह्मविभोधनाश्या
सर्पभ्रमो रज्जुविवेकतो यथा ।
रजस्तमःसत्त्वमिति प्रसिद्धा
गुणास्तदीयाः प्रथितैः स्वकार्यैः ॥
units.iast:
śuddhādvayabrahmavibhodhanāśyā
sarpabhramo rajjuvivekato yathā |
rajastamaḥsattvamiti prasiddhā
guṇāstadīyāḥ prathitaiḥ svakāryaiḥ ||
units.translation: Māyā is destroyed through realization of pure, nondual Brahman, just as the snake-delusion is dispelled by recognizing the rope. Its guṇas—rajas, tamas, and sattva—are known through their characteristic effects.
