units.editionTranslation: Maya can be destroyed by the realisation of the pure Brahman, the one without a second, just as the mistaken idea of a snake is removed by the discrimination of the rope. She has her Gunas as Rajas, Tamas and Sattva, named after their respective functions.

units.label: Verse 111
units.deva:
विक्षेपशक्ती रजसः क्रियात्मिका
यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ।
रागादयोऽस्याः प्रभवन्ति नित्यं
दुःखादयो ये मनसो विकाराः ॥
units.iast:
vikṣepaśaktī rajasaḥ kriyātmikā
yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī |
rāgādayo'syāḥ prabhavanti nityaṃ
duḥkhādayo ye manaso vikārāḥ ||
units.translation: Rajas’s projecting power is active in nature, and from it flows the primordial current of activity. From it continually arise attachment and the other mental changes, including sorrow and the like.
units.editionTranslation: Rajas has its Vikshepa-Shakti or projecting power, which is of the nature of an activity, and from which this primeval flow of activity has emanated. From this also, mental modifications such as attachment and grief are continually produced.

units.label: Verse 112
units.deva:
कामः क्रोधो लोभदम्भाद्यसूया
अहंकारेर्ष्यामत्सराद्यास्तु घोराः ।
धर्मा एते राजसाः पुम्प्रवृत्तिः
यस्मादेषा तद्रजो बन्धहेतुः ॥
units.iast:
kāmaḥ krodho lobhadambhādyasūyā
ahaṃkārerṣyāmatsarādyāstu ghorāḥ |
dharmā ete rājasāḥ pumpravṛttiḥ
yasmādeṣā tadrajo bandhahetuḥ ||
units.translation: Desire, anger, greed, arrogance, envy, egoism, jealousy, and the rest are terrible qualities of rajas. Human activity arises from it; therefore rajas is a cause of bondage.
units.editionTranslation: Lust, anger, avarice, arrogance, spite, egoism, envy, jealousy, etc., -- these are the dire attributes of Rajas, from which the worldly tendency of man is produced. Therefore Rajas is a cause of bondage.

units.label: Verse 113
units.deva:
एषावृतिर्नाम तमोगुणस्य
शक्तिर्मया वस्त्ववभासतेऽन्यथा ।
सैषा निदानं पुरुषस्य संसृतेः
विक्षेपशक्तेः प्रवणस्य हेतुः ॥
units.iast:
eṣāvṛtirnāma tamoguṇasya
śaktirmayā vastvavabhāsate'nyathā |
saiṣā nidānaṃ puruṣasya saṃsṛteḥ
vikṣepaśakteḥ pravaṇasya hetuḥ ||
units.translation: This veiling power, called Māyā, belongs to tamas and makes reality appear otherwise. It is the source of a person’s transmigration and the cause that sets the projecting power in motion.

gloss.en: of what is inclined to act

units.editionTranslation: Avriti or the veiling power is the power of Tamas, which makes things appear other than what they are. It is this that causes man’s repeated transmigrations, and starts the action of the projecting power (Vikshepa).

units.label: Verse 114
units.deva:
प्रज्ञावान् अपि पण्डितोऽपि चतुरोऽप्य् अत्यन्तसूक्ष्मात्मदृग्-
व्यालीढस् तमसा न वेत्ति बहुधा संबोधितोऽपि स्फुटम् ।
भ्रान्त्यारोपितम् एव साधु कलयत्यालम्बते तद्गुणान्
हन्तासौ प्रबला दुरन्ततमसः शक्तिर्महत्यावृतिः ॥
units.iast:
prajñāvān api paṇḍito'pi caturo'py atyantasūkṣmātmadṛg-
vyālīḍhas tamasā na vetti bahudhā saṃbodhito'pi sphuṭam |
bhrāntyāropitam eva sādhu kalayatyālambate tadguṇān
hantāsau prabalā durantatamasaḥ śaktirmahatyāvṛtiḥ ||
units.translation: Even an intelligent, learned, clever person who perceives the extremely subtle Self, overwhelmed by tamas, does not know the Self—even if clearly instructed in many ways. He accepts as true what delusion has superimposed and clings to its qualities. Alas, how powerful is the great veiling power of dreadful darkness!

gloss.en: one who perceives the extremely subtle Self

units.editionTranslation: Even wise and learned men and men who are clever and adept in the vision of the exceedingly subtle Atman, are overpowered by Tamas and do not understand the Atman, even though clearly explained in various ways. What is simply superimposed by delusion, they consider as true, and attach themselves to its effects. Alas ! How powerful is the great Avriti Shakti of dreadful Tamas !

units.label: Verse 115
units.deva:
अभावना वा विपरीतभावना
असंभावना विप्रतिपत्तिरस्याः ।
संसर्गयुक्तं न विमुञ्चति ध्रुवं
विक्षेपशक्तिः क्षपयत्यजस्रम् ॥
units.iast:
abhāvanā vā viparītabhāvanā
asaṃbhāvanā vipratipattirasyāḥ |
saṃsargayuktaṃ na vimuñcati dhruvaṃ
vikṣepaśaktiḥ kṣapayatyajasram ||
units.translation: Non-recognition or mistaken understanding, lack of conviction, and misapprehension are effects of this veiling power. It never releases anyone caught up in it; the projecting power wears that person down without ceasing.
units.editionTranslation: Absence of the right judgment, or contrary judgment, want of definite belief and doubt – these certainly never desert one who has any connection with this veiling power, and then the projecting power gives ceaseless trouble.

units.label: Verse 116
units.deva:
अज्ञानमालस्यजडत्वनिद्रा-
प्रमादमूढत्वमुखास्तमोगुणाः ।
एतैः प्रयुक्तो नहि वेत्ति किंचिन्
निद्रालुवत्स्तम्भवद् एव तिष्ठति ॥
units.iast:
ajñānamālasyajaḍatvanidrā-
pramādamūḍhatvamukhāstamoguṇāḥ |
etaiḥ prayukto nahi vetti kiṃcin
nidrāluvatstambhavad eva tiṣṭhati ||
units.translation: Ignorance, laziness, dullness, sleep, heedlessness, stupidity, and the like are qualities of tamas. Driven by these, one understands nothing and remains like a sleeper, like a post.
units.editionTranslation: Ignorance, lassitude, dullness, sleep, inadvertence, stupidity, etc., are attributes of Tamas. One tied to these does not comprehend anything, but remains like one asleep or like a stock or stone.

units.label: Verse 117
units.deva:
सत्त्वं विशुद्धं जलवत्तथापि
ताभ्यां मिलित्वा सरणाय कल्पते ।
यत्रात्मबिम्बः प्रतिबिम्बितः सन्
प्रकाशयत्यर्क इवाखिलं जडम् ॥
units.iast:
sattvaṃ viśuddhaṃ jalavattathāpi
tābhyāṃ militvā saraṇāya kalpate |
yatrātmabimbaḥ pratibimbitaḥ san
prakāśayatyarka ivākhilaṃ jaḍam ||
units.translation: Pure sattva is clear like water; yet, when mixed with those two [rajas and tamas], it serves transmigration. When the image of the Self is reflected in it, it illuminates everything inert, like the sun.
units.editionTranslation: Pure Sattva is (clear) like water, yet in conjunction with Rajas and Tamas it makes for transmigration. The reality of the Atman becomes reflected in Sattva and like the sun reveals the entire world of matter.

units.label: Verse 118
units.deva:
मिश्रस्य सत्त्वस्य भवन्ति धर्माः
त्वमानिताद्या नियमा यमाद्याः ।
श्रद्धा च भक्तिश्च मुमुक्षता च
दैवी च सम्पत्तिरसन्निवृत्तिः ॥
units.iast:
miśrasya sattvasya bhavanti dharmāḥ
tvamānitādyā niyamā yamādyāḥ |
śraddhā ca bhaktiśca mumukṣatā ca
daivī ca sampattirasannivṛttiḥ ||
units.translation: The qualities of mixed sattva are indeed humility (freedom from conceit) and the like, observances and restraints beginning with yama, faith, devotion, longing for liberation, divine virtues, and turning away from what is unreal.

gloss.en: beginning with humility (freedom from conceit), and the like
yama and the rest; restraints and the like
turning away from what is unreal

units.editionTranslation: The traits of mixed Sattva are an utter absence of pride etc., and Niyama, Yama, etc., as well as faith, devotion, yearning for Liberation, the divine tendencies and turning away from the unreal.

units.label: Verse 119
units.deva:
विशुद्धसत्त्वस्य गुणाः प्रसादः
स्वात्मानुभूतिः परमा प्रशान्तिः ।
तृप्तिः प्रहर्षः परमात्मनिष्ठा
यया सदानन्दरसं समृच्छति ॥
units.iast:
viśuddhasattvasya guṇāḥ prasādaḥ
svātmānubhūtiḥ paramā praśāntiḥ |
tṛptiḥ praharṣaḥ paramātmaniṣṭhā
yayā sadānandarasaṃ samṛcchati ||
units.translation: The qualities of pure sattva are clarity, realization of one’s own Self, supreme peace, contentment, joy, and steadfast abidance in the Supreme Self; through this, one attains the essence of eternal bliss.

gloss.en: steadfast abidance in the Supreme Self

units.editionTranslation: The traits of pure Sattva are cheerfulness, the realisation of one’s own Self, supreme peace, contentment, bliss, and steady devotion to the Atman, by which the aspirant enjoys bliss everlasting.

units.label: Verse 120
units.deva:
अव्यक्तमेतत्त्रिगुणैर् निरुक्तं
तत्कारणं नाम शरीरम् आत्मनः ।
सुषुप्तिरेतस्य विभक्त्यवस्था
प्रलीनसर्वेन्द्रियबुद्धिवृत्तिः ॥
units.iast:
avyaktametattriguṇair niruktaṃ
tatkāraṇaṃ nāma śarīram ātmanaḥ |
suṣuptiretasya vibhaktyavasthā
pralīnasarvendriyabuddhivṛttiḥ ||
units.translation: This unmanifest, described as constituted by the three guṇas, is the causal body of the Self. Deep sleep is its distinct state, in which all the functions of the senses and intellect are dissolved.
units.editionTranslation: This Undifferentiated, spoken of as the compound of the three Gunas, is the causal body of the soul. Profound sleep is its special state, in which the functions of the mind and all its organs are suspended.

units.label: Verse 121
units.deva:
सर्वप्रकारप्रमितिप्रशान्तिः
बीजात्मनावस्थितिर् एव बुद्धेः ।
सुषुप्तिरेतस्य किल प्रतीतिः
किंचिन् न वेद्मीति जगत्प्रसिद्धेः ॥
units.iast:
sarvaprakārapramitipraśāntiḥ
bījātmanāvasthitir eva buddheḥ |
suṣuptiretasya kila pratītiḥ
kiṃcin na vedmīti jagatprasiddheḥ ||
units.translation: In deep sleep, every kind of cognition ceases, and the intellect remains only in seed form. Its sign is indeed the universally familiar report, “I knew nothing.”
units.editionTranslation: Profound sleep is the cessation of all kinds of perception, in which the mind remains in a subtle seed-like form. The test of this is the universal verdict, "I did not know anything then".

units.label: Verse 122
units.deva:
देहेन्द्रियप्राणमनोऽहम् आदयः
सर्वे विकारा विषयाः सुखादयः ।
व्योमादिभूतान्यखिलं च विश्वं
अव्यक्तपर्यन्तमिदं ह्यनात्मा ॥
units.iast:
dehendriyaprāṇamano'ham ādayaḥ
sarve vikārā viṣayāḥ sukhādayaḥ |
vyomādibhūtānyakhilaṃ ca viśvaṃ
avyaktaparyantamidaṃ hyanātmā ||
units.translation: The body, senses, vital breaths, mind, ego, and the like; all modifications, sense objects, pleasures, the elements beginning with space, and the whole universe up to the unmanifest—this is indeed the non-Self.
units.editionTranslation: The body, organs, Pranas, Manas, egoism, etc., all modifications, the sense-objects, pleasure and the rest, the gross elements such as the ether, in fact, the whole universe, up to the Undifferentiated – all this is the non-Self.

units.label: Verse 123
units.deva:
माया मायाकार्यं सर्वं महदादिदेहपर्यन्तम् ।
असदिदमनात्मतत्त्वं विद्धि त्वं मरुमरीचिकाकल्पम् ॥
units.iast:
māyā māyākāryaṃ sarvaṃ mahadādidehaparyantam |
asadidamanātmatattvaṃ viddhi tvaṃ marumarīcikākalpam ||
units.translation: Māyā and all its effects, from Mahat down to the body, are unreal and of the nature of the non-Self. Know them to be like a mirage in the desert.

gloss.en: of the nature of the non-Self

units.editionTranslation: From Mahat down to the gross body everything is the effect of Maya: These and Maya itself know thou to be the non-Self, and therefore unreal like the mirage in a desert.

units.label: Verse 124
units.deva:
अथ ते संप्रवक्ष्यामि स्वरूपं परम् आत्मनः ।
यद्विज्ञाय नरो बन्धान्मुक्तः कैवल्यमश्नुते ॥
units.iast:
atha te saṃpravakṣyāmi svarūpaṃ param ātmanaḥ |
yadvijñāya naro bandhānmuktaḥ kaivalyamaśnute ||
units.translation: Now I will explain to you the supreme nature of the Self. Having known it, a person is freed from bondage and attains liberation.
units.editionTranslation: Now I am going to tell thee of the real nature of the supreme Self, realising which man is freed from bondage and attains Liberation.

units.label: Verse 125
units.deva:
अस्ति कश्चित्स्वयं नित्यमहंप्रत्ययलम्बनः ।
अवस्थात्रयसाक्षी संपञ्चकोशविलक्षणः ॥
units.iast:
asti kaścitsvayaṃ nityamahaṃpratyayalambanaḥ |
avasthātrayasākṣī saṃpañcakośavilakṣaṇaḥ ||
units.translation: There is a certain entity, eternal in itself, the basis of the “I”-notion, the witness of the three states, and distinct from the five sheaths.
units.editionTranslation: There is some Absolute Entity, the eternal substratum of the consciousness of egoism, the witness of the three states, and distinct from the five sheaths or coverings:

units.label: Verse 126
units.deva:
यो विजानाति सकलं जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तिषु ।
बुद्धितद्वृत्तिसद्भावमभावमहमित्ययम् ॥
units.iast:
yo vijānāti sakalaṃ jāgratsvapnasuṣuptiṣu |
buddhitadvṛttisadbhāvamabhāvamahamityayam ||
units.translation: That which knows everything in waking, dream, and deep sleep; which knows the presence and absence of the intellect and its functions—this is what is meant by “I.”
units.editionTranslation: Which knows everything that happens in the waking state, in dream and in profound sleep; which is aware of the presence or absence of the mind and its functions; and which is the background of the notion of egoism. – This is That.

units.label: Verse 127
units.deva:
यः पश्यति स्वयं सर्वं यं न पश्यति कश्चन ।
यश्चेतयति बुद्ध्यादि न तद्यं चेतयत्ययम् ॥
units.iast:
yaḥ paśyati svayaṃ sarvaṃ yaṃ na paśyati kaścana |
yaścetayati buddhyādi na tadyaṃ cetayatyayam ||
units.translation: That which sees everything by itself, but which no one sees; that which makes the intellect and the like conscious, but which they do not make conscious—this is the Self.
units.editionTranslation: Which Itself sees all, but which no one beholds, which illumines the intellect etc., but which they cannot illumine. – This is That.

units.label: Verse 128
units.deva:
येन विश्वमिदं व्याप्तं यं न व्याप्नोति किंचन ।
आभारूपमिदं सर्वं यं भान्तमनुभात्ययम् ॥
units.iast:
yena viśvamidaṃ vyāptaṃ yaṃ na vyāpnoti kiṃcana |
ābhārūpamidaṃ sarvaṃ yaṃ bhāntam anubhātyayam ||
units.translation: That which pervades this universe, but which nothing pervades, is the shining Self; all this world appears as its reflection and shines after it.
units.editionTranslation: By which this universe is pervaded, but which nothing pervades, which shining, all this (universe) shines as Its reflection. – This is That.

units.label: Verse 129
units.deva:
यस्य सन्निधिमात्रेण देहेन्द्रियमनोधियः ।
विषयेषु स्वकीयेषु वर्तन्ते प्रेरिता इव ॥
units.iast:
yasya sannidhimātreṇa dehendriyamanodhiyaḥ |
viṣayeṣu svakīyeṣu vartante preritā iva ||
units.translation: By whose mere presence, the body, senses, mind, and intellect seem impelled to act in their own respective fields.
units.editionTranslation: By whose very presence the body, the organs, mind and intellect keep to their respective spheres of action, like servants !

units.label: Verse 130
units.deva:
अहङ्कारादिदेहान्ता विषयाश्च सुखादयः ।
वेद्यन्ते घटवद् येन नित्यबोधस्वरूपिणा ॥
units.iast:
ahaṅkārādidehāntā viṣayāśca sukhādayaḥ |
vedyante ghaṭavad yena nityabodhasvarūpiṇā ||
units.translation: The ego and everything from it down to the body, along with sense objects and pleasures, are known like a pot by that whose nature is eternal awareness.

gloss.en: by that whose nature is eternal awareness

units.editionTranslation: By which everything from egoism down to the body, the sense-objects and pleasure etc., is known as palpably as a jar – for It is the essence of Eternal Knowledge !

units.label: Verse 131
units.deva:
एषोऽन्तरात्मा पुरुषः पुराणो
निरन्तराखण्डसुखानुभूतिः ।
सदैकरूपः प्रतिबोधमात्रो
येनेषिता वागसवश्चरन्ति ॥
units.iast:
eṣo 'ntarātmā puruṣaḥ purāṇo
nirantarākhaṇḍasukhānubhūtiḥ |
sadaikarūpaḥ pratibodhamātro
yeneṣitā vāgasavaścaranti ||
units.translation: This is the innermost Self, the primordial Person, whose nature is the continuous experience of unbroken bliss. Always one in nature and pure awareness in every cognition, it is the one by whose command speech and the vital breaths function.
units.editionTranslation: This is the innermost Self, the primeval Purusha (Being), whose essence is the constant realisation of infinite Bliss, which is ever the same, yet reflecting through the different mental modifications, and commanded by which the organs and Pranas perform their functions.

units.label: Verse 132
units.deva:
अत्रैव सत्त्वात्मनि धीगुहायां
अव्याकृताकाश उशत्प्रकाशः ।
आकाश उच्चै रविवत्प्रकाशते
स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं प्रकाशयन् ॥
units.iast:
atraiva sattvātmani dhīguhāyāṃ
avyākṛtākāśa uśatprakāśaḥ |
ākāśa uccai ravivatprakāśate
svatejasā viśvamidaṃ prakāśayan ||
units.translation: In this very body, in the sattvic mind, in the cave of the intellect, and in the unmanifest space, the Self of radiant splendor shines high like the sun, illuminating this universe by its own light.

gloss.en: in the cave of the intellect

units.editionTranslation: In this very body, in the mind full of Sattva, in the secret chamber of the intellect, in the Akasha known as the Unmanifested, the Atman, of charming splendour, shines like the sun aloft, manifesting this universe through Its own effulgence.

units.label: Verse 133
units.deva:
ज्ञाता मनोऽहंकृतिविक्रियाणां
देहेन्द्रियप्राणकृतक्रियाणाम् ।
अयोऽग्निवत्ताननुवर्तमानो
न चेष्टते नो विकरोति किंचन ॥
units.iast:
jñātā mano 'haṃkṛtivikriyāṇāṃ
dehendriyaprāṇakṛtakriyāṇām |
ayo 'gnivattānanuvartamāno
na ceṣṭate no vikaroti kiṃcana ||
units.translation: The knower of the mind’s and ego’s changes, and of actions performed by the body, senses, and vital breaths, seems to follow their forms like fire in a ball of iron; it does not act or change in the least.
units.editionTranslation: The Knower of the modifications of mind and egoism, and of the activities of the body, the organs and Pranas, apparently taking their forms, like the fire in a ball of iron; It neither acts nor is subject to change in the least.

units.label: Verse 134
units.deva:
न जायते नो म्रियते न वर्धते
न क्षीयते नो विकरोति नित्यः ।
विलीयमानेऽपि वपुष्यमुष्मिन्
न लीयते कुम्भ इवाम्बरं स्वयम् ॥
units.iast:
na jāyate no mriyate na vardhate
na kṣīyate no vikaroti nityaḥ |
vilīyamāne 'pi vapuṣyamuṣmin
na līyate kumbha ivāmbaraṃ svayam ||
units.translation: It is not born, does not die, does not grow, does not decay, and does not change; it is eternal. Even when this body dissolves, it does not dissolve, just as space itself does not disappear when a pot breaks.
units.editionTranslation: It is neither born nor dies, It neither grows nor decays, nor does It undergo any change, being eternal. It does not cease to exist even when this body is destroyed, like the sky in a jar (after it is broken), for It is independent.

units.label: Verse 135
units.deva:
प्रकृतिविकृतिभिन्नः शुद्धबोधस्वभावः
सदसदिदमशेषं भासयन्निर्विशेषः ।
विलसति परमात्मा जाग्रदादिष्ववस्था-
स्वहमहमिति साक्षात्साक्षिरूपेण बुद्धेः ॥
units.iast:
prakṛtivikṛtibhinnaḥ śuddhabodhasvabhāvaḥ
sadasadidamaśeṣaṃ bhāsayannirviśeṣaḥ |
vilasati paramātmā jāgradādiṣvavasthā-
svahamahamiti sākṣātsākṣirūpeṇa buddheḥ ||
units.translation: Distinct from primordial nature and its changes, of the nature of pure awareness and without distinctions, the Supreme Self shines. It illuminates all this—being and non-being—in waking and the other states, directly as the witness of the intellect, as “I, I.”
units.editionTranslation: The Supreme Self, different from the Prakriti and its modifications, of the essence of Pure Knowledge, and Absolute, directly manifests this entire gross and subtle universe, in the waking and other states, as the substratum of the persistent sense of egoism, and manifests Itself as the Witness of the Buddhi, the determinative faculty.

units.label: Verse 136
units.deva:
नियमितमनसामुं त्वं स्वमात्मानम् आत्मन्य्
अयमहमिति साक्षाद्विद्धि बुद्धिप्रसादात् ।
जनिमरणतरङ्गापारसंसारसिन्धुं
प्रतर भव कृतार्थो ब्रह्मरूपेण संस्थः ॥
units.iast:
niyamitamanasāmuṃ tvaṃ svamātmānam ātmany
ayamahamiti sākṣādviddhi buddhiprasādāt |
janimaraṇataraṅgāpārasaṃsārasindhuṃ
pratara bhava kṛtārtho brahmarūpeṇa saṃsthaḥ ||
units.translation: With a disciplined mind and a clear intellect, directly know your own Self within yourself as “This I am.” Cross the shoreless ocean of saṃsāra, whose waves are birth and death; established as Brahman, be fulfilled.
units.editionTranslation: By means of a regulated mind and the purified intellect (Buddhi), realise directly thy own Self in the body so as to identify thyself with It, cross the boundless ocean of Samsara whose waves are birth and death, and firmly established in Brahman as thy own essence, be blessed.

units.label: Verse 137
units.deva:
अत्रानात्मन्यहमिति मतिर्बन्ध एषोऽस्य पुंसः
प्राप्तोऽज्ञानाज्जननमरणक्लेशसंपातहेतुः ।
येनैवायं वपुरिदमसत्सत्यमित्य् आत्मबुद्ध्या
पुष्यत्युक्षत्यवति विषयैस्तन्तुभिः कोशकृद्वत् ॥
units.iast:
atrānātmanyahamiti matirbandha eṣo 'sya puṃsaḥ
prāpto 'jñānājjananamaraṇakleśasaṃpātahetuḥ |
yenaivāyaṃ vapuridamasatsatyamity ātmabuddhyā
puṣyatyukṣatyavati viṣayaistantubhiḥ kośakṛdvat ||
units.translation: The notion “I” in what is not the Self is this person’s bondage; arising from ignorance, it causes the distress of birth and death. Because of this, he treats this unreal body as real and as the Self, nourishing, bathing, and protecting it with sense objects, like a silkworm with the threads of its cocoon.

gloss.en: with the notion that it is the Self

units.editionTranslation: Identifying the Self with this non-Self – this is the bondage of man, which is due to his ignorance, and brings in its train the miseries of birth and death. It is through this that one considers this evanescent body as real, and identifying oneself with it, nourishes, bathes, and preserves it by means of (agreeable) sense-objects, by which he becomes bound as the caterpillar by the threads of its cocoon.

units.label: Verse 138
units.deva:
अतस्मिंस्तद्बुद्धिः प्रभवति विमूढस्य तमसा
विवेकाभावाद्वै स्फुरति भुजगे रज्जुधिषणा ।
ततोऽनर्थव्रातो निपतति समादातुरधिकः
ततो योऽसद्ग्राहः स हि भवति बन्धः शृणु सखे ॥
units.iast:
atasmiṃstadbuddhiḥ prabhavati vimūḍhasya tamasā
vivekābhāvādvai sphurati bhujage rajjudhiṣaṇā |
tato 'narthavrāto nipatati samādāturadhikaḥ
tato yo 'sadgrāhaḥ sa hi bhavati bandhaḥ śṛṇu sakhe ||
units.translation: Through tamas, the deluded person takes one thing for what it is not. From lack of discrimination, he sees a rope in a snake; then great misfortune falls on the one who picks it up. So grasping what is unreal is indeed bondage—listen, friend.

gloss.en: on the one who takes hold

units.editionTranslation: One who is overpowered by ignorance mistakes a thing for what it is not; It is the absence of discrimination that causes one to mistake a snake for a rope, and great dangers overtake him when he seizes it through that wrong notion. Hence, listen, my friend, it is the mistaking of transitory things as real that constitutes bondage.

units.label: Verse 139
units.deva:
अखण्डनित्याद्वयबोधशक्त्या
स्फुरन्तमात्मानमनन्तवैभवम् ।
समावृणोत्यावृतिशक्तिरेषा
तमोमयी राहुरिवार्कबिम्बम् ॥
units.iast:
akhaṇḍanityādvayabodhaśaktyā
sphurantamātmānamanantavaibhavam |
samāvṛṇotyāvṛtiśaktireṣā
tamomayī rāhurivārkabimbam ||
units.translation: This veiling power, made of tamas, covers the Self, which shines with the power of indivisible, eternal, nondual awareness and has limitless glory, just as Rāhu covers the orb of the sun.
units.editionTranslation: This veiling power (Avriti), which preponderates in ignorance, covers the Self, whose glories are infinite and which manifests Itself through the power of knowledge, indivisible, eternal and one without a second – as Rahu does the orb of the sun.

units.label: Verse 140
units.deva:
तिरोभूते स्वात्मन्यमलतरतेजोवति पुमान्
अनात्मानं मोहादहमिति शरीरं कलयति ।
ततः कामक्रोधप्रभृतिभिरमुं बन्धनगुणैः
परं विक्षेपाख्या रजस उरुशक्तिर्व्यथयति ॥
units.iast:
tirobhūte svātmanyamalataratejovati pumān
anātmānaṃ mohādahamiti śarīraṃ kalayati |
tataḥ kāmakrodhaprabhṛtibhiramuṃ bandhanaguṇaiḥ
paraṃ vikṣepākhyā rajasa uruśaktirvyathayati ||
units.translation: When his own Self, endowed with the purest radiance, is obscured, the man through delusion takes the non-Self body to be “I.” Then the mighty power of rajas, called projection, torments him greatly with the binding strands of desire, anger, and the like.
units.editionTranslation: When his own Self, endowed with the purest splendour, is hidden from view, a man through ignorance falsely identifies himself with this body, which is the non-Self. And then the great power of rajas called the projecting power sorely afflicts him through the binding fetters of lust, anger, etc.,

units.label: Verse 141
units.deva:
महामोहग्राहग्रसनगलितात्मावगमनो
धियो नानावस्थां स्वयमभिनयंस्तद्गुणतया ।
अपारे संसारे विषयविषपूरे जलनिधौ
निमज्योन्मज्यायं भ्रमति कुमतिः कुत्सितगतिः ॥
units.iast:
mahāmohagrāhagrāsanagalitātmāvagamano
dhiyo nānāvasthāṃ svayamabhinayaṃstadguṇatayā |
apāre saṃsāre viṣayaviṣapūre jalanidhau
nimajyonmajyāyaṃ bhramati kumatiḥ kutsitagatiḥ ||
units.translation: His knowledge of the Self has been swallowed by the crocodile of great delusion. Identifying with the intellect’s qualities, this foolish person enacts its many states and wanders with wretched fate in the shoreless ocean of saṃsāra, full of the poison of sense objects, sinking and rising.
units.editionTranslation: The man of perverted intellect, having his Self-knowledge swallowed up by the shark of utter ignorance, himself imitates the various states of the intellect (Buddhi), as that is Its superimposed attribute, and drifts up and down in this boundless ocean of Samsara which is full of the poison of sense-enjoyment, now sinking, now rising – a miserable fate indeed!

units.label: Verse 142
units.deva:
भानुप्रभासंजनिताभ्रपङ्क्तिः
भानुं तिरोधाय विजृम्भते यथा ।
आत्मोदिताहंकृतिर् आत्मतत्त्वं
तथा तिरोधाय विजृम्भते स्वयम् ॥
units.iast:
bhānuprabhāsaṃjanitābhrapaṅktiḥ
bhānuṃ tirodhāya vijṛmbhate yathā |
ātmoditāhaṃkṛtir ātmatattvaṃ
tathā tirodhāya vijṛmbhate svayam ||
units.translation: Just as a bank of clouds produced by the sun’s radiance expands and covers the sun, so ego, arising from the Self, expands on its own and covers the reality of the Self.
units.editionTranslation: As layers of clouds generated by the sun’s rays cover the sun and alone appear (in the sky), so egoism generated by the Self, covers the reality of the Self and appears by itself.

units.label: Verse 143
units.deva:
कवलितदिननाथे दुर्दिने सान्द्रमेघैः
व्यथयति हिमझञ्झावायुरुग्रो यथैतान् ।
अविरततमसात्मन्यावृते मूढबुद्धिं
क्षपयति बहुदुःखैस्तीव्रविक्षेपशक्तिः ॥
units.iast:
kavalitadinanāthe durdine sāndrameghaiḥ
vyathayati himajhañjhāvāyurugro yathaitān |
aviratamasātmani āvṛte mūḍhabuddhiṃ
kṣapayati bahuduḥkhaistīvravikṣepaśaktiḥ ||
units.translation: Just as, on an overcast day with the sun hidden by dense clouds, a fierce cold gale torments people, so when the Self is enveloped by unceasing tamas, the intense projecting power wears down the deluded person with many sorrows.

gloss.en: when the lord of the day (the sun)

units.editionTranslation: Just as, on a cloudy day, when the sun is swallowed up by dense clouds, violent cold blasts trouble them, so when the Atman is hidden by intense ignorance, the dreadful Vikshepa Shakti (projecting power) afflicts the foolish man with numerous griefs.

units.label: Verse 144
units.deva:
एताभ्याम् एव शक्तिभ्यां बन्धः पुंसः समागतः ।
याभ्यां विमोहितो देहं मत्वात्मानं भ्रमत्ययम् ॥
units.iast:
etābhyām eva śaktibhyāṃ bandhaḥ puṃsaḥ samāgataḥ |
yābhyāṃ vimohito dehaṃ matvātmānaṃ bhramatyayam ||
units.translation: A person’s bondage arises from these two powers alone. Deluded by them, this person wanders, taking the body to be the Self.
units.editionTranslation: It is from these two powers that man’s bondage has proceeded – beguiled by which he mistakes the body for the Self and wanders (from body to body).

units.label: Verse 145
units.deva:
बीजं संसृतिभूमिजस्य तु तमो देहात्मधीरङ्कुरो
रागः पल्लवमम्बु कर्म तु वपुः स्कन्धोऽसवः शाखिकाः ।
अग्राणीन्द्रियसंहतिश्च विषयाः पुष्पाणि दुःखं फलं
नानाकर्मसमुद्भवं बहुविधं भोक्तात्र जीवः खगः ॥
units.iast:
bījaṃ saṃsṛtibhūmijasya tu tamo dehātmadhīraṅkuro
rāgaḥ pallavamambu karma tu vapuḥ skandho 'savaḥ śākhikāḥ |
agrāṇīndriyasaṃhatiśca viṣayāḥ puṣpāṇi duḥkhaṃ phalaṃ
nānākarmasamudbhavaṃ bahuvidhaṃ bhoktātra jīvaḥ khagaḥ ||
units.translation: In the tree rooted in saṃsāra, ignorance is the seed; the idea that the body is the Self, its sprout; attachment, its tender leaf; karma, its water; the body, its trunk; the vital breaths, its branches; the senses, its twigs; sense objects, its flowers; and the many sorrows born of varied actions, its fruits. The individual being who experiences them is the bird in this tree.
units.editionTranslation: Of the tree of Samsara ignorance is the seed, the identification with the body is its sprout, attachment its tender leaves, work its water, the body its trunk, the vital forces its branches, the organs its twigs, the sense-objects its flowers, various miseries due to diverse works are its fruits, and the individual soul is the bird on it.

units.label: Verse 146
units.deva:
अज्ञानमूलोऽयमनात्मबन्धो
नैसर्गिकोऽनादिरनन्त ईरितः ।
जन्माप्ययव्याधिजरादिदुःख-
प्रवाहपातं जनयत्यमुष्य ॥
units.iast:
ajñānamūlo 'yamanātmabandho
naisargiko 'nādirananta īritaḥ |
janmāpyayavyādhijarādiduḥkha-
pravāhapātaṃ janayatyamuṣya ||
units.translation: This bondage to the non-Self has ignorance as its root; it is inherent, beginningless, and endless, the sages declare. It causes this person to fall into the stream of sorrows such as birth, death, illness, and old age.
units.editionTranslation: This bondage of the non-Self springs from ignorance, is self-caused, and is described as without beginning and end. It subjects one to the long train of miseries such as birth, death, disease and decrepitude.

units.label: Verse 147
units.deva:
नास्त्रैर् न शस्त्रैर् अनिलेन वह्निना
छेत्तुं न शक्यो न च कर्मकोटिभिः ।
विवेकविज्ञानमहासिना विना
धातुः प्रसादेन शितेन मञ्जुना ॥
units.iast:
nāstrair na śastrair anilena vahninā
chettuṃ na śakyo na ca karmakoṭibhiḥ |
vivekavijñānamahāsinā vinā
dhātuḥ prasādena śitena mañjunā ||
units.translation: This bondage cannot be cut by missiles, weapons, wind, fire, or millions of actions. It can be cut only by the great sword of discriminative knowledge, sharp and fine, through the Creator’s grace.
units.editionTranslation: This bondage can be destroyed neither by weapons nor by wind, nor by fire, nor by millions of acts – by nothing except the wonderful sword of knowledge that comes of discrimination, sharpened by the grace of the Lord.

units.label: Verse 148
units.deva:
श्रुतिप्रमाणैकमतेः स्वधर्म
निष्ठा तयैवात्मविशुद्धिरस्य ।
विशुद्धबुद्धेः परम् आत्मवेदनं
तेनैव संसारसमूलनाशः ॥
units.iast:
śrutipramāṇaikamateḥ svadharma
niṣṭhā tayaivātmaviśuddhirasya |
viśuddhabuddheḥ param ātmavedanaṃ
tenaiva saṃsārasamūlanāśaḥ ||
units.translation: For one who holds śruti as the sole authority, steadfastness in one’s own dharma brings inner purification. From that alone, the clear-minded person realizes the Supreme Self; by that alone, saṃsāra is destroyed down to its root.
units.editionTranslation: One who is passionately devoted to the authority of the Shrutis acquires steadiness in his Svadharma, which alone conduces to the purity of his mind. The man of pure mind realises the Supreme Self, and by this alone Samsara with its root is destroyed.

units.label: Verse 149
units.deva:
कोशैर् अन्नमयाद्यैः पञ्चभिरात्मा न संवृतो भाति ।
निजशक्तिसमुत्पन्नैः शैवालपटलैर् इवाम्बु वापीस्थम् ॥
units.iast:
kośair annamayādyaiḥ pañcabhirātmā na saṃvṛto bhāti |
nijaśaktisamutpannaiḥ śaivālapaṭalair ivāmbu vāpīstham ||
units.translation: The Self, covered by the five sheaths beginning with the food sheath, does not shine forth—like water in a pool hidden by layers of algae produced by its own power.
units.editionTranslation: Covered by the five sheaths – the material one and the rest – which are the products of Its own power, the Self ceases to appear, like the water of a tank by its accumulation of sedge.

units.label: Verse 150
units.deva:
तच्छैवालापनये सम्यक् सलिलं प्रतीयते शुद्धम् ।
तृष्णासन्तापहरं सद्यः सौख्यप्रदं परं पुंसः ॥
units.iast:
tacchaivālāpanaye samyak salilaṃ pratīyate śuddham |
tṛṣṇāsantāpaharaṃ sadyaḥ saukhyapradaṃ paraṃ puṃsaḥ ||
units.translation: When that algae is thoroughly removed, the water appears pure—at once relieving the burning of thirst and giving a person the highest happiness.
units.editionTranslation: On the removal of that sedge the perfectly pure water that allays the pangs of thirst and gives immediate joy, appears unobstructed before the man.

units.label: Verse 151
units.deva:
पञ्चानाम् अपि कोशानामपवादे विभात्ययं शुद्धः ।
नित्यानन्दैकरसः प्रत्यग्रूपः परः स्वयंज्योतिः ॥
units.iast:
pañcānām api kośānāmapavāde vibhātyayaṃ śuddhaḥ |
nityānandaikarasaḥ pratyagrūpaḥ paraḥ svayaṃjyotiḥ ||
units.translation: When the five sheaths are all set aside, this pure Self shines forth—of the sole essence of eternal bliss, inward in nature, supreme, and self-luminous.
units.editionTranslation: When all the five sheaths have been eliminated, the Self of man appears – pure, of the essence of everlasting and unalloyed bliss, indwelling, supreme and self-effulgent.

units.label: Verse 152
units.deva:
आत्मानात्मविवेकः कर्तव्यो बन्धमुक्तये विदुषा ।
तेनैवानन्दी भवति स्वं विज्ञाय सच्चिदानन्दम् ॥
units.iast:
ātmānātmavivekaḥ kartavyo bandhamuktaye viduṣā |
tenaivānandī bhavati svaṃ vijñāya saccidānandam ||
units.translation: The wise person should distinguish the Self from the non-Self to be free of bondage. By that alone, knowing one’s own Self as Being-Consciousness-Bliss, one becomes blissful.
units.editionTranslation: To remove his bondage the wise man should discriminate between the Self and the non-Self. By that alone he comes to know his own Self as Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute and becomes happy.

units.label: Verse 153
units.deva:
मुञ्जादिषीकाम् इव दृश्यवर्गात्
प्रत्यञ्चमात्मानमसङ्गमक्रियम् ।
विविच्य तत्र प्रविलाप्य सर्वं
तद् आत्मना तिष्ठति यः स मुक्तः ॥
units.iast:
muñjādiṣīkām iva dṛśyavargāt
pratyañcamātmānamasaṅgamakriyam |
vivicya tatra pravilāpya sarvaṃ
tad ātmanā tiṣṭhati yaḥ sa muktaḥ ||
units.translation: Whoever, like separating the inner stalk from muñja grass, distinguishes the inward Self—unattached and inactive—from everything seen, dissolves all into it, and remains as that Self, is liberated.
units.editionTranslation: He indeed is free who discriminates between all sense-objects and the indwelling, unattached and inactive Self – as one separates a stalk of grass from its enveloping sheath – and merging everything in It, remains in a state of identity with That.

units.label: Verse 154
units.deva:
देहोऽयमन्नभवनोऽन्नमयस्तु कोशः
चान्नेन जीवति विनश्यति तद्विहीनः ।
त्वक्चर्ममांसरुधिरास्थिपुरीषराशिः
नायं स्वयं भवितुमर्हति नित्यशुद्धः ॥
units.iast:
deho 'yamannabhavano 'nnamayastu kośaḥ
cānnena jīvati vinaśyati tadvihīnaḥ |
tvakcarmamāṃsarudhirāsthipurīṣarāśiḥ
nāyaṃ svayaṃ bhavitumarhati nityaśuddhaḥ ||
units.translation: This body, produced from food, is the food-made sheath. It lives on food and perishes without it. A heap of skin, hide, flesh, blood, bones, and waste cannot itself be the eternally pure Self.
units.editionTranslation: This body of ours is the product of food and comprises the material sheath; it lives on food and dies without it; it is a mass of skin, flesh, blood, bones and filth, and can never be the eternally pure, self-existent Atman.

units.label: Verse 155
units.deva:
पूर्वं जनेरधिमृतेर् अपि नायमस्ति
जातक्षणः क्षणगुणोऽनियतस्वभावः ।
नैको जडश्च घटवत्परिदृश्यमानः
स्वात्मा कथं भवति भावविकारवेत्ता ॥
units.iast:
pūrvaṃ janeradhimṛter api nāyamasti
jātakṣaṇaḥ kṣaṇaguṇo 'niyatasvabhāvaḥ |
naiko jaḍaśca ghaṭavatparidṛśyamānaḥ
svātmā kathaṃ bhavati bhāvavikāravettā ||
units.translation: It does not exist before birth or after death; it is momentary and unstable by nature, not unitary, inert, and seen like a pot. How could it be one’s own Self, the knower of changes in things?

gloss.en: lasting only an instant from birth

units.editionTranslation: It does not exist prior to inception or posterior to dissolution, but lasts only for a short (intervening) period; its virtues are transient, and it is changeful by nature; it is manifold, inert, and is a sense-object, like a jar; how can it be one’s own Self, the Witness of changes in all things ?

units.label: Verse 156
units.deva:
पाणिपादादिमान्देहो नात्मा व्यङ्गेऽपि जीवनात् ।
तत्तच्छक्तेरनाशाच्च न नियम्यो नियामकः ॥
units.iast:
pāṇipādādimān deho nātmā vyaṅge 'pi jīvanāt |
tattacchakteranāśāc ca na niyamyo niyāmakaḥ ||
units.translation: The body, with hands, feet, and other limbs, is not the Self: life continues even when a limb is impaired. And since the corresponding faculties have not disappeared, what is governed is not the governor.

gloss.en: having hands, feet, and other limbs

units.editionTranslation: The body, consisting of arms, legs, etc., cannot be the Atman, for one continues to live even when particular limbs are gone, and the different functions of the organism also remain intact. The body which is subject to another’s rule cannot be the Self which is the Ruler of all.

units.label: Verse 157
units.deva:
देहतद्धर्मतत्कर्मतदवस्थादिसाक्षिणः ।
सत एव स्वतःसिद्धं तद्वैलक्षण्यम् आत्मनः ॥
units.iast: dehataddharmatatkarmatadavasthādisākṣiṇaḥ sata eva svataḥ siddhaṃ tadvailakṣaṇyam ātmanaḥ ||
units.translation: The Self—the existent witness of the body, its properties, actions, states, and so on—is self-evidently distinct from it.

gloss.en: of the existent; of what is real

units.editionTranslation: That the Atman as the abiding Reality is different from the body, its characteristics, its activities, its states, etc., of which It is the witness, is self-evident.

units.label: Verse 158
units.deva:
शल्यराशिर्मांसलिप्तो मलपूर्णोऽतिकश्मलः ।
कथं भवेदयं वेत्ता स्वयमेतद्विलक्षणः ॥
units.iast:
śalyarāśir māṃsalipto malapūrṇo 'tikaśmalaḥ |
kathaṃ bhaved ayaṃ vettā svayam etad-vilakṣaṇaḥ ||
units.translation: How could this [body]—a heap of bones smeared with flesh, full of filth, and exceedingly impure—be the knower, which is itself distinct from this [body]?
units.editionTranslation: How can the body, being a pack of bones, covered with flesh, full of filth and highly impure, be the self-existent Atman, the Knower, which is ever distinct from it ?

units.label: Verse 159
units.deva:
त्वङ्मांसमेदोऽस्थिपुरीषराशा-
वहंमतिं मूढजनः करोति ।
विलक्षणं वेत्ति विचारशीलो
निजस्वरूपं परमार्थ भूतम् ॥
units.iast:
tvaṅmāṃsamedo 'sthipurīṣarāśāv ahaṃmatiṃ mūḍhajanaḥ karoti |
vilakṣaṇaṃ vetti vicāraśīlo nija-svarūpaṃ paramārtha-bhūtam ||
units.translation: The foolish person forms the thought “I” in the heap of skin, flesh, fat, bones, and excrement. The reflective person knows his own nature, distinct from it, as the ultimate Reality.
units.editionTranslation: It is the foolish man who identifies himself with a mass of skin, flesh, fat, bones and filth, while the man of discrimination knows his own Self, the only Reality that there is, as distinct from the body.

units.label: Verse 160
units.deva:
देहोऽहम् इत्य् एव जडस्य बुद्धिः
देहे च जीवे विदुषस्त्वहंधीः ।
विवेकविज्ञानवतो महात्मनो
ब्रह्माहम् इत्य् एव मतिः सदात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
deho 'ham ity eva jaḍasya buddhiḥ
dehe ca jīve viduṣas tv ahaṃdhīḥ |
vivekavijñānavato mahātmanaḥ
brahmāham ity eva matiḥ sadātmani ||
units.translation: The dull person’s thought is only “I am the body.” The learned person’s sense of “I” is in the body and the individual soul; the great one endowed with discriminative knowledge holds only the thought “I am Brahman” in the ever-existent Self.

gloss.en: of the dull or ignorant person
of one endowed with discriminative knowledge

units.editionTranslation: The stupid man thinks he is the body, the book-learned man identifies himself with the mixture of body and soul, while the sage possessed of realisation due to discrimination looks upon the eternal Atman as his Self, and thinks, "I am Brahman".

units.label: Verse 161
units.deva:
अत्रात्मबुद्धिं त्यज मूढबुद्धे
त्वङ्मांसमेदोऽस्थिपुरीषराशौ ।
सर्वात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे
कुरुष्व शान्ति परमां भजस्व ॥
units.iast:
atrātmabuddhiṃ tyaja mūḍhabuddhe
tvaṅmāṃsamedo 'sthipurīṣarāśau |
sarvātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe
kuruṣva śāntiṃ paramāṃ bhajasva ||
units.translation: Here, O dull-minded one, abandon the notion of Self in this heap of skin, flesh, fat, bones, and excrement. In nondual Brahman, the Self of all, establish supreme peace; seek it.
units.editionTranslation: O foolish person, cease to identify thyself with this bundle of skin, flesh, fat, bones and filth, and identify thyself instead with the Absolute Brahman, the Self of all, and thus attain to supreme Peace.

units.label: Verse 162
units.deva:
देहेन्द्रियादावसति भ्रमोदितां
विद्वानहन्तां न जहाति यावत् ।
तावन् न तस्यास्ति विमुक्तिवार्ताप्य्
अस्त्वेष वेदान्तनयान्तदर्शी ॥
units.iast:
dehendriyādāv asati bhramoditāṃ
vidvānahantāṃ na jahāti yāvat |
tāvan na tasyāsti vimuktivārtāpy
astveṣa vedāntanayāntadarśī ||
units.translation: As long as the text-learned person does not give up the ego-sense born of delusion and lodged in the unreal body, senses, and so on, there is not even talk of liberation for him—even if he has studied Vedānta to its end.

gloss.en: one who has seen or studied

units.editionTranslation: As long as the book-learned man does not give up his mistaken identification with the body, organs, etc., which are unreal, there is no talk of emancipation for him, even if he be ever so erudite in the Vedanta philosophy.

units.label: Verse 163
units.deva:
छायाशरीरे प्रतिबिम्बगात्रे
यत्स्वप्नदेहे हृदि कल्पिताङ्गे ।
यथात्मबुद्धिस्तव नास्ति काचिज्
जीवच्छरीरे च तथैव मास्तु ॥
units.iast:
chāyāśarīre pratibimbagātre
yat svapnadehe hṛdi kalpitāṅge |
yathātmabuddhis tava nāsti kācij
jīvaccharīre ca tathaiva māstu ||
units.translation: Just as you have no notion of Self in the shadow-body, reflected body, dream-body, or body imagined in the mind, so let there be none in the living body either.
units.editionTranslation: Just as thou dost not identify thyself with the shadow-body, the image-body, the dream-body, or the body thou hast in the imaginations of thy heart, cease thou to do likewise with the living body also.

units.label: Verse 164
units.deva:
देहात्मधीर् एव नृणामसद्धियां
जन्मादिदुःखप्रभवस्य बीजम् ।
यतस्ततस्त्वं जहि तां प्रयत्नात्
त्यक्ते तु चित्ते न पुनर्भवाशा ॥
units.iast:
dehātmadhīr eva nṛṇām asaddhiyāṃ
janmādiduḥkhaprabhavasya bījam |
yatas tatas tvaṃ jahi tāṃ prayatnāt
tyakte tu citte na punarbhavāśā ||
units.translation: For people whose understanding is false, the thought “the body is the Self” is the seed from which birth and suffering arise. Therefore, make an effort to abandon it. When the mind is relinquished, there is no expectation of rebirth.

gloss.en: thought that the body is the Self

units.editionTranslation: Identifications with the body alone is the root that produces the misery of birth etc., of people who are attached to the unreal; therefore destroy thou this with the utmost care. When this identification caused by the mind is given up, there is no more chance for rebirth.

units.label: Verse 165
units.deva:
कर्मेन्द्रियैः पञ्चभिरञ्चितोऽयं
प्राणो भवेत्प्राणमयस्तु कोशः ।
येनात्मवानन्नमयोऽनुपूर्णः
प्रवर्ततेऽसौ सकलक्रियासु ॥
units.iast:
karmendriyaiḥ pañcabhir añcito 'yaṃ
prāṇo bhavet prāṇamayas tu kośaḥ |
yenātmavān annamayo 'nupūrṇaḥ
pravartate 'sau sakala-kriyāsu ||
units.translation: Joined with the five organs of action, prāṇa is the prāṇamaya sheath. Through it, the food-made sheath is filled throughout, becomes living, and carries out every activity.
units.editionTranslation: The Prana, with which we are all familiar, coupled with the five organs of action, forms the vital sheath, permeated by which the material sheath engages itself in all activities as if it were living.

units.label: Verse 166
units.deva:
नैवात्मापि प्राणमयो वायुविकारो
गन्तागन्ता वायुवदन्तर्बहिरेषः ।
यस्मात् किंचित् क्वापि न वेत्तीष्टमनिष्टं
स्वं वान्यं वा किंचन नित्यं परतन्त्रः ॥
units.iast:
naivātmāpi prāṇamayo vāyuvikāro
gantāgantā vāyuvad antarbahir eṣaḥ |
yasmāt kiṃcit kvāpi na vettīṣṭam aniṣṭaṃ
svaṃ vānyaṃ vā kiṃcana nityaṃ paratantraḥ ||
units.translation: Nor is the prāṇamaya sheath the Self: it is a modification of air and moves in and out like the wind. It never knows anything, anywhere—what is welcome or unwelcome, its own or another’s—and is always dependent on something else.
units.editionTranslation: Neither is the vital sheath the Self – because it is a modification of Vayu, and like the air it enters into and comes out of the body, and because it never knows in the least either its own weal and woe or those of others, being eternally dependent on the Self.

units.label: Verse 167
units.deva:
ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि च मनश्च मनोमयः स्यात्
कोशो ममाहमिति वस्तुविकल्पहेतुः ।
संज्ञादिभेदकलनाकलितो बलीयांस्
तत्पूर्वकोशमभिपूर्य विजृम्भते यः ॥
units.iast:
jñānendriyāṇi ca manaś ca manomayaḥ syāt
kośo mamāham iti vastu-vikalpa-hetuḥ |
saṃjñādibhedakalanākalito balīyāṃs
tatpūrva-kośam abhipūrya vijṛmbhate yaḥ ||
units.translation: The five organs of knowledge and the mind make up the mind-made sheath, the cause of distinctions among things as “I” and “mine.” Strong and forming distinctions such as names, it expands after pervading the preceding sheath.
units.editionTranslation: The organs of knowledge together with the mind form the mental sheath – the cause of the diversity of things such as "I" and "mine". It is powerful and endued with the faculty of creating differences of name etc., It manifests itself as permeating the preceding, i.e. the vital sheath.

units.label: Verse 168
units.deva:
पञ्चेन्द्रियैः पञ्चभिर् एव होतृभिः
प्रचीयमानो विषयाज्यधारया ।
जाज्वल्यमानो बहुवासनेन्धनैः
मनोमयाग्निर्दहति प्रपञ्चम् ॥
units.iast:
pañcendriyaiḥ pañcabhir eva hotṛbhiḥ
pracīyamāno viṣayājyadhārayā |
jājvalyamāno bahuvāsanendhanaiḥ
manomayāgnir dahati prapañcam ||
units.translation: The mind-made fire, fed by the five senses acting as priests and by streams of sense-objects as ghee, blazes with the fuel of many latent tendencies and burns the manifold world.
units.editionTranslation: The mental sheath is the (sacrificial) fire which, fed with the fuel of numerous desires by the five sense-organs which serve as priests, and set ablaze by the sense-objects which act as the stream of oblations, brings about this phenomenal universe.

units.label: Verse 169
units.deva:
न ह्यस्त्य् अविद्या मनसोऽतिरिक्ता
मनो ह्यविद्या भवबन्धहेतुः ।
तस्मिन्विनष्टे सकलं विनष्टं
विजृम्भितेऽस्मिन्सकलं विजृम्भते ॥
units.iast:
na hy asty avidyā manaso 'tiriktā
mano hy avidyā bhavabandhahetuḥ |
tasmin vinaṣṭe sakalaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ
vijṛmbhite 'smin sakalaṃ vijṛmbhate ||
units.translation: There is no ignorance apart from the mind: the mind itself is ignorance, the cause of bondage to worldly existence. When it is destroyed, all is destroyed; when it expands, all this expands.
units.editionTranslation: There is no Ignorance (Avidya) outside the mind. The mind alone is Avidya, the cause of the bondage of transmigration. When that is destroyed, all else is destroyed, and when it is manifested, everything else is manifested.

units.label: Verse 170
units.deva:
स्वप्नेऽर्थशून्ये सृजति स्वशक्त्या
भोक्त्रादिविश्वं मन एव सर्वम् ।
तथैव जाग्रत्य् अपि नो विशेषः
तत्सर्वमेतन्मनसो विजृम्भणम् ॥
units.iast:
svapne 'rthaśūnye sṛjati svaśaktyā
bhoktrādiviśvaṃ mana eva sarvam |
tathaiva jāgraty api no viśeṣaḥ
tat sarvam etan manaso vijṛmbhaṇam ||
units.translation: In a dream devoid of external objects, the mind alone creates by its own power the whole world, beginning with the experiencer. The same is true in waking; there is no difference. All this is an expansion of the mind.
units.editionTranslation: In dreams, when there is no actual contact with the external world, the mind alone creates the whole universe consisting of the experiencer etc. Similarly in the waking state also; there is no difference. Therefore all this (phenomenal universe) is the projection of the mind.

units.label: Verse 171
units.deva:
सुषुप्तिकाले मनसि प्रलीने
नैवास्ति किञ्चित् सकलप्रसिद्धेः ।
अतो मनःकल्पित एव पुंसः
संसार एतस्य न वस्तुतोऽस्ति ॥
units.iast:
suṣuptikāle manasi pralīne
naivāsti kiṃcit sakalaprasiddheḥ |
ato manaḥkalpita eva puṃsaḥ
saṃsāra etasya na vastuto 'sti ||
units.translation: During deep sleep, when the mind has dissolved, nothing whatsoever exists, as is well known to all. Therefore, this person’s saṃsāra is imagined by the mind alone and does not exist in reality.
units.editionTranslation: In dreamless sleep, when the mind is reduced to its causal state, there exists nothing (for the person asleep), as is evident from universal experience. Hence man’s relative existence is simply the creation of his mind, and has no objective reality.

units.label: Verse 172
units.deva:
वायुनानीयते मेघः पुनस्तेनैव नीयते ।
मनसा कल्प्यते बन्धो मोक्षस्तेनैव कल्प्यते ॥
units.iast:
vāyunānīyate meghaḥ punas tenaiva nīyate |
manasā kalpyate bandho mokṣas tenaiva kalpyate ||
units.translation: Wind carries a cloud along, then carries it away again. The mind conceives bondage, and by that very mind liberation is conceived.
units.editionTranslation: Clouds are brought in by the wind and again driven away by the same agency. Similarly, man’s bondage is caused by the mind, and Liberation too is caused by that alone.

units.label: Verse 173
units.deva:
देहादिसर्वविषये परिकल्प्य रागं
बध्नाति तेन पुरुषं पशुवद्गुणेन ।
वैरस्यमत्र विषवत् सुविधाय पश्चाद्
एनं विमोचयति तन्मन एव बन्धात् ॥
units.iast:
dehādisarvaviṣaye parikalpya rāgaṃ
badhnāti tena puruṣaṃ paśuvad guṇena |
vairasyam atra viṣavat suvidhāya paścād
enaṃ vimocayati tan mana eva bandhāt ||
units.translation: Having formed attachment to all objects beginning with the body, the mind binds a person with that rope as it would an animal. Later, having firmly established distaste for them as for poison, that same mind alone frees this person from bondage.
units.editionTranslation: It (first) creates an attachment in man for the body and all other sense-objects, and binds him through that attachment like a beast by means of ropes. Afterwards, the selfsame mind creates in the individual an utter distaste for these sense-objects as if they were poison, and frees him from the bondage.

units.label: Verse 174
units.deva:
तस्मान्मनः कारणमस्य जन्तोः
बन्धस्य मोक्षस्य च वा विधाने ।
बन्धस्य हेतुर्मलिनं रजोगुणैः
मोक्षस्य शुद्धं विरजस्तमस्कम् ॥
units.iast:
tasmān manaḥ kāraṇam asya jantoḥ
bandhasya mokṣasya ca vā vidhāne |
bandhasya hetur malinaṃ rajoguṇaiḥ
mokṣasya śuddhaṃ virajastamaskam ||
units.translation: Therefore the mind is the cause of this being’s bondage or liberation. Impure through the qualities of rajas, it causes bondage; pure and free of rajas and tamas, it causes liberation.
units.editionTranslation: Therefore the mind is the only cause that brings about man’s bondage or Liberation: when tainted by the effects of Rajas it leads to bondage, and when pure and divested of the Rajas and Tamas elements it conduces to Liberation.

units.label: Verse 175
units.deva:
विवेकवैराग्यगुणातिरेकाच्
छुद्धत्वमासाद्य मनो विमुक्त्यै ।
भवत्यतो बुद्धिमतो मुमुक्षोस्
ताभ्यां दृढाभ्यां भवितव्यमग्रे ॥
units.iast:
vivekavairāgyaguṇātirekāc
chuddhatvam āsādya mano vimuktyai |
bhavatyato buddhimato mumukṣos
tābhyāṃ dṛḍhābhyāṃ bhavitavyam agre ||
units.translation: Through a predominance of discrimination and dispassion, the mind attains purity and becomes fit for liberation. Therefore, an intelligent seeker of liberation must make these two firm from the outset.
units.editionTranslation: Attaining purity through a preponderance of discrimination and renunciation, the mind makes for Liberation. Hence the wise seeker after Liberation must first strengthen these two.

units.label: Verse 176
units.deva:
मनो नाम महाव्याघ्रो विषयारण्यभूमिषु ।
चरत्यत्र न गच्छन्तु साधवो ये मुमुक्षवः ॥
units.iast:
mano nāma mahāvyāghro viṣayāraṇyabhūmiṣu |
caraty atra na gacchantu sādhavo ye mumukṣavaḥ ||
units.translation: The mind, called the great tiger, roams in the forest of sense-objects. Let the good seekers of liberation not go there.
units.editionTranslation: In the forest-tract of sense-pleasures there prowls a huge tiger called the mind. Let good people who have a longing for Liberation never go there.

units.label: Verse 177
units.deva:
मनः प्रसूते विषयानशेषान्
स्थूलात्मना सूक्ष्मतया च भोक्तुः ।
शरीरवर्णाश्रमजातिभेदान्
गुणक्रियाहेतुफलानि नित्यम् ॥
units.iast:
manaḥ prasūte viṣayān aśeṣān
sthūlātmanā sūkṣmatayā ca bhoktuḥ |
śarīravarṇāśramajātibhedān
guṇakriyāhetuphalāni nityam ||
units.translation: The mind continually produces every object for the experiencer, in gross or subtle form. It also produces distinctions of body, social class, life-stage, and birth, along with qualities, actions, causes, and results.
units.editionTranslation: The mind continually produces for the experiencer all sense-objects without exception, whether perceived as gross or fine, the differences of body, caste, order of life, and tribe, as well as the varieties of qualification, action, means and results.

units.label: Verse 178
units.deva:
असङ्गचिद्रूपममुं विमोह्य
देहेन्द्रियप्राणगुणैर् निबद्ध्य ।
अहंममेति भ्रमयत्यजस्रं
मनः स्वकृत्येषु फलोपभुक्तिषु ॥
units.iast:
asaṅgacidrūpam amuṃ vimohya
dehendriyaprāṇaguṇair nibaddhya |
ahaṃmameti bhramayaty ajasraṃ
manaḥ svakṛtyeṣu phalopabhuktiṣu ||
units.translation: After deluding this one, whose nature is unattached consciousness, and binding it with the qualities of body, senses, and vital breath, the mind continually makes it wander through its own actions and enjoyment of their fruits, thinking “I” and “mine.”
units.editionTranslation: Deluding the Jiva, which is unattached Pure Intelligence, and binding it by the ties of body, organs and Pranas, the mind causes it to wander, with ideas of "I" and "mine", amidst the varied enjoyment of results achieved by itself.

units.label: Verse 179
units.deva:
अध्यासदोषात्पुरुषस्य संसृतिः
अध्यासबन्धस्त्वमुनैव कल्पितः ।
रजस्तमोदोषवतोऽविवेकिनो
जन्मादिदुःखस्य निदानमेतत् ॥
units.iast:
adhyāsadoṣāt puruṣasya saṃsṛtiḥ
adhyāsabandhas tv amunaiva kalpitaḥ |
rajastamodoṣavato 'vivekino
janmādiduḥkhasya nidānam etat ||
units.translation: A person’s transmigration comes from the defect of superimposition, and bondage through superimposition is imagined by this [mind] alone. For the undiscerning person, tainted by the faults of rajas and tamas, this is the source of suffering beginning with birth.

gloss.en: of one tainted by the faults

units.editionTranslation: Man’s transmigration is due to the evil of superimposition, and the bondage of superimposition is created by the mind alone. It is this that causes the misery of birth etc., for the man of non-discrimination who is tainted by Rajas and Tamas.

units.label: Verse 180
units.deva:
अतः प्राहुर्मनोऽविद्यां पण्डितास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ।
येनैव भ्राम्यते विश्वं वायुनेवाभ्रमण्डलम् ॥
units.iast:
ataḥ prāhur mano 'vidyāṃ paṇḍitās tattvadarśinaḥ |
yenaiva bhrāmyate viśvaṃ vāyunevābhra-maṇḍalam ||
units.translation: Therefore the wise who see the truth call the mind ignorance: by the mind alone the universe is driven about, as a mass of clouds is driven by the wind.
units.editionTranslation: Hence sages who have fathomed its secret have designated the mind as Avidya or ignorance, by which alone the universe is moved to and fro, like masses of clouds by the wind.

units.label: Verse 181
units.deva:
तन्मनःशोधनं कार्यं प्रयत्नेन मुमुक्षुणा ।
विशुद्धे सति चैतस्मिन्मुक्तिः करफलायते ॥
units.iast:
tan manaḥśodhanaṃ kāryaṃ prayatnena mumukṣuṇā |
viśuddhe sati caitasmin muktiḥ kara-phalāyate ||
units.translation: Therefore a seeker of liberation should purify the mind with effort. When this mind is pure, liberation is as easy to attain as a fruit in the palm.
units.editionTranslation: Therefore the seeker after Liberation must carefully purify the mind. When this is purified, Liberation is as easy of access as a fruit on the palm of one’s hand.

units.label: Verse 182
units.deva:
मोक्षैकसक्त्या विषयेषु रागं
निर्मूल्य संन्यस्य च सर्वकर्म ।
सच्छ्रद्धया यः श्रवणादिनिष्ठो
रजःस्वभावं स धुनोति बुद्धेः ॥
units.iast:
mokṣaika-saktyā viṣayeṣu rāgaṃ
nirmūlya saṃnyasya ca sarva-karma |
sacchraddhayā yaḥ śravaṇādi-niṣṭho
rajaḥ-svabhāvaṃ sa dhunoti buddheḥ ||
units.translation: Whoever, with single-minded devotion to liberation, uproots attachment to sense-objects, renounces all action, and is steadfast in hearing and the rest with true faith, shakes the rajas nature from the intellect.
units.editionTranslation: He who by means of one-pointed devotion to Liberation roots out the attachment to sense-objects, renounces all actions, and with faith in the Real Brahman regularly practices hearing, etc., succeeds in purging the Rajasika nature of the intellect.

units.label: Verse 183
units.deva:
मनोमयो नापि भवेत्परात्मा
ह्याद्यन्तवत्त्वात्परिणामिभावात् ।
दुःखात्मकत्वाद्विषयत्वहेतोः
द्रष्टा हि दृश्यात्मतया न दृष्टः ॥
units.iast:
manomayo nāpi bhavet parātmā
hy ādyantavattvāt pariṇāmibhāvāt |
duḥkhātmakatvād viṣayatvahetoḥ
draṣṭā hi dṛśyātmatayā na dṛṣṭaḥ ||
units.translation: The mind-made sheath cannot be the Supreme Self either: it has a beginning and an end, is changeable, is marked by suffering, and is an object. The seer is never seen as something observed.

gloss.en: because of having the nature of

units.editionTranslation: Neither can the mental sheath be the Supreme Self, because it has a beginning and an end, is subject to modifications, is characterised by pain and suffering and is an object; whereas the subject can never be identified with the objects of knowledge.

units.label: Verse 184
units.deva:
बुद्धिर्बुद्धीन्द्रियैः सार्धं सवृत्तिः कर्तृलक्षणः ।
विज्ञानमयकोशः स्यात्पुंसः संसारकारणम् ॥
units.iast:
buddhir buddhīndriyaiḥ sārdhaṃ savṛttiḥ kartṛ-lakṣaṇaḥ |
vijñānamaya-kośaḥ syāt puṃsaḥ saṃsāra-kāraṇam ||
units.translation: The intellect, together with the sense-organs of knowledge and its thought-modes, forms the vijñānamaya sheath, marked by the sense of doership and causing a person’s transmigration.
units.editionTranslation: The Buddhi with its modifications and the organs of knowledge, forms the Vijnanamaya Kosha or knowledge sheath, of the agent, having the characteristics which is the cause of man’s transmigration.

units.label: Verse 185
units.deva:
अनुव्रजच्चित्प्रतिबिम्बशक्तिः
विज्ञानसंज्ञः प्रकृतेर्विकारः ।
ज्ञानक्रियावानहमित्यजस्रं
देहेन्द्रियादिष्वभिमन्यते भृशम् ॥
units.iast:
anuvrajaccitpratibimbaśaktiḥ
vijñānasaṃjñaḥ prakṛter vikāraḥ |
jñānakriyāvān aham ity ajasraṃ
deha-indriyādiṣv abhimanyate bhṛśam ||
units.translation: Called vijñāna and accompanied by the reflecting power of consciousness, this sheath is a modification of prakṛti. With the functions of knowledge and action, it continually identifies the body, senses, and so on as “I.”
units.editionTranslation: This knowledge sheath, which seems to be followed by a reflection of the power of the Chit, is a modification of the Prakriti, is endowed with the function of knowledge, and always wholly identifies itself with the body, organs, etc.

units.label: Verses 186–187
units.deva:
अनादिकालोऽयमहंस्वभावो
जीवः समस्तव्यवहारवोढा ।
करोति कर्माण्य् अपि पूर्ववासनः
पुण्यान्यपुण्यानि च तत्फलानि ॥

भुङ्क्ते विचित्रास्व् अपि योनिषु व्रजन्
नायाति निर्यात्यध ऊर्ध्वमेषः ।
अस्यैव विज्ञानमयस्य जाग्रत्-
स्वप्नाद्यवस्थाः सुखदुःखभोगः ॥
units.iast:
anādikālo 'yam ahaṃsvabhāvo
jīvaḥ samastavyavahāravoḍhā |
karoti karmāṇy api pūrvavāsanaḥ
puṇyāny apuṇyāni ca tatphalāni ||

bhuṅkte vicitrāsv api yoniṣu vrajan
nāyāti niryāty adha ūrdhvam eṣaḥ |
asyaiva vijñānamayasya jāgrat-
svapnādyavasthāḥ sukhaduḥkhabhogaḥ ||
units.translation:
Beginningless and having the nature “I,” this jīva carries on every worldly transaction. Conditioned by prior tendencies, it performs meritorious and unmeritorious actions and experiences their results.

Moving through various wombs, it experiences those results and goes downward and upward, coming and going. The waking, dream, and other states, and experiences of pleasure and pain, belong to this very vijñānamaya sheath.
units.editionTranslation: It is without beginning, characterised by egoism, is called the Jiva, and carries on all the activities on the relative plane. Through previous desires it performs good and evil actions and experiences their results. Being born in various bodies, it comes and goes, up and down. It is this knowledge sheath that has the waking, dream and other states, and experiences joy and grief.

units.label: Verse 188
units.deva:
देहादिनिष्ठाश्रमधर्मकर्म-
गुणाभिमानः सततं ममेति ।
विज्ञानकोशोऽयमतिप्रकाशः
प्रकृष्टसान्निध्यवशात्परात्मनः ।
अतो भवत्येष उपाधिरस्य
यद् आत्मधीः संसरति भ्रमेण ॥
units.iast:
dehādiniṣṭhāśramadharmakarma-
guṇābhimānaḥ satataṃ mameti |
vijñānakośo 'yam atiprakāśaḥ
prakṛṣṭasānnidhyavaśāt parātmanaḥ |
ato bhavaty eṣa upādhir asya
yad ātmadhīḥ saṃsarati bhrameṇa ||
units.translation: This vijñāna sheath continually claims as “mine” the duties, actions, and qualities of the life-stages that belong to the body and the rest. It shines brightly because of its close proximity to the Supreme Self. It therefore becomes that Self’s limiting adjunct: through the deluded notion “I am this,” one transmigrates.
units.editionTranslation: It always mistakes the duties, functions and attributes of the orders of life which belong to the body, as its own. The knowledge sheath is exceedingly effulgent, owing to its close proximity to the Supreme Self, which identifying Itself with it suffers transmigration through delusion. It is therefore a superimposition on the Self.

units.label: Verse 189
units.deva:
योऽयं विज्ञानमयः प्राणेषु हृदि स्फुरत्ययं ज्योतिः ।
कूटस्थः सन्नात्मा कर्ता भोक्ता भवत्युपाधिस्थः ॥
units.iast:
yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu hṛdi sphuraty ayaṃ jyotiḥ |
kūṭasthaḥ sann ātmā kartā bhoktā bhavaty upādhisthaḥ ||
units.translation: This vijñānamaya sheath is where the self-luminous light shines in the heart, near the prāṇas. The changeless Self, when situated in this limiting adjunct, appears as doer and experiencer.
units.editionTranslation: The self-effulgent Atman, which is Pure Knowledge, shines in the midst of the Pranas, within the heart. Though immutable, It becomes the agent and experiencer owing to Its superimposition, the knowledge sheath.

units.label: Verse 190
units.deva:
स्वयं परिच्छेदमुपेत्य बुद्धेः
तादात्म्यदोषेण परं मृषात्मनः ।
सर्वात्मकः सन्न् अपि वीक्षते स्वयं
स्वतः पृथक्त्वेन मृदो घटान् इव ॥
units.iast:
svayaṃ paricchedam upetya buddheḥ
tādātmyadoṣeṇa paraṃ mṛṣātmanaḥ |
sarvātmakaḥ sann api vīkṣate svayaṃ
svataḥ pṛthaktvena mṛdo ghaṭān iva ||
units.translation: Assuming the intellect’s limitation and through the error of identifying with the false self, the Supreme Self, though it is the Self of all, sees itself as separate from itself, as pots appear separate from clay.
units.editionTranslation: Though the Self of everything that exists, this Atman, Itself assuming the limitations of the Buddhi and wrongly identifying Itself with this totally unreal entity, looks upon Itself as something different – like earthen jars from the clay of which they are made.

units.label: Verse 191
units.deva:
उपाधिसंबन्धवशात्परात्मा
ह्युपाधिधर्माननुभाति तद्गुणः ।
अयोविकारानविकारिवन्हिवत्
सदैकरूपोऽपि परः स्वभावात् ॥
units.iast:
upādhisaṃbandhavaśāt parātmā
hy upādhidharmān anubhāti tadguṇaḥ |
ayovikārān avikāri-vahnivat
sadaikarūpo 'pi paraḥ svabhāvāt ||
units.translation: Through its connection with a limiting adjunct, the Supreme Self seems to experience that adjunct’s properties, like changeless fire seeming to take on the changes of iron. Yet by nature the Supreme is always of one form.
units.editionTranslation: Owing to Its connection with the super-impositions, the Supreme Self, even thou naturally perfect (transcending Nature) and eternally unchanging, assumes the qualities of the superimpositions and appears to act just as they do – like the changeless fire assuming the modifications of the iron which it turns red-hot.

units.label: Verse 192
units.deva:
शिष्य उवाच
भ्रमेणाप्यन्यथा वास्तु जीवभावः परात्मनः ।
तदुपाधेरनादित्वान्नानादेर्नाश इष्यते ॥
units.iast:
śiṣya uvāca
bhrameṇāpy anyathā vāstu jīvabhāvaḥ parātmanaḥ |
tadupādher anāditvān nānāder nāśa iṣyate ||
units.translation: The disciple said: Let the Supreme Self’s state as a jīva come through delusion or otherwise. Since that limiting adjunct is beginningless, destruction of what is beginningless is not accepted.
units.editionTranslation: The disciple questioned: Be it through delusion or otherwise that the Supreme Self has come to consider Itself as the Jiva, this superimposition is without beginning, and that which has no beginning cannot be supposed to have an end either.

units.label: Verse 193
units.deva:
अतोऽस्य जीवभावोऽपि नित्या भवति संसृतिः ।
न निवर्तेत तन्मोक्षः कथं मे श्रीगुरो वद ॥
units.iast:
ato 'sya jīvabhāvo 'pi nityā bhavati saṃsṛtiḥ |
na nivarteta tanmokṣaḥ kathaṃ me śrīguro vada ||
units.translation: Therefore this state of being a jīva and transmigration would both be eternal and would not end. How could liberation come about, revered teacher? Tell me.
units.editionTranslation: Therefore the Jivahood of the soul also must have no end, and its transmigration must continue for ever. How then can there be Liberation for the soul ? Kindly enlighten me on this point, O revered Master.

units.label: Verse 194
units.deva:
श्रीगुरुरुवाच
सम्यक्पृष्टं त्वया विद्वन्सावधानेन तच्छृणु ।
प्रामाणिकी न भवति भ्रान्त्या मोहितकल्पना ॥
units.iast:
śrīgurur uvāca
samyak pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā vidvan sāvadhānena tac chṛṇu |
prāmāṇikī na bhavati bhrāntyā mohitakalpanā ||
units.translation: The teacher said: You have asked rightly, learned one; listen attentively. A notion produced by delusion is not valid knowledge.
units.editionTranslation: The Teacher said: Thou hast rightly questioned, O learned man ! Listen therefore attentively: The imagination which has been conjured up by delusion can never be accepted as a fact.

units.label: Verse 195
units.deva:
भ्रान्तिं विना त्वसङ्गस्य निष्क्रियस्य निराकृतेः ।
न घटेतार्थसंबन्धो नभसो नीलतादिवत् ॥
units.iast:
bhrāntiṃ vinā tv asaṅgasya niṣkriyasya nirākṛteḥ |
na ghaṭetārthasaṃbandho nabhaso nīlatādivat ||
units.translation: But without delusion, no relation to objects could occur for the unattached, actionless, formless Self, just as blueness and the like do not truly belong to the sky.
units.editionTranslation: But for delusion there can be no connection of the Self – which is unattached, beyond activity and formless – with the objective world, as in the case of blueness etc., with reference to the sky.

units.label: Verse 196
units.deva:
स्वस्य द्रष्टुर्निर्गुणस्याक्रियस्य
प्रत्यग्बोधानन्दरूपस्य बुद्धेः ।
भ्रान्त्या प्राप्तो जीवभावो न सत्यो
मोहापाये नास्त्य् अवस्तुस्वभावात् ॥
units.iast:
svasya draṣṭur nirguṇasyākriyasya
pratyagbodhānandarūpasya buddheḥ |
bhrāntyā prāpto jīvabhāvo na satyo
mohāpāye nāsty avastusvabhāvāt ||
units.translation: The jīva-state, attained through the intellect’s delusion, is not real for the Self—the witness, attributeless, actionless, and of the nature of inward awareness and bliss. When delusion disappears, that unreal state no longer exists.
units.editionTranslation: The Jivahood of the Atman, the Witness, which is beyond qualities and beyond activity, and which is realised within as Knowledge and Bliss Absolute – has been superimposed by the delusion of the Buddhi, and is not real. And because it is by nature an unreality, it ceases to exist when the delusion is gone.

units.label: Verse 197
units.deva:
यावद्भ्रान्तिस्तावदेवास्य सत्ता
मिथ्याज्ञानोज्जृम्भितस्य प्रमादात् ।
रज्ज्वां सर्पो भ्रान्तिकालीन एव
भ्रान्तेर्नाशे नैव सर्पोऽपि तद्वत् ॥
units.iast:
yāvad bhrāntis tāvad evāsya sattā
mithyājñānojjṛmbhitasya pramādāt |
rajjvāṃ sarpo bhrāntikālīna eva
bhrānter nāśe naiva sarpo 'pi tadvat ||
units.translation: This [jīva-state], produced by false knowing and carelessness, exists only while delusion lasts. A snake appears on a rope only during the mistake; when the mistake is destroyed, no snake remains. So it is here.
units.editionTranslation: It exists only so long as the delusion lasts, being caused by indiscrimination due to an illusion. The rope is supposed to be the snake only so long as the mistake lasts, and there is no more snake when the illusion has vanished. Similar is the case here.

units.label: Verses 198–199
units.deva:
अनादित्वमविद्यायाः कार्यस्यापि तथेष्यते ।
उत्पन्नायां तु विद्यायामाविद्यकमनाद्य् अपि ॥

प्रबोधे स्वप्नवत्सर्वं सहमूलं विनश्यति ।
अनाद्यपीदं नो नित्यं प्रागभाव इव स्फुटम् ॥
units.iast:
anāditvam avidyāyāḥ kāryasyāpi tatheṣyate |
utpannāyāṃ tu vidyāyām āvidyakam anādy api ||

prabodhe svapnavat sarvaṃ sahamūlaṃ vinaśyati |
anādy apīdaṃ no nityaṃ prāgabhāva iva sphuṭam ||
units.translation: The beginninglessness of ignorance and of its effect is accepted. But when knowledge arises, even the beginningless product of ignorance perishes with its root, like everything in a dream upon waking. Clearly, this [world], though beginningless, is not eternal, like prior non-existence.
units.editionTranslation: Avidya or Nescience and its effects are likewise considered as beginningless. But with the rise of Vidya or realisation, the entire effects of Avidya, even though beginningless, are destroyed together with their root – like dreams on waking up from sleep. It is clear that the phenomenal universe, even though without beginning, is not eternal – like previous non-existence.

units.label: Verses 200–201
units.deva:
अनादेर् अपि विध्वंसः प्रागभावस्य वीक्षितः ।
यद्बुद्ध्युपाधिसंबन्धात्परिकल्पितम् आत्मनि ॥

जीवत्वं न ततोऽन्यस्तु स्वरूपेण विलक्षणः ।
संबन्धस्त्व् आत्मनो बुद्ध्या मिथ्याज्ञानपुरःसरः ॥
units.iast:
anāder api vidhvaṃsaḥ prāgabhāvasya vīkṣitaḥ |
yad buddhyupādhisaṃbandhāt parikalpitam ātmani ||

jīvatvaṃ na tato 'nyas tu svarūpeṇa vilakṣaṇaḥ |
saṃbandhas tv ātmano buddhyā mithyājñānapuraḥsaraḥ ||
units.translation: Even beginningless prior non-existence is observed to end. So jīva-hood, imagined in the Self through connection with the intellect as a limiting adjunct, is not real; the Self is distinct from it in essence. The relation between the Self and intellect is preceded by false knowledge.
units.editionTranslation: Previous non-existence, even though beginningless, is observed to have an end. So the Jivahood which is imagined to be in the Atman through its relation with superimposed attributes such as the Buddhi, is not real; whereas the other (the Atman) is essentially different from it. The relation between the Atman and the Buddhi is due to a false knowledge.

units.label: Verse 202
units.deva:
विनिवृत्तिर्भवेत्तस्य सम्यग्ज्ञानेन नान्यथा ।
ब्रह्मात्मैकत्वविज्ञानं सम्यग्ज्ञानं श्रुतेर्मतम् ॥
units.iast:
vinivṛttirbhavettasya samyagjñānena nānyathā |
brahmātmaikatvavijñānaṃ samyagjñānaṃ śrutermatam ||
units.translation: Its cessation comes through right knowledge, not otherwise. Knowledge of the oneness of Brahman and the Self is held by scripture to be right knowledge.
units.editionTranslation: The cessation of that superimposition takes place through perfect knowledge, and by no other means. Perfect knowledge, according to the Shrutis, consists in the realisation of the identity of the individual soul and Brahman.

units.label: Verse 203
units.deva:
तदात्मानात्मनोः सम्यग्विवेकेनैव सिध्यति ।
ततो विवेकः कर्तव्यः प्रत्यगात्मसदात्मनोः ॥
units.iast:
tadātmānātmanoḥ samyagvivekenaiva sidhyati |
tato vivekaḥ kartavyaḥ pratyagātmasadātmanoḥ ||
units.translation: That is attained only through clear discrimination between the Self and the non-Self. Therefore one must discriminate between the inward individual Self and the real Self.

gloss.en: between the real Self and [the inward Self]

units.editionTranslation: This realisation is attained by a perfect discrimination between the Self and the non-Self. Therefore one must strive for the discrimination between the individual soul and the eternal Self.

units.label: Verse 204
units.deva:
जलं पङ्कवदत्यन्तं पङ्कापाये जलं स्फुटम् ।
यथा भाति तथात्मापि दोषाभावे स्फुटप्रभः ॥
units.iast:
jalaṃ paṅkavadatyantaṃ paṅkāpāye jalaṃ sphuṭam |
yathā bhāti tathātmāpi doṣābhāve sphuṭaprabhaḥ ||
units.translation: Just as very muddy water appears clear when the mud is removed, so too the Self shines brightly when its defects are absent.
units.editionTranslation: Just as the water which is very muddy again appears as transparent water when the mud is removed, so the Atman also manifests Its undimmed lustre when the taint has been removed.

units.label: Verse 205
units.deva:
असन्निवृत्तौ तु सदात्मना स्फुटं
प्रतीतिरेतस्य भवेत्प्रतीचः ।
ततो निरासः करणीय एव
सदात्मनः साध्वहमादिवस्तुनः ॥
units.iast:
asannivṛttau tu sadātmanā sphuṭaṃ
pratītiretasya bhavetpratīcaḥ |
tato nirāsaḥ karaṇīya eva
sadātmanaḥ sādhvahamādivastunaḥ ||
units.translation: When the unreal has ceased, the inward Self is clearly recognized as the real Self. Therefore one must indeed thoroughly remove from the real Self things beginning with the ego, the sense of “I.”
units.editionTranslation: When the unreal ceases to exist, this very individual soul is definitely realised as the eternal Self. Therefore one must make it a point completely to remove things like egoism from the eternal Self.

units.label: Verse 206
units.deva:
अतो नायं परात्मा स्याद्विज्ञानमयशब्दभाक् ।
विकारित्वाज्जडत्वाच्च परिच्छिन्नत्वहेतुतः ।
दृश्यत्वाद्व्यभिचारित्वान्नानित्यो नित्य इष्यते ॥
units.iast:
ato nāyaṃ parātmā syādvijñānamayaśabdabhāk |
vikāritvājjaḍatvācca paricchinnatvahetutaḥ |
dṛśyatvādvyabhicāritvānnānityo nitya iṣyate ||
units.translation: Therefore, what is called the “knowledge-made” sheath cannot be the Supreme Self: it changes, is inert, limited, perceptible, and inconstant. What is non-eternal is not accepted as eternal.
units.editionTranslation: This knowledge sheath (Vijnanamaya Kosha) that we have been speaking of, cannot be the Supreme Self for the following reasons - because it is subject to change, is insentient, is a limited thing, an object of the senses, and is not constantly present: An unreal thing cannot indeed be taken for the real Atman.

units.label: Verse 207
units.deva:
आनन्दप्रतिबिम्बचुम्बिततनुर्वृत्तिस्तमोजृम्भिता
स्यादानन्दमयः प्रियादिगुणकः स्वेष्टार्थलाभोदयः ।
पुण्यस्यानुभवे विभाति कृतिनामानन्दरूपः स्वयं
सर्वो नन्दति यत्र साधु तनुभृन्मात्रः प्रयत्नं विना ॥
units.iast:
ānanda-pratibimba-cumbita-tanur vṛttis tamo-jṛmbhitā
syād ānanda-mayaḥ priyādi-guṇakaḥ sveṣṭārtha-lābhodayaḥ |
puṇyasyānubhave vibhāti kṛtinām ānanda-rūpaḥ svayaṃ
sarvo nandati yatra sādhu tanubhṛn-mātraḥ prayatnaṃ vinā ||
units.translation: The blissful sheath is a mental modification brought forth by ignorance, its form touched by a reflection of bliss. It has pleasure and the like as qualities, and arises when one gains a desired object. It shines for the fortunate in the experience of merit, itself blissful; there every embodied being rejoices easily, without effort.

gloss.en: whose form is touched by a reflection of bliss
having pleasure and the like as qualities
arising when one's desired object is gained

units.editionTranslation: The blissful sheath (Anandamaya Kosha) is that modification of Nescience which manifests itself catching a reflection of the Atman which is Bliss Absolute; whose attributes are pleasure and the rest; and which appears in view when some object agreeable to oneself presents itself. It makes itself spontaneously felt by the fortunate during the fruition of their virtuous deeds; from which every corporeal being derives great joy without the least effort.

units.label: Verse 208
units.deva:
आनन्दमयकोशस्य सुषुप्तौ स्फूर्तिरुत्कटा ।
स्वप्नजागरयोरीषदिष्टसंदर्शनादिना ॥
units.iast:
ānandamayakośasya suṣuptau sphūrtir utkaṭā |
svapnajāgarayor īṣad iṣṭasaṃdarśanādinā ||
units.translation: The blissful sheath manifests intensely in deep sleep. In dream and waking it manifests only slightly, through seeing desired objects and the like.

gloss.en: through seeing desired things and the like

units.editionTranslation: The blissful sheath has its fullest play during profound sleep, while in the dreaming and wakeful states it has only a partial manifestation, occasioned by the sight of agreeable objects and so forth.

units.label: Verse 209
units.deva:
नैवायमानन्दमयः परात्मा
सोपाधिकत्वात्प्रकृतेर्विकारात् ।
कार्यत्वहेतोः सुकृतक्रियाया
विकारसङ्घातसमाहितत्वात् ॥
units.iast:
naivāyam ānandamayaḥ parātmā
sopādhikatvāt prakṛter vikārāt |
kāryatvahetoḥ sukṛtakriyāyā
vikārasaṅghātasamāhitatvāt ||
units.translation: This blissful sheath is not the Supreme Self, because it has limiting conditions, is a modification of primordial nature, is an effect of meritorious action, and is contained within an aggregate of changing things.

gloss.en: because it is contained within an aggregate of changing things

units.editionTranslation: Nor is the blissful sheath the Supreme Self, because it is endowed with the changeful attributes, is a modification of the Prakriti, is the effect of past good deeds, and imbedded in the other sheaths which are modifications.

units.label: Verse 210
units.deva:
पञ्चानाम् अपि कोशानां निषेधे युक्तितः श्रुतेः ।
तन्निषेधावधि साक्षी बोधरूपोऽवशिष्यते ॥
units.iast:
pañcānām api kośānāṃ niṣedhe yuktitaḥ śruteḥ |
tanniṣedhāvadhi sākṣī bodharūpo 'vaśiṣyate ||
units.translation: When all five sheaths are negated through reasoning grounded in scripture, what remains at the end of their negation is the witness, whose nature is awareness.

gloss.en: at the end of their negation

units.editionTranslation: When all the five sheaths have been eliminated by the reasoning on Shruti passages, what remains as the culminating point of the process, is the Witness, the Knowledge Absolute – the Atman.

units.label: Verse 211
units.deva:
योऽयमात्मा स्वयंज्योतिः पञ्चकोशविलक्षणः ।
अवस्थात्रयसाक्षी सन्निर्विकारो निरञ्जनः

सदानन्दः स विज्ञेयः स्वात्मत्वेन विपश्चिता ॥
units.iast:
yo 'yam ātmā svayaṃjyotiḥ pañcakośavilakṣaṇaḥ |
avasthātrayasākṣī san nirvikāro nirañjanaḥ
sadānandaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ svātmatvena vipaścitā ||
units.translation: The wise person should know this Self—self-luminous, distinct from the five sheaths, witness of the three states, changeless, unstained, and ever-blissful—as their own Self.
units.editionTranslation: This self-effulgent Atman which is distinct from the five sheaths, the Witness of the three states, the Real, the Changeless, the Untainted, the everlasting Bliss – is to be realised by the wise man as his own Self.

units.label: Verse 212
units.deva:
शिष्य उवाच
मिथ्यात्वेन निषिद्धेषु कोशेष्वेतेषु पञ्चसु ।
सर्वाभावं विना किंचिन् न पश्याम्यत्र हे गुरो ।
विज्ञेयं किमु वस्त्वस्ति स्वात्मनात्मविपश्चिता ॥
units.iast:
śiṣya uvāca
mithyātvena niṣiddheṣu kośeṣv eteṣu pañcasu |
sarvābhāvaṃ vinā kiṃcin na paśyāmy atra he guro |
vijñeyaṃ kim u vastv asti svātmanātmavipaścitā ||
units.translation: When these five sheaths have been rejected as unreal, I see nothing here, O teacher, except total absence. What reality is there for the wise knower of the Self to realize as their own Self?

gloss.en: by the wise knower of the Self

units.editionTranslation: The disciple questioned: After these five sheaths have been eliminated as unreal, I find nothing, O Master, in this universe but a Void, the absence of everything. What entity is there left forsooth with which the wise knower of the Self should realise his identity.

units.label: Verses 213–214
units.deva:
श्रीगुरुरुवाच
सत्यमुक्तं त्वया विदन्निपुणोऽसि विचारणे ।
अहमादिविकारास्ते तदभावोऽयमप्यनु ॥

सर्वे येनानुभूयन्ते यः स्वयं नानुभूयते ।
तमात्मानं वेदितारं विद्धि बुद्ध्या सुसूक्ष्मया ॥
units.iast:
śrīgurur uvāca
satyam uktaṃ tvayā vidan nipuṇo 'si vicāraṇe |
ahamādi-vikārās te tad-abhāvo 'yam apy anu ||
sarve yenānubhūyante yaḥ svayaṃ nānubhūyate |
tam ātmānaṃ veditāraṃ viddhi buddhyā susūkṣmayā ||
units.translation:
The teacher said: You have spoken truly; you are skilled in inquiry. The changes beginning with ego, and their absence too, are perceived.

That by which all things are experienced, but which itself is not experienced—know that Self, the knower, through a very subtle intellect.
units.editionTranslation: The Guru answered: Thou has rightly said, O learned man ! Thou art clever indeed in discrimination. That by which all those modifications such as egoism as well as their subsequent absence (during deep sleep) are perceived, but which Itself is not perceived, know thou that Atman – the Knower – through the sharpest intellect.
