units.label: Verse 215
units.deva:
तत्साक्षिकं भवेत्तत्तद्यद्यद्येनानुभूयते ।
कस्याप्यननुभूतार्थे साक्षित्वं नोपयुज्यते ॥
units.iast:
tat-sākṣikaṃ bhavet tat-tad yad-yad yenānubhūyate |
kasyāpy ananubhūtārthe sākṣitvaṃ nopayujyate ||
units.translation: Whatever is experienced by a knower has that knower as its witness. No one can be a witness to an object that has not been experienced.

gloss.en: with regard to an unexperienced object

units.editionTranslation: That which is perceived by something else has for its witness the latter. When there is no agent to perceive a thing, we cannot speak of it as having been perceived at all.

units.label: Verse 216
units.deva:
असौ स्वसाक्षिको भावो यतः स्वेनानुभूयते ।
अतः परं स्वयं साक्षात्प्रत्यगात्मा न चेतरः ॥
units.iast:
asau svasākṣiko bhāvo yataḥ svenānubhūyate |
ataḥ paraṃ svayaṃ sākṣāt pratyagātmā na caitaraḥ ||
units.translation: Since this self-witnessed reality is experienced by itself, the inward Self itself is directly the Supreme, and not anything else.
units.editionTranslation: This Atman is a self-cognised entity because It is cognised by Itself. Hence the individual soul is itself and directly the Supreme Brahman, and nothing else.

units.label: Verse 217
units.deva:
जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तिषु स्फुटतरं योऽसौ समुज्जृम्भते
प्रत्यग्रूपतया सदाहमहमित्यन्तः स्फुरन्नैकधा ।
नानाकारविकारभागिन इमान् पश्यन्नहंधीमुखान्
नित्यानन्दचिदात्मना स्फुरति तं विद्धि स्वमेतं हृदि ॥
units.iast:
jāgratsvapnasuṣuptiṣu sphuṭataraṃ yo 'sau samujjṛmbhate
pratyagrūpatayā sadāhamaham ity antaḥ sphuran naikadhā |
nānākāravikārabhāgina imān paśyan ahaṃdhīmukhān
nityānandacidātmanā sphurati taṃ viddhi svam etaṃ hṛdi ||
units.translation: Know in your heart as your own Self that which manifests most clearly in waking, dream, and deep sleep; shines always within as “I, I” in many ways; sees these diverse changing forms beginning with the ego-thought; and shines as the Self of eternal bliss and consciousness.

gloss.en: sharing in diverse forms and changes
as the Self of eternal bliss and consciousness

units.editionTranslation: That which clearly manifests Itself in the states of wakefulness, dream and profound sleep; which is inwardly perceived in the mind in various forms as an unbroken series of egoistic impressions; which witnesses the egoism, the Buddhi, etc., which are of diverse forms and modifications; and which makes Itself felt as the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute; know thou this Atman, thy own Self, within thy heart.

units.label: Verse 218
units.deva:
घटोदके बिम्बितमर्कबिम्बम्
आलोक्य मूढो रविम् एव मन्यते ।
तथा चिदाभासमुपाधिसंस्थं
भ्रान्त्याहम् इत्य् एव जडोऽभिमन्यते ॥
units.iast:
ghaṭodake bimbitam arkabimbam
ālokya mūḍho ravim eva manyate |
tathā cidābhāsam upādhisaṃsthaṃ
bhrāntyāham ity eva jaḍo 'bhimanyate ||
units.translation: Seeing the sun’s reflection in the water of a jar, the fool thinks it is the sun itself. Likewise, through delusion, the dull-minded person identifies the reflection of consciousness situated in a limiting adjunct as “I.”

gloss.en: in the water of a jar

units.editionTranslation: Seeing the reflection of the sun mirrored in the water of a jar, the fool thinks it is the sun itself. Similarly the stupid man, through delusion, identifies himself with the reflection of the Chit caught in the Buddhi, which is Its superimposition.

units.label: Verse 219
units.deva:
घटं जलं तद्गतमर्कबिम्बं
विहाय सर्वं विनिरीक्ष्यतेऽर्कः ।
तटस्थ एतत्त्रितयावभासकः
स्वयंप्रकाशो विदुषा यथा तथा ॥
units.iast:
ghaṭaṃ jalaṃ tadgatam arkabimbaṃ
vihāya sarvaṃ vinirīkṣyate 'rkaḥ |
taṭastha etat-tritayāvabhāsakaḥ
svayaṃprakāśo viduṣā yathā tathā ||
units.translation: Just as the wise person sets aside the jar, the water, and the sun’s reflection in it, and sees the sun itself—standing apart, illuminating those three, and self-luminous—
units.editionTranslation: Just as the wise man leaves aside the jar, the water and the reflection of the sun in it, and sees the self-luminous sun which illumines these three and is independent of them;

units.label: Verses 220–222
units.deva:
देहं धियं चित्प्रतिबिम्बम् एवं
विसृज्य बुद्धौ निहितं गुहायाम् ।
द्रष्टारमात्मानमखण्डबोधं
सर्वप्रकाशं सदसद्विलक्षणम् ॥

नित्यं विभुं सर्वगतं सुसूक्ष्मं
अन्तर्बहिःशून्यमनन्यम् आत्मनः ।
विज्ञाय सम्यङ्निजरूपमेतत्
पुमान् विपाप्मा विरजो विमृत्युः ॥

विशोक आनन्दघनो विपश्चित्
स्वयं कुतश्चिन् न बिभेति कश्चित् ।
नान्योऽस्ति पन्था भवबन्धमुक्तेः
विना स्वतत्त्वावगमं मुमुक्षोः ॥
units.iast:
dehaṃ dhiyaṃ citpratibimbam evaṃ
visṛjya buddhau nihitaṃ guhāyām |
draṣṭāram ātmānam akhaṇḍabodhaṃ
sarvaprakāśaṃ sadasadvilakṣaṇam ||
nityaṃ vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ susūkṣmaṃ
antarbahiḥśūnyam ananyam ātmanaḥ |
vijñāya samyaṅ nijarūpam etat
pumān vipāpmā virajo vimṛtyuḥ ||
viśoka ānandaghano vipaścit
svayaṃ kutaścin na bibheti kaścit |
nānyo 'sti panthā bhavabandhamukteḥ
vinā svatattvāvagamaṃ mumukṣoḥ ||
units.translation:
So, leaving aside the body, the intellect, and the reflection of consciousness, one should know the Witness, the Self: undivided awareness, illuminating all, distinct from what exists and what does not, and hidden in the cave of the intellect.

Knowing fully this true nature as one's own—the eternal, all-pervading, very subtle, without inside or outside, and not other than oneself—a person becomes sinless, stainless, and free from death and sorrow, a wise embodiment of bliss. Such a person fears nothing. For one seeking liberation, there is no path out of the bondage of worldly existence except realizing one's own true nature.

gloss.en: distinct from what exists and what does not
realization of one's own true nature

units.editionTranslation: Similarly, discarding the body, the Buddhi and the reflection of the Chit in it, and realising the Witness, the Self, the Knowledge Absolute, the cause of the manifestation of everything, which is hidden in the recesses of the Buddhi, is distinct from the gross and subtle, eternal, omnipresent, all-pervading and extremely subtle, and which has neither interior nor exterior and is identical with one self – fully realising this true nature of oneself, one becomes free from sin, taint, death and grief, and becomes the embodiment of Bliss. Illumined himself, he is afraid of none. For a seeker after Liberation there is no other way to the breaking of the bonds of transmigration than the realisation of the truth of one’s own Self.

units.label: Verse 223
units.deva:
ब्रह्माभिन्नत्वविज्ञानं भवमोक्षस्य कारणम् ।
येनाद्वितीयमानन्दं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते बुधैः ॥
units.iast:
brahmābhinnatva-vijñānaṃ bhava-mokṣasya kāraṇam |
yena advitīyam ānandaṃ brahma sampadyate budhaiḥ ||
units.translation: Knowing oneself to be non-different from Brahman is the cause of release from worldly existence. Through this, the wise attain Brahman, nondual bliss.

gloss.en: knowledge that one is non-different from Brahman

units.editionTranslation: The realisation of one’s identity with Brahman is the cause of Liberation from the bonds of Samsara, by means of which the wise man attains Brahman, the One without a second, the Bliss Absolute.

units.label: Verse 224
units.deva:
ब्रह्मभूतस्तु संसृत्यै विद्वान्नावर्तते पुनः ।
विज्ञातव्यमतः सम्यग्ब्रह्माभिन्नत्वम् आत्मनः ॥
units.iast:
brahmabhūtas tu saṃsṛtyai vidvān nāvartate punaḥ |
vijñātavyam ataḥ samyak brahmābhinnatvam ātmanaḥ ||
units.translation: The wise person who has become Brahman does not return again to transmigration. Therefore the Self’s non-difference from Brahman must be fully known.
units.editionTranslation: Once having realised Brahman, one no longer returns to the realm of transmigration. Therefore one must fully realise one’s identity with Brahman.

units.label: Verse 225
units.deva:
सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तं ब्रह्म विशुद्धं परं स्वतःसिद्धम् ।
नित्यानन्दैकरसं प्रत्यगभिन्नं निरन्तरं जयति ॥
units.iast:
satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma viśuddhaṃ paraṃ svataḥsiddham |
nityānandaikarasaṃ pratyagabhinnaṃ nirantaraṃ jayati ||
units.translation: Brahman is truth, knowledge, and infinite; pure, supreme, and self-established; of the single essence of eternal bliss; not different from the inward Self; and shining without interruption.

gloss.en: having the single essence of eternal bliss
not different from the inward Self

units.editionTranslation: Brahman is Existence, Knowledge, Infinity, pure, supreme, self-existent, eternal and indivisible Bliss, not different (in reality) from the individual soul, and devoid of interior or exterior. It is (ever) triumphant.

units.label: Verse 226
units.deva:
सदिदं परमाद्वैतं स्वस्मादन्यस्य वस्तुनोऽभावात् ।
न ह्यन्यदस्ति किंचित् सम्यक् परमार्थतत्त्वबोधदशायाम् ॥
units.iast:
sad idaṃ paramādvaitaṃ svasmād anyasya vastuno 'bhāvāt |
na hy anyad asti kiṃcit samyak paramārthatattvabodhadaśāyām ||
units.translation: This is the real, supreme nonduality, because no entity exists apart from the Self. Indeed, in the clear knowledge of ultimate reality, nothing else exists.

gloss.en: in the state of knowing ultimate reality

units.editionTranslation: It is this Supreme Oneness which alone is real, since there is nothing else but the Self. Verily, there remains no other independent entity in the state of realisation of the highest Truth.

units.label: Verse 227
units.deva:
यदिदं सकलं विश्वं नानारूपं प्रतीतमज्ञानात् ।
तत्सर्वं ब्रह्मैव प्रत्यस्ताशेषभावनादोषम् ॥
units.iast:
yad idaṃ sakalaṃ viśvaṃ nānārūpaṃ pratītam ajñānāt |
tat sarvaṃ brahmaiva pratyastāśeṣabhāvanādoṣam ||
units.translation: This entire universe, perceived through ignorance as having many forms, is all Brahman alone, free from every defect of imagined distinctions.
units.editionTranslation: All this universe which through ignorance appears as of diverse forms, is nothing else but Brahman which is absolutely free from all the limitations of human thought.

units.label: Verse 228
units.deva:
मृत्कार्यभूतोऽपि मृदो न भिन्नः
कुम्भोऽस्ति सर्वत्र तु मृत्स्वरूपात् ।
न कुम्भरूपं पृथगस्ति कुम्भः
कुतो मृषा कल्पितनाममात्रः ॥
units.iast:
mṛtkāryabhūto 'pi mṛdo na bhinnaḥ
kumbho 'sti sarvatra tu mṛtsvarūpāt |
na kumbharūpaṃ pṛthag asti kumbhaḥ
kuto mṛṣā kalpitanāmamātraḥ ||
units.translation: A pot, though produced as an effect of clay, is not different from clay; everywhere, its nature is clay. No pot-form exists apart from clay. How, then, is there a pot? It is false, merely an imagined name.
units.editionTranslation: A jar, though a modification of clay, is not different from it; everywhere the jar is essentially the same as the clay. Why then call it a jar ? It is fictitious, a fancied name merely.

units.label: Verse 229
units.deva:
केनापि मृद्भिन्नतया स्वरूपं
घटस्य संदर्शयितुं न शक्यते ।
अतो घटः कल्पित एव मोहान्
मृद् एव सत्यं परमार्थभूतम् ॥
units.iast:
kenāpi mṛdbhinnatayā svarūpaṃ
ghaṭasya saṃdarśayituṃ na śakyate |
ato ghaṭaḥ kalpita eva mohān
mṛd eva satyaṃ paramārthabhūtam ||
units.translation: No one can show that a pot’s essential nature is different from clay. Therefore the pot is indeed imagined through delusion; clay alone is real, the ultimate reality.
units.editionTranslation: None can demonstrate that the essence of a jar is something other than the clay (of which it is made). Hence the jar is merely imagined (as separate) through delusion, and the component clay alone is the abiding reality in respect of it.

units.label: Verse 230
units.deva:
सद्ब्रह्मकार्यं सकलं सदेवं
तन्मात्रमेतन् न ततोऽन्यदस्ति ।
अस्तीति यो वक्ति न तस्य मोहो
विनिर्गतो निद्रितवत्प्रजल्पः ॥
units.iast:
sadbrahmakāryaṃ sakalaṃ sa-devaṃ
tanmātram etan na tato 'nyad asti |
astīti yo vakti na tasya moho
vinirgato nidritavat prajalpaḥ ||
units.translation: The whole universe, including the gods, is an effect of real Brahman and is only That; nothing else exists apart from That. Whoever says “it exists” as a separate thing has not escaped delusion; that is babbling like someone asleep.
units.editionTranslation: Similarly, the whole universe, being the effect of the real Brahman, is in reality nothing but Brahman. Its essence is That, and it does not exist apart from It. He who says it does is still under delusion – he babbles like one asleep.

units.label: Verse 231
units.deva:
ब्रह्मैवेदं विश्वम् इत्य् एव वाणी
श्रौती ब्रूतेऽथर्वनिष्ठा वरिष्ठा ।
तस्मादेतद्ब्रह्ममात्रं हि विश्वं
नाधिष्ठानाद्भिन्नतारोपितस्य ॥
units.iast:
brahmaivedaṃ viśvam ity eva vāṇī
śrautī brūte 'tharvaniṣṭhā variṣṭhā |
tasmād etad brahmamātraṃ hi viśvaṃ
nādhiṣṭhānād bhinnatāropitasya ||
units.translation: The highest scriptural utterance, grounded in the Atharva Veda, declares: “This universe is Brahman alone.” Therefore this universe is nothing but Brahman, for what is superimposed is not separate from its substratum.
units.editionTranslation: This universe is verily Brahman – such is the august pronouncement of the Atharva Veda. Therefore this universe is nothing but Brahman, for that which is superimposed (on something) has no separate existence from its substratum.

units.label: Verse 232
units.deva:
सत्यं यदि स्याज्जगदेतदात्मनोऽनन्तत्वहानिर्निगमाप्रमाणता ।
असत्यवादित्वमपीशितुः स्यान्
नैतत्त्रयं साधु हितं महात्मनाम् ॥
units.iast:
satyaṃ yadi syāj jagad etad ātmano 'nantatva-hānir nigamāpramāṇatā |
asatyavāditvam apīśituḥ syān
naitat trayaṃ sādhu hitaṃ mahātmanām ||
units.translation: If this universe were real as it appears, the Self would lose its infinitude, scripture would lose its authority, and the Lord too would be speaking falsely. These three are neither right nor beneficial for the great-souled.
units.editionTranslation: If the universe, as it is, be real, there would be no cessation of the dualistic element, the scriptures would be falsified, and the Lord Himself would be guilty of an untruth. None of these three is considered either desirable or wholesome by the noble-minded.

units.label: Verse 233
units.deva:
ईश्वरो वस्तुतत्त्वज्ञो न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः ।
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानीत्येवमेव व्यचीकॢपत् ॥
units.iast:
īśvaro vastutattvajño na cāhaṃ teṣv avasthitaḥ |
na ca matsthāni bhūtānīty evam eva vyacīkḷpat ||
units.translation: The Lord, knower of the nature of reality, explained just this: “And I am not situated in them, nor are beings situated in Me.”

gloss.en: knower of the nature of reality

units.editionTranslation: The Lord, who knows the secret of all things has supported this view in the words: "But I am not in them" … "nor are the beings in Me".

units.label: Verse 234
units.deva:
यदि सत्यं भवेद्विश्वं सुषुप्तावुपलभ्यताम् ।
यन्नोपलभ्यते किञ्चिदतोऽसत्स्वप्नवन्मृषा ॥
units.iast:
yadi satyaṃ bhaved viśvaṃ suṣuptāv upalabhyatām |
yan nopalabhyate kiñcid ato 'sat svapnavan mṛṣā ||
units.translation: If the universe were real, it should be perceived in deep sleep. Since nothing at all is perceived there, it is therefore unreal—false like a dream.

gloss.en: let it be perceived; it should be perceived

units.editionTranslation: If the universe be true, let it then be perceived in the state of deep sleep also. As it is not at all perceived, it must be unreal and false, like dreams.

units.label: Verse 235
units.deva:
अतः पृथङ्नास्ति जगत्परात्मनः
पृथक्प्रतीतिस्तु मृषा गुणादिवत् ।
आरोपितस्यास्ति किमर्थवत्ता-
धिष्ठानमाभाति तथा भ्रमेण ॥
units.iast:
ataḥ pṛthaṅ nāsti jagat parātmanaḥ
pṛthakpratītis tu mṛṣā guṇādivat |
āropitasyāsti kimarthavattā-
dhiṣṭhānam ābhāti tathā bhrameṇa ||
units.translation: Therefore the universe does not exist apart from the Supreme Self. Its appearance as separate is false, like the sky’s apparent qualities such as blueness. What reality does a superimposed thing possess? The substratum itself appears that way through delusion.
units.editionTranslation: Therefore the universe does not exist apart from the Supreme Self; and the perception of its separateness is false like the qualities (of blueness etc., in the sky). Has a superimposed attribute any meaning apart from its substratum ? It is the substratum which appears like that through delusion.

units.label: Verse 236
units.deva:
भ्रान्तस्य यद्यद्भ्रमतः प्रतीतं
ब्रह्मैव तत्तद्रजतं हि शुक्तिः ।
इदंतया ब्रह्म सदैव रूप्यते
त्वारोपितं ब्रह्मणि नाममात्रम् ॥
units.iast:
bhrāntasya yad yad bhramataḥ pratītaṃ
brahmaiva tad tad rajataṃ hi śuktiḥ |
idaṃtayā brahma sadaiva rūpyate
tv āropitaṃ brahmaṇi nāmamātram ||
units.translation: Whatever a deluded person perceives while deluded is Brahman alone; what appears as silver is indeed the shell. Brahman is always presented as “this”; what is superimposed upon Brahman is merely a name.
units.editionTranslation: Whatever a deluded man perceives through mistake, is Brahman and Brahman alone: The silver is nothing but the mother-of-pearl. It is Brahman which is always considered as this universe, whereas that which is superimposed on the Brahman, viz. the universe, is merely a name.

units.label: Verses 237–238
units.deva:
अतः परं ब्रह्म सदद्वितीयं
विशुद्धविज्ञानघनं निरञ्जनम् ।
प्रशान्तमाद्यन्तविहीनमक्रियं
निरन्तरानन्दरसस्वरूपम् ॥

निरस्तमायाकृतसर्वभेदं
नित्यं सुखं निष्कलमप्रमेयम् ।
अरूपमव्यक्तमनाख्यमव्ययं
ज्योतिः स्वयं किञ्चिदिदं चकास्ति ॥
units.iast:
ataḥ paraṃ brahma sadadvitīyaṃ
viśuddhavijñānaghanaṃ nirañjanam |
praśāntamādyantavihīnamakriyaṃ
nirantarānandarasasvarūpam ||

nirastamāyākṛtasarvabhedaṃ
nityaṃ sukhaṃ niṣkalamaprameyam |
arūpamavyaktamanākhyamavyayaṃ
jyotiḥ svayaṃ kiñcid idaṃ cakāsti ||
units.translation: Therefore the supreme Brahman—real and nondual, a mass of pure consciousness, stainless, utterly peaceful, without beginning or end, actionless, and of the nature of uninterrupted bliss; free from every distinction created by Māyā, eternal happiness, partless, immeasurable, formless, unmanifest, nameless, and imperishable—is this self-luminous something that shines by itself.
units.editionTranslation: Hence whatever is manifested, viz. this universe, is the Supreme Brahman Itself, the Real, the One without a second, pure, the Essence of Knowledge, taintless, serene, devoid of beginning and end, beyond activity, the Essence of Bliss Absolute – transcending all the diversities created by Maya or Nescience, eternal, ever beyond the reach of pain, indivisible, immeasurable, formless, undifferentiated, nameless, immutable, self-luminous.

units.label: Verse 239
units.deva:
ज्ञातृज्ञेयज्ञानशून्यमनन्तं निर्विकल्पकम् ।
केवलाखण्डचिन्मात्रं परं तत्त्वं विदुर्बुधाः ॥
units.iast:
jñātṛjñeyajñānaśūnyam anantaṃ nirvikalpakam |
kevalākhaṇḍacinmātraṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ vidur budhāḥ ||
units.translation: The wise know the supreme reality as infinite and free from the knower, the known, and knowing; without distinctions, and nothing but pure, undivided consciousness.

gloss.en: the known; what can be known

units.editionTranslation: Sages realise the Supreme Truth, Brahman, in which there is no differentiation of knower, knowledge and known, which is infinite, transcendent, and the Essence of Knowledge Absolute.

units.label: Verse 240
units.deva:
अहेयमनुपादेयं मनोवाचामगोचरम् ।
अप्रमेयमनाद्यन्तं ब्रह्म पूर्णमहं महः ॥
units.iast:
aheyam anupādeyaṃ manovācām agocaram |
aprameyam anādyantaṃ brahma pūrṇam ahaṃ mahaḥ ||
units.translation: I am the complete Brahman, the great Light—impossible to reject or grasp, beyond mind and speech, immeasurable, and without beginning or end.

gloss.en: impossible to reject; not to be abandoned
impossible to grasp; not to be taken up

units.editionTranslation: Which can be neither thrown away nor taken up, which is beyond the reach of mind and speech, immeasurable, without beginning and end, the Whole, one’s very Self, and of surpassing glory.

units.label: Verses 241–242
units.deva:
तत्त्वंपदाभ्यामभिधीयमानयोः
ब्रह्मात्मनोः शोधितयोर्यदीत्थम् ।
श्रुत्या तयोस्तत्त्वमसीति सम्यग्
एकत्वम् एव प्रतिपाद्यते मुहुः ॥

ऐक्यं तयोर्लक्षितयोर्न वाच्ययोः
निगद्यतेऽन्योन्यविरुद्धधर्मिणोः ।
खद्योतभान्वोरिव राजभृत्ययोः
कूपाम्बुराश्योः परमाणुमेर्वोः ॥
units.iast:
tattvaṃpadābhyām abhidhīyamānayoḥ
brahmātmanoḥ śodhitayor yad ittham |
śrutyā tayoḥ tat tvam asīti samyag
ekatvam eva pratipādyate muhuḥ ||

aikyaṃ tayor lakṣitayor na vācyayoḥ
nigadyate 'nyonyaviruddhadharmiṇoḥ |
khadyotabhānv-or iva rājabhṛtyayoḥ
kūpāmburāśyoḥ paramāṇumervoḥ ||
units.translation:
When the meanings of Brahman and the Self, pointed to by the words “That” and “you,” are purified in this way, scripture repeatedly teaches their complete oneness through “You are That.”

That oneness is in their implied meanings, not their literal meanings, which have mutually opposed qualities—like a firefly and the sun, a king and a servant, a well and the ocean, or an atom and Mount Meru.

gloss.en: of a firefly and the sun
of a king and a servant
of a well and the ocean
of an atom and Mount Meru

units.editionTranslation: If thus the Shruti, in the dictum "Thou art That" (Tat-Tvam-Asi), repeatedly establishes the absolute identity of Brahman (or Ishwara) and Jiva, denoted by the terms That (Tat) and thou (Tvam) respectively, divesting these terms of their relative associations, then it is the identity of their implied, not literal, meanings which is sought to be inculcated; for they are of contradictory attributes to each other – like the sun and a glow-worm, the king and a servant, the ocean and a well, or Mount Meru and an atom.

units.label: Verse 243
units.deva:
तयोर्विरोधोऽयमुपाधिकल्पितो
न वास्तवः कश्चिदुपाधिरेषः ।
ईशस्य माया महदादिकारणं
जीवस्य कार्यं शृणु पञ्चकोशम् ॥
units.iast:
tayor virodho 'yam upādhikalpito
na vāstavaḥ kaścid upādhir eṣaḥ |
īśasya māyā mahadādikāraṇaṃ
jīvasya kāryaṃ śṛṇu pañcakośam ||
units.translation: Their apparent contradiction is imagined through limiting adjuncts; it is not real. Hear what these adjuncts are: Māyā, the cause of Mahat and the rest, for the Lord; and its effect—the five sheaths—for the individual self.
units.editionTranslation: This contradiction between them is created by superimposition, and is not something real. This superimposition, in the case of Ishwara (the Lord), is Maya or Nescience, which is the cause of Mahat and the rest, and in the case of the Jiva (the individual soul), listen – the five sheaths, which are the effects of Maya, stand for it.

units.label: Verse 244
units.deva:
एतावुपाधी परजीवयोस्तयोः
सम्यङ्निरासे न परो न जीवः ।
राज्यं नरेन्द्रस्य भटस्य खेटक्
तयोरपोहे न भटो न राजा ॥
units.iast:
etāv upādhī parajīvayos tayoḥ
samyag nirāse na paro na jīvaḥ |
rājyaṃ narendrasya bhaṭasya kheṭak
tayor apohe na bhaṭo na rājā ||
units.translation: These two are adjuncts of the Supreme and the individual self; when they are fully removed, neither remains as a separate one. It is like removing a king’s kingdom and a soldier’s shield: without the two, there is neither king nor soldier.

gloss.en: of the Supreme and the individual self

units.editionTranslation: These two are the superimpositions of Ishwara and the Jiva respectively, and when these are perfectly eliminated, there is neither Ishwara nor Jiva. A kingdom is the symbol of a king, and a shield of the soldier, and when these are taken away, there is neither king nor soldier.

units.label: Verse 245
units.deva:
अथात आदेश इति श्रुतिः स्वयं
निषेधति ब्रह्मणि कल्पितं द्वयम् ।
श्रुतिप्रमाणानुगृहीतबोधात्
तयोर् निरासः करणीय एव ॥
units.iast:
athāta ādeśa iti śrutiḥ svayaṃ
niṣedhati brahmaṇi kalpitaṃ dvayam |
śrutipramāṇānugṛhītabodhāt
tayor nirāsaḥ karaṇīya eva ||
units.translation: The revealed scripture itself, beginning “Now then, the teaching…,” negates the duality imagined in Brahman. Those two imagined aspects must indeed be removed through understanding supported by scriptural authority.
units.editionTranslation: The Vedas themselves in the words "now then is the injunction" etc., repudiate the duality imagined in Brahman. One must needs eliminate those two superimpositions by means of realisation supported by the authority of the Vedas.

units.label: Verse 246
units.deva:
नेदं नेदं कल्पितत्वान्न सत्यं
रज्जुदृष्टव्यालवत्स्वप्नवच्च ।
इत्थं दृश्यं साधुयुक्त्या व्यपोह्य
ज्ञेयः पश्चादेकभावस्तयोर्यः ॥
units.iast:
nedaṃ nedaṃ kalpitatvān na satyaṃ
rajjudṛṣṭavyālavatsvapnavacca |
itthaṃ dṛśyaṃ sādhuyuktyā vyapohya
jñeyaḥ paścād ekabhāvas tayoḥ yaḥ ||
units.translation: “Not this, not this”: because it is imagined, it is not real, like a snake seen in a rope or a dream. Having carefully set aside what is seen through sound reasoning, one should then know the single reality of those two.
units.editionTranslation: Neither this gross nor this subtle universe (is the Atman). Being imagined, they are not real – like the snake seen in the rope, and like dreams. Perfectly eliminating the objective world in this way by means of reasoning, one should next realise the oneness that underlies Ishwara and the Jiva.

units.label: Verse 247
units.deva:
ततस्तु तौ लक्षणया सुलक्ष्यौ
तयोरखण्डैकरसत्वसिद्धये ।
नालं जहत्या न तथाजहत्या
किन्तूभयार्थात्मिकयैव भाव्यम् ॥
units.iast:
tatastu tau lakṣaṇayā sulakṣyau
tayor akhaṇḍaikarasatvasiddhaye |
nālaṃ jahatyā na tathājahatyā
kintūbhayārthātmikayaiva bhāvyam ||
units.translation: To establish their indivisible oneness, those two are to be understood through implication. Neither total rejection nor total retention is enough; they must be understood through an interpretation that takes the relevant meaning from both.

gloss.en: by that which has as its nature

units.editionTranslation: Hence those two terms (Ishwara and Jiva) must be carefully considered through their implied meanings, so that their absolute identity may be established. Neither the method of total rejection nor that of complete retention will do. One must reason out through the process which combines the two.

units.label: Verses 248–249
units.deva:
स देवदत्तोऽयमितीह चैकता
विरुद्धधर्मांशमपास्य कथ्यते ।
यथा तथा तत्त्वमसीतिवाक्ये
विरुद्धधर्मानुभयत्र हित्वा ॥

संलक्ष्य चिन्मात्रतया सदात्मनोः
अखण्डभावः परिचीयते बुधैः ।
एवं महावाक्यशतेन कथ्यते
ब्रह्मात्मनोरैक्यमखण्डभावः ॥
units.iast:
sa devadatto 'yam itīha caikatā
viruddhadharmāṃśam apāsya kathyate |
yathā tathā tattvam asīti vākye
viruddhadharmān ubhayatra hitvā ||

saṃlakṣya cinmātratayā sadātmanoḥ
akhaṇḍabhāvaḥ paricīyate budhaiḥ |
evaṃ mahāvākyaśatena kathyate
brahmātmanor aikyam akhaṇḍabhāvaḥ ||
units.translation:
Just as the identity in “This is that Devadatta” is stated here after setting aside the conflicting attributes, so in the sentence “You are That,” the conflicting attributes on both sides are set aside.

By recognizing Brahman and the Self as pure consciousness, the wise discern their undivided nature. In this way, a hundred great sayings teach the indivisible oneness of Brahman and the Self.
units.editionTranslation: Just as in the sentence, "This is that Devadatta", the identity is spoken of, eliminating the contradictory portions, so in the sentence "Thou art That", the wise man must give up the contradictory elements on both sides and recognise the identity of Ishwara and Jiva, noticing carefully the essence of both, which is Chit, Knowledge Absolute. Thus hundreds of scriptural texts inculcate the oneness and identity of Brahman and Jiva.

units.label: Verse 250
units.deva:
अस्थूलमित्येतदसन्निरस्य
सिद्धं स्वतो व्योमवदप्रतर्क्यम् ।
अतो मृषामात्रमिदं प्रतीतं
जहीहि यत्स्वात्मतया गृहीतम्

ब्रह्माहम् इत्य् एव विशुद्धबुद्ध्या
विद्धि स्वमात्मानमखण्डबोधम् ॥
units.iast:
asthūlamityetadasannirasya
siddhaṃ svato vyomavadapratarkyam |
ato mṛṣāmātramidaṃ pratītaṃ
jahīhi yatsvātmatayā gṛhītam

brahmāham ity eva viśuddhabuddhyā
viddhi svamātmānamakhaṇḍabodham ||
units.translation: Having rejected the unreal through the teaching “not gross,” etc., [the Self] is self-established like space and beyond reasoning. Therefore abandon this mere false appearance that you have taken to be your own Self. With a purified intellect, know “I am Brahman”—your own Self, undivided awareness.
units.editionTranslation: Eliminating the not-Self, in the light of such passages as "It is not gross" etc., (one realises the Atman), which is self-established, unattached like the sky, and beyond the range of thought. Therefore dismiss this mere phantom of a body which thou perceivest and hast accepted as thy own self. By means of the purified understanding that thou art Brahman, realise thy own self, the Knowledge Absolute.

units.label: Verse 251
units.deva:
मृत्कार्यं सकलं घटादि सततं मृन्मात्रमेवाहितं
तद्वत्सज्जनितं सदात्मकमिदं सन्मात्रमेवाखिलम् ।
यस्मान्नास्ति सतः परं किमपि तत्सत्यं स आत्मा स्वयं
तस्मात्तत्त्वमसि प्रशान्तममलं ब्रह्माद्वयं यत्परम् ॥
units.iast:
mṛtkāryaṃ sakalaṃ ghaṭādi satataṃ mṛnmātram evāhitam
tadvatsajjanitaṃ sadātmakam idaṃ sanmātram evākhilam |
yasmān nāsti sataḥ paraṃ kim api tat satyaṃ sa ātmā svayaṃ
tasmāt tat tvam asi praśāntam amalaṃ brahmādvayaṃ yat param ||
units.translation: All effects of clay, such as pots, are always clay alone, established in clay. Likewise, this entire universe, born from Being and of the nature of Being, is Being alone. Since nothing at all exists beyond Being, That is the Real, the Self itself. Therefore, you are That: the peaceful, pure, supreme, nondual Brahman.
units.editionTranslation: All modifications of clay, such as the jar, which are always accepted by the mind as real, are (in reality) nothing but clay. Similarly, this entire universe which is produced from the real Brahman, is Brahman Itself and nothing but That. Because there is nothing else whatever but Brahman, and That is the only self-existent Reality, our very Self, therefore art thou that serene, pure, Supreme Brahman, the One without a second.

units.label: Verse 252
units.deva:
निद्राकल्पितदेशकालविषयज्ञात्रादि सर्वं यथा
मिथ्या तद्वदिहापि जाग्रति जगत्स्वाज्ञानकार्यत्वतः ।
यस्मादेवमिदं शरीरकरणप्राणाहमाद्यप्यसत्
तस्मात्तत्त्वमसि प्रशान्तममलं ब्रह्माद्वयं यत्परम् ॥
units.iast:
nidrākalpitadeśakālaviṣayajñātrādi sarvaṃ yathā
mithyā tadvad ihāpi jāgrati jagat svājñānakāryatvataḥ |
yasmād evam idaṃ śarīrakaraṇaprāṇāhamādy apy asat
tasmāt tat tvam asi praśāntam amalaṃ brahmādvayaṃ yat param ||
units.translation: Just as place, time, objects, the knower, and everything else imagined in a dream are unreal, so too the waking world is unreal, being an effect of one’s own ignorance. Since this body, the senses, life-breaths, ego, and the rest are also unreal, you are That: the peaceful, pure, supreme, nondual Brahman.

gloss.en: because it is an effect of one’s own ignorance

units.editionTranslation: As the place, time, objects, knower, etc., called up in dream are all unreal, so is also the world experienced here in the waking state, for it is all an effect of one’s own ignorance. Because this body, the organs, the Pranas, egoism, etc., are also thus unreal, therefore art thou that serene, pure, supreme Brahman, the One without a second.

units.label: Verse 253
units.deva:
यत्र भ्रान्त्या कल्पितं तद्विवेके
तत्तन्मात्रं नैव तस्माद्विभिन्नम् ।
स्वप्ने नष्टं स्वप्नविश्वं विचित्रं
स्वस्माद्भिन्नं किन्नु दृष्टं प्रबोधे ॥
units.iast:
yatra bhrāntyā kalpitaṃ tadviveke
tattanmātraṃ naiva tasmādvibhinnam |
svapne naṣṭaṃ svapnaviśvaṃ vicitraṃ
svasmādbhinnaṃ kinnu dṛṣṭaṃ prabodhe ||
units.translation: Where something is imagined through delusion, discernment shows it to be nothing but that basis, not different from it. The varied dream-world that has vanished—has it ever been seen as separate from oneself on waking?
units.editionTranslation: (What is) erroneously supposed to exist in something, is, when the truth about it has been known, nothing but that substratum, and not at all different from it: The diversified dream universe (appears and) passes away in the dream itself. Does it appear on waking as something distinct from one’s own Self ?

units.label: Verse 254
units.deva:
जातिनीतिकुलगोत्रदूरगं
नामरूपगुणदोषवर्जितम् ।
देशकालविषयातिवर्ति यद्
ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
jātinītikulagotradūragaṃ
nāmarūpaguṇadoṣavarjitam |
deśakālaviṣayātivarti yad
brahma tat tvam asi bhāvayātmani ||
units.translation: That Brahman, beyond caste, conduct, family, and lineage; free from name, form, qualities, and faults; beyond space, time, and objects of experience—you are That. Contemplate it within yourself.
units.editionTranslation: That which is beyond caste and creed, family and lineage; devoid of name and form, merit and demerit; transcending space, time and sense-object – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 255
units.deva:
यत्परं सकलवागगोचरं
गोचरं विमलबोधचक्षुषः ।
शुद्धचिद्घनमनादि वस्तु यद्
ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
yatparaṃ sakalavāgagocaraṃ
gocaraṃ vimalabodhacakṣuṣaḥ |
śuddhacidghanamanādi vastu yad
brahma tat tvam asi bhāvayātmani ||
units.translation: That supreme Brahman is beyond the reach of all speech, yet within reach of the eye of pure knowledge; it is pure, a mass of consciousness, and beginningless. You are that Brahman; contemplate it within yourself.

gloss.en: to the eye; by the eye

units.editionTranslation: That Supreme Brahman which is beyond the range of all speech, but accessible to the eye of pure illumination; which is pure, the Embodiment of Knowledge, the beginningless entity – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 256
units.deva:
षड्भिरूर्मिभिरयोगि योगिहृद्-
भावितं न करणैर् विभावितम् ।
बुद्ध्यवेद्यमनवद्यमस्ति यद्
ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
ṣaḍbhirūrmibhirayogi yogihṛd-
bhāvitaṃ na karaṇair vibhāvitam |
buddhyavedyamanavadyam asti yad
brahma tat tvam asi bhāvayātmani ||
units.translation: That which is untouched by the six waves of change, contemplated in a yogi’s heart, not perceived by the senses, beyond the intellect, and flawless—you are that Brahman; contemplate it within yourself.
units.editionTranslation: That which is untouched by the sixfold wave; meditated upon by the Yogi’s heart, but not grasped by the sense-organs; which the Buddhi cannot know; and which is unimpeachable – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 257
units.deva:
भ्रान्तिकल्पितजगत्कलाश्रयं
स्वाश्रयं च सदसद्विलक्षणम् ।
निष्कलं निरुपमानवद्धि यद्
ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
bhrāntikalpitajagatkalāśrayaṃ
svāśrayaṃ ca sadasadvilakṣaṇam |
niṣkalaṃ nirupamānavad dhi yad
brahma tat tvam asi bhāvayātmani ||
units.translation: That Brahman is the support of the world’s many parts imagined through delusion, yet is supported by itself; it is distinct from both existence and nonexistence, partless, and without equal. You are That; contemplate it within yourself.
units.editionTranslation: That which is the substratum of the universe with its various subdivisions, which are all creations of delusion; which Itself has no other support; which is distinct from the gross and subtle; which has no parts, and has verily no exemplar – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 258
units.deva:
जन्मवृद्धिपरिणत्यपक्षय-
व्याधिनाशनविहीनमव्ययम् ।
विश्वसृष्ट्यवविघातकारणं
ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
janmavṛddhipariṇatyapakṣaya-
vyādhināśanavihīnamavyayam |
viśvasṛṣṭyavavighātakāraṇaṃ
brahma tat tvam asi bhāvayātmani ||
units.translation: That Brahman is free from birth, growth, change, decline, illness, and destruction; it is imperishable and the cause of the universe’s creation, preservation, and dissolution. You are That; contemplate it within yourself.
units.editionTranslation: That which is free from birth, growth, development, waste, disease and death; which is indestructible; which is the cause of the projection, maintenance and dissolution of the universe – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 259
units.deva:
अस्तभेदमनपास्तलक्षणं
निस्तरङ्गजलराशिनिश्चलम् ।
नित्यमुक्तमविभक्तमूर्ति यद्
ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
astabhedamanapāstalakṣaṇaṃ
nistaraṅgajalarāśiniścalam |
nityamuktamavibhaktamūrti yad
brahma tat tvam asi bhāvayātmani ||
units.translation: That Brahman is free of distinctions, has a nature that is never lost, is still like a sea without waves, ever free, and of undivided form. You are That; contemplate it within yourself.
units.editionTranslation: That which is free from differentiation; whose essence is never non-existent; which is unmoved like the ocean without waves; the ever-free; of indivisible Form – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 260
units.deva:
एकम् एव सदनेककारणं
कारणान्तरनिरास्यकारणम् ।
कार्यकारणविलक्षणं स्वयं
ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
ekam eva sat anekakāraṇaṃ
kāraṇāntaranirāsyakāraṇam |
kāryakāraṇavilakṣaṇaṃ svayaṃ
brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani ||
units.translation: The one Existence alone is the cause of the many, the cause that rules out any other cause, and itself distinct from effect and cause. That is Brahman. You are That; contemplate it within yourself.
units.editionTranslation: That which, though One only, is the cause of the many; which refutes all other causes, but is Itself without cause; distinct from Maya and its effect, the universe; and independent – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 261
units.deva:
निर्विकल्पकमनल्पमक्षरं
यत्क्षराक्षरविलक्षणं परम् ।
नित्यमव्ययसुखं निरञ्जनं
ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
nirvikalpakam analpam akṣaraṃ
yat kṣarākṣaravilakṣaṇaṃ param |
nityam avyayasukhaṃ nirañjanaṃ
brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani ||
units.translation: That which is free from conceptual distinctions, boundless, imperishable, distinct from the perishable and the imperishable, supreme, eternal, inexhaustible bliss, and unstained is Brahman. You are That; contemplate it within yourself.
units.editionTranslation: That which is free from duality; which is infinite and indestructible; distinct from the universe and Maya, supreme, eternal; which is undying Bliss; taintless – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 262
units.deva:
यद्विभाति सदनेकधा भ्रमान्
नामरूपगुणविक्रियात्मना ।
हेमवत्स्वयमविक्रियं सदा
ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
yad vibhāti sad anekadhā bhramān
nāmarūpaguṇavikriyātmanā |
hemavat svayam avikriyaṃ sadā
brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani ||
units.translation: That Existence which, through delusion, appears in many ways in the form of name, form, quality, and change, yet itself remains always unchanged like gold, is Brahman. You are That; contemplate it within yourself.
units.editionTranslation: That Reality which (though One) appears variously owing to delusion, taking on names and forms, attributes and changes, Itself always unchanged, like gold in its modifications – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 263
units.deva:
यच्चकास्त्यनपरं परात्परं
प्रत्यगेकरसम् आत्मलक्षणम् ।
सत्यचित्सुखमनन्तमव्ययं
ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
yac cakāsti anaparaṃ parātparam
pratyag ekarasaṃ ātmalakṣaṇam |
satya-cit-sukham anantam avyayaṃ
brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani ||
units.translation: That which shines forth, with nothing beyond it, higher than the highest, inward and of a single essence, the very nature of the Self—truth, consciousness, and bliss, limitless and imperishable—is Brahman. You are That; contemplate it within yourself.

gloss.en: with nothing beyond it; without a second
whose defining nature is the Self

units.editionTranslation: That beyond which there is nothing; which shines even above Maya, which again is superior to its effect, the universe; the inmost Self of all, free from differentiation; the Real Self, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute; infinite and immutable – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 264
units.deva:
उक्तमर्थमिमम् आत्मनि स्वयं
भावयेत्प्रथितयुक्तिभिर्धिया ।
संशयादिरहितं कराम्बुवत्
तेन तत्त्वनिगमो भविष्यति ॥
units.iast:
uktam artham imam ātmani svayaṃ
bhāvayet prathitayuktibhir dhiyā |
saṃśayādirahitaṃ karāmbuvat
tena tattvanigamo bhaviṣyati ||
units.translation: One should oneself contemplate this meaning stated above within the Self, with the intellect and by well-established reasoning. Through this, certainty about the truth will arise, free from doubt and the like, as clear as water in one's palm.
units.editionTranslation: On the Truth, inculcated above, one must oneself meditate in one’s mind, through the intellect, by means of the recognised arguments. By that means one will realise the truth free from doubt etc., like water in the palm of one’s hand.

units.label: Verse 265
units.deva:
संबोधमात्रं परिशुद्धतत्त्वं
विज्ञाय सङ्घे नृपवच्च सैन्ये ।
तदाश्रयः स्वात्मनि सर्वदा स्थितो
विलापय ब्रह्मणि विश्वजातम् ॥
units.iast:
saṃbodhamātraṃ pariśuddhatattvaṃ
vijñāya saṅghe nṛpavac ca sainye |
tadāśrayaḥ svātmani sarvadā sthito
vilāpaya brahmaṇi viśvajātam ||
units.translation: Having recognized the perfectly pure Reality that is consciousness alone, like a king amid an assembled army, rely on That, remain always established in your own Self, and dissolve the whole universe into Brahman.

gloss.en: amid the assembly; among the host
the whole creation; what has arisen

units.editionTranslation: Realising in this body the Knowledge Absolute free from Nescience and its effects – like the king in an army – and being ever established in thy own Self by resting on that Knowledge, merge the universe in Brahman.

units.label: Verse 266
units.deva:
बुद्धौ गुहायां सदसद्विलक्षणं
ब्रह्मास्ति सत्यं परमद्वितीयम् ।
तद् आत्मना योऽत्र वसेद्गुहायां
पुनर्न तस्याङ्गगुहाप्रवेशः ॥
units.iast:
buddhau guhāyāṃ sadasadvilakṣaṇaṃ
brahmāsti satyaṃ paramadvitīyam |
tadātmanā yo 'tra vased guhāyāṃ
punar na tasya aṅgaguhāpraveśaḥ ||
units.translation: In the cave of the intellect there is Brahman, distinct from being and non-being, real, supreme, and without a second. Whoever dwells here in the cave as that Self does not enter the cave of the body again.
units.editionTranslation: In the cave of the Buddhi there is the Brahman, distinct from the gross and subtle, the Existence Absolute, Supreme, the One without a second. For one who lives in this cave as Brahman, O beloved, there is no more entrance into the mother’s womb.

units.label: Verse 267
units.deva:
ज्ञाते वस्तुन्य् अपि बलवती वासनानादिरेषा
कर्ता भोक्ताप्यहमिति दृढा यास्य संसारहेतुः ।
प्रत्यग्दृष्ट्यात्मनि निवसता सापनेया प्रयत्नान्
मुक्तिं प्राहुस्तदिह मुनयो वासनातानवं यत् ॥
units.iast:
jñāte vastuny api balavatī vāsanānādireṣā
kartā bhoktāpy aham iti dṛḍhā yā asya saṃsārahetuḥ |
pratyagdṛṣṭyātmani nivasatā sāpaneyā prayatnān
muktiṃ prāhus tad iha munayo vāsanātānavaṃ yat ||
units.translation: Even when Reality is known, this strong, beginningless latent tendency—“I am the doer and experiencer too”—which causes one’s saṃsāra must be removed through effort by dwelling in the Self with inward vision. Sages call the thinning of latent tendencies here and now “liberation.”
units.editionTranslation: Even after the Truth has been realised, there remains that strong, beginningless, obstinate impression that one is the agent and experiencer, which is the cause of one’s transmigration. It has to be carefully removed by living in a state of constant identification with the Supreme Self. Sages call that Liberation which is the attenuation of Vasanas (impressions) here and now.

units.label: Verse 268
units.deva:
अहं ममेति यो भावो देहाक्षादावनात्मनि ।
अध्यासोऽयं निरस्तव्यो विदुषा स्वात्मनिष्ठया ॥
units.iast:
ahaṃ mameti yo bhāvo dehākṣādāv anātmani |
adhyāso 'yaṃ nirastavyo viduṣā svātmaniṣṭhayā ||
units.translation: The notion “I” and “mine” placed on the body, senses, and other things that are not the Self is this superimposition; a discerning person must remove it through steadfastness in their own Self.

gloss.en: in what is not the Self
through steadfastness in one's own Self

units.editionTranslation: The idea of "me and mine" in the body, organs, etc., which are the non-Self – this superimposition the wise man must put a stop to, by identifying himself with the Atman.

units.label: Verse 269
units.deva:
ज्ञात्वा स्वं प्रत्यगात्मानं बुद्धितद्वृत्तिसाक्षिणम् ।
सोऽहम् इत्य् एव सद्वृत्त्यानात्मन्यात्ममतिं जहि ॥
units.iast:
jñātvā svaṃ pratyagātmānaṃ buddhitadvṛttisākṣiṇam |
so 'ham ity eva sadvṛttyānātmanyātmamatiṃ jahi ||
units.translation: Having recognized your own inner Self, the witness of the intellect and its states, abandon the notion that the non-Self is the Self by holding to the true thought, “I am That.”
units.editionTranslation: Realising thy own Inmost Self, the Witness of the Buddhi and its modifications, and constantly revolving the positive thought, "I am That", conquer this identification with the non-Self.

units.label: Verse 270
units.deva:
लोकानुवर्तनं त्यक्त्वा त्यक्त्वा देहानुवर्तनम् ।
शास्त्रानुवर्तनं त्यक्त्वा स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥
units.iast:
lokānuvartanaṃ tyaktvā tyaktvā dehānuvartanam |
śāstrānuvartanaṃ tyaktvā svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru ||
units.translation: Give up conformity to the world; give up conformity to the body; give up conformity to scripture; remove your own superimposition.
units.editionTranslation: Relinquishing the observance of social formalities, giving up all ideas of trimming up the body, and avoiding too mush engrossment with the Scriptures, do away with the superimposition that has come upon thyself.

units.label: Verse 271
units.deva:
लोकवासनया जन्तोः शास्त्रवासनयापि च ।
देहवासनया ज्ञानं यथावन्नैव जायते ॥
units.iast:
lokavāsanayā jantoḥ śāstravāsanayāpi ca |
dehavāsanayā jñānaṃ yathāvannaiva jāyate ||
units.translation: Because of worldly, scriptural, and bodily preoccupations, a person's knowledge does not arise fully as it should.
units.editionTranslation: Owing to the desire to run after society, the passion for too much study of the Scriptures and the desire to keep the body in good trim, people cannot attain to proper Realisation.

units.label: Verse 272
units.deva:
संसारकारागृहमोक्षमिच्छोर्
अयोमयं पादनिबन्धशृङ्खलम् ।
वदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः पटु वासनात्रयं
योऽस्माद्विमुक्तः समुपैति मुक्तिम् ॥
units.iast:
saṃsāra-kārāgṛha-mokṣam icchor
a-yomayaṃ pādanibandhaśṛṅkhalam |
vadanti tajjñāḥ paṭu vāsanātrayaṃ
yo 'smād vimuktaḥ samupaiti muktim ||
units.translation: For one who wants release from the prison of saṃsāra, the knowers call the three strong latent tendencies an iron chain binding the feet. Whoever is freed from these attains liberation.
units.editionTranslation: For one who seeks deliverance from the prison of this world (Samsara), those three desires have been designated by the wise as strong iron fetters to shackle one’s feet. He who is free from them truly attains to Liberation.

units.label: Verse 273
units.deva:
जलादिसंसर्गवशात्प्रभूत-
दुर्गन्धधूतागरुदिव्यवासना ।
संघर्षणेनैव विभाति सम्यग्-
विधूयमाने सति बाह्यगन्धे ॥
units.iast:
jalādi-saṃsarga-vaśāt prabhūta-durgandha-dhūta-agaru-divya-vāsanā |
saṃgharṣaṇenaiva vibhāti samyag-
vidhūyamāne sati bāhya-gandhe ||
units.translation: After contact with water and the like gives agaru a strong foul odor, its divine fragrance shines clearly when that outer smell is removed by rubbing.
units.editionTranslation: The lovely odour of the Agaru (agalochum) which is hidden by a powerful stench due to its contact with water etc., manifests itself as soon as the foreign smell has been fully removed by rubbing.

units.label: Verse 274
units.deva:
अन्तःश्रितानन्तदूरन्तवासना-
धूलीविलिप्ता परम् आत्मवासना ।
प्रज्ञातिसंघर्षणतो विशुद्धा
प्रतीयते चन्दनगन्धवत् स्फुटम् ॥
units.iast:
antaḥśritānanta-dūranta-vāsanā-
dhūlī-viliptā paramātma-vāsanā |
prajñāti-saṃgharṣaṇato viśuddhā
pratīyate candana-gandhavat sphuṭam ||
units.translation: Like sandalwood's fragrance, the latent tendency toward the Supreme Self—smeared with dust from the endless, hard-to-end tendencies lodged within—is perceived clearly when purified by the intense rubbing of discernment.

gloss.en: far-reaching; hard to bring to an end

units.editionTranslation: Like the fragrance of the sandal-wood, the perfume of the Supreme Self, which is covered with the dust of endless, violent impressions imbedded in the mind, when purified by the constant friction of Knowledge, is (again) clearly perceived.

units.label: Verse 275
units.deva:
अनात्मवासनाजालैस्तिरोभूतात्मवासना ।
नित्यात्मनिष्ठया तेषां नाशे भाति स्वयं स्फुटम् ॥
units.iast:
anātmavāsanājālair tirobhūtātmavāsanā |
nityātmaniṣṭhayā teṣāṃ nāśe bhāti svayaṃ sphuṭam ||
units.translation: The latent tendency toward the Self is concealed by networks of tendencies toward what is not the Self. When those are destroyed through steadfast abidance in the eternal Self, the Self shines clearly of itself.
units.editionTranslation: The desire for Self-realisation is obscured by innumerable desires for things other than the Self. When they have been destroyed by the constant attachment to the Self, the Atman clearly manifests Itself of Its own accord.

units.label: Verse 276
units.deva:
यथा यथा प्रत्यगवस्थितं मनः
तथा तथा मुञ्चति बाह्यवासनाम् ।
निःशेषमोक्षे सति वासनानां
आत्मानुभूतिः प्रतिबन्धशून्या ॥
units.iast:
yathā yathā pratyagavasthitaṃ manaḥ
tathā tathā muñcati bāhyavāsanām |
niḥśeṣamokṣe sati vāsanānām
ātmānubhūtiḥ pratibandhaśūnyā ||
units.translation: To the degree that the mind is established inwardly, to that same degree it lets go of external tendencies. When the latent tendencies are completely removed, realization of the Self is unobstructed.
units.editionTranslation: As the mind becomes gradually established in the Inmost Self, it proportionately gives up the desires for external objects. And when all such desires have been eliminated, there takes place the unobstructed realisation of the Atman.

units.label: Verse 277
units.deva:
स्वात्मन्य् एव सदा स्थित्वा मनो नश्यति योगिनः ।
वासनानां क्षयश्चातः स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥
units.iast:
svātmany eva sadā sthitvā mano naśyati yoginaḥ |
vāsanānāṃ kṣayaś cātaḥ svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru ||
units.translation: When the yogi remains always established in the Self alone, the mind dissolves and the latent tendencies are destroyed. Therefore, remove your own superimposition.
units.editionTranslation: The Yogi’s mind dies, being constantly fixed on his own Self. Thence follows the cessation of desires. Therefore do away with thy superimposition.

units.label: Verse 278
units.deva:
तमो द्वाभ्यां रजः सत्त्वात्सत्त्वं शुद्धेन नश्यति ।
तस्मात्सत्त्वमवष्टभ्य स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥
units.iast:
tamo dvābhyāṃ rajaḥ sattvāt sattvaṃ śuddhena naśyati |
tasmāt sattvam avaṣṭabhya svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru ||
units.translation: Tamas is destroyed by the two [rajas and sattva]; rajas is destroyed by sattva; and sattva is destroyed by the pure. Therefore, hold fast to sattva and remove your own superimposition.
units.editionTranslation: Tamas is destroyed by both Sattva and Rajas, Rajas by Sattva, and Sattva dies when purified. Therefore do way with thy superimposition through the help of Sattva.

units.label: Verse 279
units.deva:
प्रारब्धं पुष्यति वपुरिति निश्चित्य निश्चलः ।
धैर्यमालम्ब्य यत्नेन स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥
units.iast:
prārabdhaṃ puṣyati vapuḥ iti niścitya niścalaḥ |
dhairyam ālambya yatnena svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru ||
units.translation: Having firmly understood, “Prārabdha sustains the body,” remain steady, take courage, and work to remove your own superimposition.
units.editionTranslation: Knowing for certain that the Prarabdha work will maintain this body, remain quiet and do away with thy superimposition carefully and with patience.

units.label: Verse 280
units.deva:
नाहं जीवः परं ब्रह्मेत्यतद्व्यावृत्तिपूर्वकम् ।
वासनावेगतः प्राप्तस्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥
units.iast:
nāhaṃ jīvaḥ paraṃ brahmety atad-vyāvṛtti-pūrvakam |
vāsanā-vegataḥ prāpta-svādhyāsa-apanayaṃ kuru ||
units.translation: With the understanding “I am not the individual self; I am supreme Brahman,” first reject what is not the Self, then remove your own superimposition that has arisen through the force of latent tendencies.
units.editionTranslation: "I am not the individual soul, but the Supreme Brahman" – eliminating thus all that is not-Self, do away with thy superimposition, which has come through the momentum of (past) impressions.

units.label: Verse 281
units.deva:
श्रुत्या युक्त्या स्वानुभूत्या ज्ञात्वा सार्वात्म्यम् आत्मनः ।
क्वचिदाभासतः प्राप्तस्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥
units.iast:
śrutyā yuktyā svānubhūtyā jñātvā sārvātmyam ātmanaḥ |
kvacid ābhāsataḥ prāpta-svādhyāsa-apanayaṃ kuru ||
units.translation: Having known through scripture, reasoning, and your own experience that the Self is the Self of all, remove your own superimposition whenever even a semblance of it appears.

gloss.en: the nature of being the Self of all

units.editionTranslation: Realising thyself as the Self of all by means of Scripture, reasoning and by thy own realisation, do away thy superimposition, even when a trace of it seems to appear.

units.label: Verse 282
units.deva:
अनादानविसर्गाभ्यामीषन्नास्ति क्रिया मुनेः ।
तदेकनिष्ठया नित्यं स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥
units.iast:
anādāna-visargābhyām īṣan nāsti kriyā muneḥ |
tad-eka-niṣṭhayā nityaṃ svādhyāsa-apanayaṃ kuru ||
units.translation: Because the sage neither takes things up nor casts them away, there is scarcely any activity for him. Therefore, remain always steadfast in That alone and remove your own superimposition.
units.editionTranslation: The sage has no connection with action, since he has no idea of accepting or giving up. Therefore, through constant engrossment on the Brahman, do away with thy superimposition.

units.label: Verse 283
units.deva:
तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्योत्थब्रह्मात्मैकत्वबोधतः ।
ब्रह्मण्य् आत्मत्वदार्ढ्याय स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥
units.iast:
tattvam-asi-ādi-vākyottha-brahmātmaikatva-bodhataḥ |
brahmaṇy ātmatva-dārḍhyāya svādhyāsa-apanayaṃ kuru ||
units.translation: From the knowledge of the oneness of Brahman and the Self that arises from statements such as “You are That,” remove your own superimposition so that your identity as the Self in Brahman becomes firm.
units.editionTranslation: Through the realisation of the identity of Brahman and the soul, resulting from such great dicta as "Thou art That", do away with thy superimposition, with a view to strengthening thy identification with Brahman.

units.label: Verse 284
units.deva:
अहंभावस्य देहेऽस्मिन्निःशेषविलयावधि ।
सावधानेन युक्तात्मा स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥
units.iast:
ahaṃbhāvasya dehe 'smin niḥśeṣa-vilayāvadhi |
sāvadhānena yuktātmā svādhyāsa-apanayaṃ kuru ||
units.translation: Until the sense of “I” in this body has been completely dissolved, remain vigilant and collected, and remove your own superimposition.
units.editionTranslation: Until the identification with this body is completely rooted out, do away with thy superimposition with watchfulness and a concentrated mind.

units.label: Verse 285
units.deva:
प्रतीतिर्जीवजगतोः स्वप्नवद्भाति यावता ।
तावन्निरन्तरं विद्वन्स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥
units.iast:
pratītir jīva-jagatoḥ svapnavad bhāti yāvatā |
tāvat nirantaraṃ vidvan sva-adhyāsa-apanayaṃ kuru ||
units.translation: O wise one, for as long as the perception of the individual and the world appears like a dream, keep removing your own superimposition without interruption.
units.editionTranslation: So long as even a dream-like perception of the universe and souls persists, do away with thy superimposition, O learned man, without the least break.

units.label: Verse 286
units.deva:
निद्राया लोकवार्तायाः शब्दादेर् अपि विस्मृतेः ।
क्वचिन्नावसरं दत्त्वा चिन्तयात्मानम् आत्मनि ॥
units.iast:
nidrāyā lokavārtāyāḥ śabdāder api vismṛteḥ |
kvacin na avasaraṃ dattvā cintaya ātmānam ātmani ||
units.translation: Giving no room for forgetfulness caused by sleep, worldly concerns, sound, or the other sense-objects, contemplate the Self within yourself.
units.editionTranslation: Without giving the slightest chance to oblivion on account of sleep, concern in secular matters or the sense-objects, reflect on the Self in thy mind.

units.label: Verse 287
units.deva:
मातापित्रोर् मलोद्भूतं मलमांसमयं वपुः ।
त्यक्त्वा चाण्डालवद्दूरं ब्रह्मीभूय कृती भव ॥
units.iast:
mātā-pitroḥ malodbhūtaṃ mala-māṃsamayaṃ vapuḥ |
tyaktvā cāṇḍālavaddūraṃ brahmībhūya kṛtī bhava ||
units.translation: Having left behind this body, born from the impurities of mother and father and made of impurity and flesh, keep it far away as one would an outcaste; become Brahman and be fulfilled.
units.editionTranslation: Shunning from a safe distance the body which has come from impurities of the parents and itself consists of flesh and impurities – as one does an outcast – be thou Brahman and realise the consummation of thy life.

units.label: Verse 288
units.deva:
घटाकाशं महाकाश इवात्मानं परात्मनि ।
विलाप्याखण्डभावेन तूष्णी भव सदा मुने ॥
units.iast:
ghaṭākāśaṃ mahākāśa ivātmānaṃ parātmani |
vilāpya akhaṇḍa-bhāvena tūṣṇī bhava sadā mune ||
units.translation: Having dissolved the Self into the Supreme Self, as pot-space [is dissolved] into great space, through the understanding of non-division, remain always silent, O sage.

gloss.en: through the understanding; in the state

units.editionTranslation: Merging the finite soul in the Supreme Self, like the space enclosed by a jar in the infinite space, by means of meditation on their identity, always keep quiet, O sage.

units.label: Verse 289
units.deva:
स्वप्रकाशमधिष्ठानं स्वयंभूय सदात्मना ।
ब्रह्माण्डम् अपि पिण्डाण्डं त्यज्यतां मलभाण्डवत् ॥
units.iast:
svaprakāśam adhiṣṭhānaṃ svayaṃ bhūya sadātmanā |
brahmāṇḍam api piṇḍāṇḍaṃ tyajyatāṃ mala-bhāṇḍavat ||
units.translation: Become yourself the self-luminous ground, abiding as the true Self; abandon both the cosmic whole and the individual body as if they were vessels of filth.
units.editionTranslation: Becoming thyself the self-effulgent Brahman, the substratum of all phenomena – as that Reality give up both the macrocosm and the microcosm, like two filthy receptacles.

units.label: Verse 290
units.deva:
चिदात्मनि सदानन्दे देहारूढामहंधियम् ।
निवेश्य लिङ्गमुत्सृज्य केवलो भव सर्वदा ॥
units.iast:
cidātmani sadānande dehārūḍhām ahaṃ-dhiyam |
niveśya liṅgam utsṛjya kevalo bhava sarvadā ||
units.translation: Place the body-rooted sense of “I” in the consciousness-Self, which is ever blissful; abandon the subtle body and remain the Self alone, always.
units.editionTranslation: Transferring the identification now rooted in the body to the Atman, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, and discarding the subtle body, be thou ever alone, independent.

units.label: Verse 291
units.deva:
यत्रैष जगदाभासो दर्पणान्तः पुरं यथा ।
तद्ब्रह्माहमिति ज्ञात्वा कृतकृत्यो भविष्यसि ॥
units.iast:
yatraiṣa jagadābhāso darpaṇāntaḥ puraṃ yathā |
tad brahmāham iti jñātvā kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi ||
units.translation: In That, this appearance of the world is like a city inside a mirror. Knowing “I am that Brahman,” you will have accomplished what is to be done.
units.editionTranslation: That in which there is this reflection of the universe, as of a city in a mirror – that Brahman art thou; knowing this thou wilt attain the consummation of thy life.

units.label: Verse 292
units.deva:
यत्सत्यभूतं निजरूपमाद्यं
चिदद्वयानन्दमरूपमक्रियम् ।
तदेत्य मिथ्यावपुरुत्सृजेत
शैलूषवद्वेषमुपात्तमात्मनः ॥
units.iast:
yat satyabhūtaṃ nija-rūpam ādyam
cid-advayānandam arūpam akriyam |
tad etya mithyā-vapur utsṛjeta
śailūṣavad veṣam upāttam ātmanaḥ ||
units.translation: Having reached that which is truly real, one's own original nature—nondual consciousness and bliss, formless and actionless—one should cast off the false body one has assumed, like an actor casting off a costume.
units.editionTranslation: That which is real and one’s own primeval Essence, that Knowledge and Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, which is beyond form and activity – attaining That one should cease to identify oneself with one’s false bodies, like an actor giving up his assumed mask.

units.label: Verse 293
units.deva:
सर्वात्मना दृश्यमिदं मृषैव
नैवाहमर्थः क्षणिकत्वदर्शनात् ।
जानाम्यहं सर्वमिति प्रतीतिः
कुतोऽहम् आदेः क्षणिकस्य सिध्येत् ॥
units.iast:
sarvātmanā dṛśyam idaṃ mṛṣaiva
naivāhamārthaḥ kṣaṇikatva-darśanāt |
jānāmy ahaṃ sarvam iti pratītiḥ
kuto 'ham-ādeḥ kṣaṇikasya sidhyet ||
units.translation: This entire visible world is indeed false, and the ego—the mistaken meaning of “I”—is not real, since it is seen to be momentary. How could the thought “I know everything” be established as true of the momentary ego and the like?
units.editionTranslation: This objective universe is absolutely unreal; neither is egoism a reality, for it is observed to be momentary. How can the perception, "I know all", be true of egoism etc., which are momentary ?

units.label: Verse 294
units.deva:
अहंपदार्थस्त्वहमादिसाक्षी
नित्यं सुषुप्ताव् अपि भावदर्शनात् ।
ब्रूते ह्यजो नित्य इति श्रुतिः स्वयं
तत्प्रत्यगात्मा सदसद्विलक्षणः ॥
units.iast:
ahaṃ-pada-arthaḥ tv aham-ādi-sākṣī
nityaṃ suṣuptāv api bhāva-darśanāt |
brūte hy ajo nitya iti śrutiḥ svayaṃ
tat pratyag-ātmā sad-asad-vilakṣaṇaḥ ||
units.translation: But the referent of “I” is the witness of the ego and the rest, ever present because its existence is recognized even in deep sleep. Scripture itself declares it unborn and eternal. That inner Self is distinct from being and non-being.
units.editionTranslation: But the real ‘I" is that which witnesses the ego and the rest. It exists always, even in the state of profound sleep. The Shruti itself says, "It is birthless, eternal", etc. Therefore the Paramatman is different from the gross and subtle bodies.

units.label: Verse 295
units.deva:
विकारिणां सर्वविकारवेत्ता
नित्याविकारो भवितुं समर्हति ।
मनोरथस्वप्नसुषुप्तिषु स्फुटं
पुनः पुनर्दृष्टमसत्त्वमेतयोः ॥
units.iast:
vikāriṇāṃ sarva-vikāra-vettā
nityāvikāro bhavituṃ samarhati |
manoratha-svapna-suṣuptiṣu sphuṭaṃ
punaḥ punaḥ dṛṣṭam asattvam etayoḥ ||
units.translation: The knower of every change in changing things must itself be eternally changeless. In daydream, dream, and deep sleep, the unreality of these two [the gross and subtle bodies] is seen clearly again and again.
units.editionTranslation: The knower of all changes in things subject to change should necessarily be eternal and changeless. The unreality of the gross and subtle bodies is again and again clearly observed in imagination, dream and profound sleep.

units.label: Verse 296
units.deva:
अतोऽभिमानं त्यज मांसपिण्डे
पिण्डाभिमानिन्य् अपि बुद्धिकल्पिते ।
कालत्रयाबाध्यमखण्डबोधं
ज्ञात्वा स्वमात्मानमुपैहि शान्तिम् ॥
units.iast:
ato 'bhimānaṃ tyaja māṃsa-piṇḍe
piṇḍābhimāniny api buddhi-kalpite |
kālatrayābādhyam akhaṇḍa-bodhaṃ
jñātvā svam ātmānam upaihi śāntim ||
units.translation: Therefore, give up identification with this lump of flesh and also with the body-identifying ego imagined by the intellect. Knowing your own Self as undivided awareness, not contradicted in past, present, or future, attain peace.

gloss.en: in the one identified with it

units.editionTranslation: Therefore give up the identification with this lump of flesh, the gross body, as well as with the ego or the subtle body, which are both imagined by the Buddhi. Realising thy own Self, which is Knowledge Absolute and not to be denied in the past, present or future, attain to Peace.

units.label: Verse 297
units.deva:
त्यजाभिमानं कुलगोत्रनाम-
रूपाश्रमेष्वार्द्रशवाश्रितेषु ।
लिङ्गस्य धर्मानपि कर्तृतादीन्
त्यक्त्वा भवाखण्डसुखस्वरूपः ॥
units.iast:
tyajābhimānaṃ kulagotranāma-
rūpāśrameṣv ārdrāśavāśriteṣu |
liṅgasya dharmān api kartṛtādīn
tyaktvā bhavākhaṇḍasukhasvarūpaḥ ||
units.translation: Give up identification with family, lineage, name, form, and life-stage, all resting on this moist corpse [the body]. Give up even the subtle body's traits, such as doership; having relinquished them, become the very nature of undivided bliss.
units.editionTranslation: Cease to identify thyself with the family, lineage, name, form and the order of life, which pertain to the body that is like a rotten corpse (to a man of realisation). Similarly, giving up ideas of agency and so forth, which are attributes of the subtle body, be the Essence of Bliss Absolute.

units.label: Verse 298
units.deva:
सन्त्यन्ये प्रतिबन्धाः पुंसः संसारहेतवो दृष्टाः ।
तेषाम् एवं मूलं प्रथमविकारो भवत्यहंकारः ॥
units.iast:
santy anye pratibandhāḥ puṃsaḥ saṃsāra-hetavo dṛṣṭāḥ |
teṣām evaṃ mūlaṃ prathama-vikāro bhavaty ahaṃkāraḥ ||
units.translation: Other obstacles that cause saṃsāra for a person are also seen. Their root, as described, is the first modification: the ego.
units.editionTranslation: Other obstacles are also observed to exist for men, which lead to transmigration. The root of them, for the above reasons, is the first modification of Nescience called egoism.

units.label: Verse 299
units.deva:
यावत्स्यात्स्वस्य संबन्धोऽहंकारेण दुरात्मना ।
तावन् न लेशमात्रापि मुक्तिवार्ता विलक्षणा ॥
units.iast:
yāvat syāt svasya saṃbandho 'haṃkāreṇa durātmanā |
tāvan na leśamātrāpi mukti-vārtā vilakṣaṇā ||
units.translation: As long as one remains connected to this harmful ego, there is not even the slightest question of liberation, which is of a wholly different kind.
units.editionTranslation: So long as one has any relation to this wicked ego, there should not be the least talk about Liberation, which is unique.

units.label: Verse 300
units.deva:
अहंकारग्रहान्मुक्तः स्वरूपमुपपद्यते ।
चन्द्रवद्विमलः पूर्णः सदानन्दः स्वयंप्रभः ॥
units.iast:
ahaṃkāra-grahān muktaḥ svarūpam upapadyate |
candravat vimalaḥ pūrṇaḥ sadānandaḥ svayaṃprabhaḥ ||
units.translation: Freed from the grasp of ego, one attains one's own nature: pure as the moon, full, ever-blissful, and self-luminous.
units.editionTranslation: Freed from the clutches of egoism, as the moon from those of Rahu, man attains to his real nature, and becomes pure, infinite, ever blissful and self-luminous.

units.label: Verse 301
units.deva:
यो वा पुरे सोऽहम् इति प्रतीतो
बुद्ध्या प्रकॢप्तस्तमसातिमूढया ।
तस्यैव निःशेषतया विनाशे
ब्रह्मात्मभावः प्रतिबन्धशून्यः ॥
units.iast:
yo vā pure so 'ham iti pratīto
buddhyā prakḷptas tamasātimūḍhayā |
tasyaiva niḥśeṣatayā vināśe
brahmātma-bhāvaḥ pratibandhaśūnyaḥ ||
units.translation: The notion perceived in the body as “I am that,” fashioned by an intellect utterly deluded by ignorance—when that very notion is completely destroyed, identity with Brahman is free from obstruction.

gloss.en: in the city; in the body
identity of Brahman and the Self

units.editionTranslation: That which has been created by the Buddhi extremely deluded by Nescience, and which is perceived in this body as "I am such and such" – when that egoism is totally destroyed, one attains an unobstructed identity with Brahman.

units.label: Verse 302
units.deva:
ब्रह्मानन्दनिधिर्महाबलवताहंकारघोराहिना
संवेष्ट्य् आत्मनि रक्ष्यते गुणमयैश्चण्डेस्त्रिभिर्मस्तकैः ।
विज्ञानाख्यमहासिना श्रुतिमता विच्छिद्य शीर्षत्रयं
निर्मूल्याहिमिमं निधिं सुखकरं धीरोऽनुभोक्तुंक्षमः ॥
units.iast:
brahmānanda-nidhir mahābalavatāhaṃkāra-ghorāhinā
saṃveṣṭyātmani rakṣyate guṇamayaiś caṇḍais tribhir mastakaiḥ |
vijñānākhya-mahāsinā śrutimatā vicchidya śīrṣatrayaṃ
nirmūlyāhim imaṃ nidhiṃ sukhakaraṃ dhīro 'nubhoktuṃ kṣamaḥ ||
units.translation: The treasure of Brahman-bliss is encircled and guarded by the mighty, dreadful serpent of ego, whose three fierce heads are made of the guṇas. Having severed its three heads with the great sword called knowledge, guided by scripture, and uprooted this serpent, the wise one can enjoy this bliss-giving treasure.

gloss.en: by the dreadful serpent of ego
with the great sword called knowledge
guided by scripture; endowed with śruti

units.editionTranslation: The treasure of the Bliss of Brahman is coiled round by the mighty and dreadful serpent of egoism, and guarded for its own use by means of its three fierce hoods consisting of the three Gunas. Only the wise man, destroying it by severing its three hoods with the great sword of realisation in accordance with the teachings of the Shrutis, can enjoy this treasure which confers bliss.

units.label: Verse 303
units.deva:
यावद्वा यत् किंचिद् विषदोषस्फूर्तिरस्ति चेद्देहे ।
कथम् आरोग्याय भवेत्तद्वदहन्तापि योगिनो मुक्त्यै ॥
units.iast:
yāvadvā yat kiṃcid viṣadoṣasphūrtir asti ced dehe |
katham ārogyāya bhavet tadvat ahantāpi yogino muktyai ||
units.translation: As long as even some trace of poison's harmful effect remains in the body, how could there be health? In the same way, ego-sense is an obstacle to the yogin's liberation.
units.editionTranslation: As long as there is a trace of poisoning left in the body, how can one hope for recovery ? Similar is the effect of egoism on the Yogi’s Liberation.

units.label: Verse 304
units.deva:
अहमोऽत्यन्तनिवृत्त्या तत्कृतनानाविकल्पसंहृत्या ।
प्रत्यक्तत्त्वविवेकादिदमहमस्मीति विन्दते तत्त्वम् ॥
units.iast:
ahamo 'tyanta-nivṛttyā tat-kṛta-nānā-vikalpa-saṃhṛtyā |
pratyak-tattva-vivekād idam aham asmīti vindate tattvam ||
units.translation: Through the ego's complete cessation, the dissolving of its many thought-constructs, and discrimination of the inner Reality, one realizes the Truth: “I am this.”
units.editionTranslation: Through the complete cessation of egoism, through the stoppage of the diverse mental waves due to it, and through the discrimination of the inner Reality, one realises that Reality as "I am This".

units.label: Verse 305
units.deva:
अहंकारे कर्तर्यहमिति मतिं मुञ्च सहसा
विकारात्मन्य् आत्मप्रतिफलजुषि स्वस्थितिमुषि ।
यदध्यासात्प्राप्ता जनिमृतिजरादुःखबहुला
प्रतीचश्चिन्मूर्तेस्तव सुखतनोः संसृतिरियम् ॥
units.iast:
ahaṃkāre kartary aham iti matiṃ muñca sahasā
vikārātmany ātmapratiphalajuṣi svasthitimuṣi |
yad adhyāsāt prāptā janimṛtijarāduḥkhabahulā
pratīcaścinmūrtes tava sukhatanoḥ saṃsṛtir iyam ||
units.translation: At once abandon the thought “I am the doer” in ego, which is a modification, bears a reflection of the Self, and steals your abiding in your own nature. Through superimposing it, you have come to this saṃsāra, full of the suffering of birth, death, and old age, though your nature is inward consciousness and bliss.

gloss.en: in what is by nature change
bearing a reflection of the Self
stealing one's abiding in one's own nature

units.editionTranslation: Give up immediately thy identification with egoism, the agent, which is by its nature a modification, is endued with a reflection of the Self, and diverts one from being established in the Self – identifying thyself with which thou hast come by this relative existence, full of the miseries of birth, decay and death, though thou art the Witness, the Essence of Knowledge and Bliss Absolute.

units.label: Verse 306
units.deva:
सदैकरूपस्य चिदात्मनो विभोर्
आनन्दमूर्तेरनवद्यकीर्तेः ।
नैवान्यथा क्वाप्यविकारिणस्ते
विनाहमध्यासममुष्य संसृतिः ॥
units.iast:
sadaika-rūpasya cid-ātmāno vibhor
ānanda-mūrter anavadya-kīrteḥ |
naivānyathā kvāpy avikāriṇas te
vināham-adhyāsam amuṣya saṃsṛtiḥ ||
units.translation: Without this superimposition of “I,” there is no transmigration anywhere for you—the changeless one, ever of one nature, the conscious Self, all-pervading, the form of bliss, and of flawless glory.
units.editionTranslation: But for thy identification with that egoism there can never be any transmigration for thee who art immutable and eternally the same, the Knowledge Absolute, omnipresent, the Bliss Absolute, and of untarnished glory.

units.label: Verse 307
units.deva:
तस्मादहंकारमिमं स्वशत्रुं
भोक्तुर्गले कण्टकवत्प्रतीतम् ।
विच्छिद्य विज्ञानमहासिना स्फुटं
भुङ्क्ष्वात्मसाम्राज्यसुखं यथेष्टम् ॥
units.iast:
tasmād ahaṃkāram imaṃ sva-śatruṃ
bhoktur gale kaṇṭakavat pratītam |
vicchidya vijñāna-mahāsinā sphuṭaṃ
bhuṅkṣvātma-sāmrājya-sukhaṃ yatheṣṭam ||
units.translation: Therefore, cut away this ego, your own enemy, perceived like a thorn in the enjoyer's throat, with the clear great sword of knowledge; then enjoy at will the bliss of the Self's sovereignty.
units.editionTranslation: Therefore destroying this egoism, thy enemy - which appears like a thorn sticking in the throat of a man taking meal – with the great sword of realisation, enjoy directly and freely the bliss of thy own empire, the majesty of the Atman.

units.label: Verse 308
units.deva:
ततोऽहम् आदेर्विनिवर्त्य वृत्तिं
संत्यक्तरागः परमार्थलाभात् ।
तूष्णीं समास्स्वात्मसुखानुभूत्या
पूर्णात्मना ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पः ॥
units.iast:
tato 'ham-āder vinivartya vṛttiṃ
saṃtyakta-rāgaḥ paramārtha-lābhāt |
tūṣṇīṃ samāssvātma-sukhānubhūtyā
pūrṇātmanā brahmaṇi nirvikalpaḥ ||
units.translation: Then, withdrawing the activity of ego and the rest, having abandoned attachment through attainment of the highest Reality, remain silent in Brahman, free of thought-constructs, through the experience of the Self's bliss, as the full Self.
units.editionTranslation: Checking the activities of egoism etc., and giving up all attachment through the realisation of the Supreme Reality, be free from all duality through the enjoyment of the Bliss of Self, and remain quiet in Brahman, for thou hast attained thy infinite nature.

units.label: Verse 309
units.deva:
समूलकृत्तोऽपि महानहं पुनः
व्युल्लेखितः स्याद्यदि चेतसा क्षणम् ।
संजीव्य विक्षेपशतं करोति
नभस्वता प्रावृषि वारिदो यथा ॥
units.iast:
samūla-kṛtto 'pi mahān ahaṃ punaḥ
vyullekhitaḥ syād yadi cetasā kṣaṇam |
sañjīvya vikṣepa-śataṃ karoti
nabhasvatā prāvṛṣi vārido yathā ||
units.translation: Even though cut out root and all, the great ego may be called up in the mind again, even for a moment. Revived, it creates hundreds of distractions, like a rain cloud driven by the wind in the rainy season.
units.editionTranslation: Even though completely rooted out, this terrible egoism, if revolved in the mind even for a moment, returns to life and creates hundreds of mischiefs, like a cloud ushered in by the wind during the rainy season.

units.label: Verse 310
units.deva:
निगृह्य शत्रोरहमोऽवकाशः
क्वचिन् न देयो विषयानुचिन्तया ।
स एव संजीवनहेतुरस्य
प्रक्षीणजम्बीरतरोर् इवाम्बु ॥
units.iast:
nigṛhya śatror ahamo 'vakāśaḥ
kvacin na deyo viṣayānucintayā |
sa eva saṃjīvana-hetur asya
prakṣīṇa-jambīra-taroḥ ivāmbu ||
units.translation: After subduing the enemy, ego, never give it an opening through dwelling on sense-objects. That alone revives it, like water revives an almost withered lemon tree.
units.editionTranslation: Overpowering this enemy, egoism, not a moment’s respite should be given to it by thinking on the sense-objects. That is verily the cause of its coming back to life, like water to a citron tree that has almost dried up.

units.label: Verse 311
units.deva:
देहात्मना संस्थित एव कामी
विलक्षणः कामयिता कथं स्यात् ।
अतोऽर्थसन्धानपरत्वम् एव
भेदप्रसक्त्या भवबन्धहेतुः ॥
units.iast:
dehātmanā saṃsthita eva kāmī
vilakṣaṇaḥ kāmayitā kathaṃ syāt |
ato 'rtha-sandhāna-paratvam eva
bheda-prasaktyā bhava-bandha-hetuḥ ||
units.translation: Only one established in the body as the Self is a desirer of sense-objects. How could one who is distinct from the body be a desirer? Therefore, fixation on pursuing objects, through attachment to duality, is the cause of bondage in worldly existence.

gloss.en: with the body as the Self

units.editionTranslation: He alone who has identified himself with the body is greedy after sense-pleasures. How can one, devoid of the body-idea, be greedy (like him) ? Hence the tendency to think on the sense-objects is verily the cause of the bondage of transmigration, giving rise to an idea of distinction or duality.

units.label: Verse 312
units.deva:
कार्यप्रवर्धनाद्बीजप्रवृद्धिः परिदृश्यते ।
कार्यनाशाद्बीजनाशस्तस्मात्कार्यं निरोधयेत् ॥
units.iast:
kārya-pravardhanād bīja-pravṛddhiḥ paridṛśyate |
kārya-nāśād bīja-nāśas tasmāt kāryaṃ nirodhayet ||
units.translation: Growth of the effect is seen to bring growth of the seed; when the effect is destroyed, the seed is destroyed. Therefore, one should restrain the effect.
units.editionTranslation: When the effects are developed, the seed also is observed to be such, and when the effects are destroyed, the seed also is seen to be destroyed. Therefore one must subdue the effects.

units.label: Verse 313
units.deva:
वासनावृद्धितः कार्यं कार्यवृद्ध्या च वासना ।
वर्धते सर्वथा पुंसः संसारो न निवर्तते ॥
units.iast:
vāsanā-vṛddhitaḥ kāryaṃ kārya-vṛddhyā ca vāsanā |
vardhate sarvathā puṃsaḥ saṃsāro na nivartate ||
units.translation: From the growth of latent tendencies, action grows; and through the growth of action, latent tendencies grow. Thus a person's saṃsāra grows in every way and does not cease.
units.editionTranslation: Through the increase of desires selfish work increases, and when there is an increase of selfish work, there is an increase of desire also. And man’s transmigration is never at an end.

units.label: Verse 314
units.deva:
संसारबन्धविच्छित्त्यै तद् द्वयं प्रदहेद्यतिः ।
वासनावृद्धिरेताभ्यां चिन्तया क्रियया बहिः ॥
units.iast:
saṃsāra-bandha-vicchittyai tad dvayaṃ pradahed yatiḥ |
vāsanā-vṛddhir etābhyāṃ cintayā kriyayā bahiḥ ||
units.translation: To cut the bondage of saṃsāra, the renunciate should burn those two: mental dwelling and outward action, by which latent tendencies grow.
units.editionTranslation: For the sake of breaking the chain of transmigration, the Sannyasin should burn to ashes those two; for thinking of the sense-objects and doing selfish acts lead to an increase of desires.

units.label: Verses 315–316
units.deva:
ताभ्यां प्रवर्धमाना सा सूते संसृतिम् आत्मनः ।
त्रयाणां च क्षयोपायः सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा ॥

सर्वत्र सर्वतः सर्वब्रह्ममात्रावलोकनैः ।
सद्भाववासनादार्ढ्यात्तत्त्रयं लयमश्नुते ॥
units.iast:
tābhyāṃ pravardhamānā sā sūte saṃsṛtim ātmanaḥ |
trayāṇāṃ ca kṣayopāyaḥ sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā ||

sarvatra sarvataḥ sarvabrahmamātrāvalokanaiḥ |
sadbhāvavāsanādārḍhyāt tat trayaṃ layam aśnute ||
units.translation: Growing through those two, the latent tendency gives rise to a person's saṃsāra. The way to end the three [tendency, thought, and action] at all times and in every state is to see everything, everywhere, as Brahman alone; by strengthening the disposition toward true Being, that triad dissolves.

gloss.en: in every way; from all sides

units.editionTranslation: Augmented by these two, desires produce one’s transmigration. The way to destroy these three, however, lies in looking upon everything, under all circumstances, always, everywhere and in all respects, as Brahman and Brahman alone. Through the strengthening of the longing to be one with Brahman, those three are annihilated.

units.label: Verse 317
units.deva:
क्रियानाशे भवेच्चिन्तानाशोऽस्माद्वासनाक्षयः ।
वासनाप्रक्षयो मोक्षः सा जीवन्मुक्तिरिष्यते ॥
units.iast:
kriyānāśe bhavec cintānāśo 'smād vāsanākṣayaḥ |
vāsanāprakṣayo mokṣaḥ sā jīvanmuktir iṣyate ||
units.translation: When action ceases, thought ceases; from this comes the exhaustion of latent tendencies. The complete exhaustion of latent tendencies is liberation, and that is called liberation while living.
units.editionTranslation: With the cessation of selfish action the brooding on the sense-objects is stopped, which is followed by the destruction of desires. The destruction of desires is Liberation, and this is considered as Liberation-in-life

units.label: Verse 318
units.deva:
सद्वासनास्फूर्तिविजृम्भणे सति
ह्यसौ विलीनाप्यहमादिवासना ।
अतिप्रकृष्टाप्यरुणप्रभायां
विलीयते साधु यथा तमिस्रा ॥
units.iast:
sad-vāsanā-sphūrti-vijṛmbhaṇe sati
hy asau vilīnā api ahamādi-vāsanā |
ati-prakṛṣṭā api aruṇa-prabhāyāṃ
vilīyate sādhu yathā tamisrā ||
units.translation: When the disposition toward the Real strongly manifests, even deep-rooted tendencies of “I” and the rest dissolve completely, just as darkness dissolves in the glow of dawn.
units.editionTranslation: When the desire for realising Brahman has a marked manifestation, the egoistic desires readily vanish, as the most intense darkness effectively vanishes before the glow of the rising sun.

units.label: Verse 319
units.deva:
तमस्तमःकार्यमनर्थजालं
न दृश्यते सत्युदिते दिनेशे ।
तथाद्वयानन्दरसानुभूतौ
न वास्ति बन्धो न च दुःखगन्धः ॥
units.iast:
tamastamaḥkāryamanarthajālaṃ
na dṛśyate satyudite dineśe |
tathādvayānandarasānubhūtau
na vāsti bandho na ca duḥkhagandhaḥ ||
units.translation: Darkness and its web of harm are not seen once the sun has risen. Likewise, in the experience of nondual bliss, there is no bondage and not even a trace of suffering.
units.editionTranslation: Darkness and the numerous evils that attend on it are not noticed when the sun rises. Similarly, on the realisation of the Bliss Absolute, there is neither bondage nor the least trace of misery.

units.label: Verse 320
units.deva:
दृश्यं प्रतीतं प्रविलापयन्सन्
सन्मात्रमानन्दघनं विभावयन् ।
समाहितः सन्बहिरन्तरं वा
