कालं नयेथाः सति कर्मबन्धे ॥
units.iast:
dṛśyaṃ pratītaṃ pravilāpayan san
sanmātram ānandaghanaṃ vibhāvayan |
samāhitaḥ san bahiḥ antaram vā
kālaṃ nayethāḥ sati karmabandhe ||
units.translation: While karmic bondage remains, dissolve the perceived world, outer and inner, and contemplate pure Being alone, a mass of bliss. Remaining absorbed, spend your time in this way.
units.editionTranslation: Causing the external and internal universe, which are now perceived, to vanish, and meditating on the Reality, the Bliss Embodied, one should pass one’s time watchfully, if there be any residue of Prarabdha work left.

units.label: Verse 321
units.deva:
प्रमादो ब्रह्मनिष्ठायां न कर्तव्यः कदाचन ।
प्रमादो मृत्युरित्याह भगवान्ब्रह्मणः सुतः ॥
units.iast:
pramādo brahmaniṣṭhāyāṃ na kartavyaḥ kadācana |
pramādo mṛtyur ity āha bhagavān brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ ||
units.translation: Never be heedless in steadfastness to Brahman. The blessed son of Brahmā says: heedlessness is death.
units.editionTranslation: One should never be careless in one’s steadfastness to Brahman. Bhagavan Sanatkumara, who is Brahma’s son, has called inadvertence to be death itself.

units.label: Verse 322
units.deva:
न प्रमादादनर्थोऽन्यो ज्ञानिनः स्वस्वरूपतः ।
ततो मोहस्ततोऽहंधीस्ततो बन्धस्ततो व्यथा ॥
units.iast:
na pramādād anartho 'nyo jñāninaḥ svasvarūpataḥ |
tato mohas tato 'haṃdhīs tato bandhas tato vyathā ||
units.translation: For a knower, there is no calamity greater than heedlessness about one's own true nature. From it comes delusion; from delusion, the ego-notion; from that, bondage; and from bondage, suffering.
units.editionTranslation: There is no greater danger for the Jnanin than carelessness about his own real nature. From this comes delusion, thence egoism, this is followed by bondage, and then comes misery.

units.label: Verse 323
units.deva:
विषयाभिमुखं दृष्ट्वा विद्वांसम् अपि विस्मृतिः ।
विक्षेपयति धीदोषैर् योषा जारम् इव प्रियम् ॥
units.iast:
viṣayābhimukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidvāṃsam api vismṛtiḥ |
vikṣepayati dhīdoṣair yoṣā jāram iva priyam ||
units.translation: Seeing even a wise person turned toward sense-objects, forgetfulness distracts him through faults of the intellect, like a woman [distracting] her beloved lover.
units.editionTranslation: Finding even a wise man hankering after the sense-objects, oblivion torments him through the evil propensities of the Buddhi, as a woman does her doting paramour.

units.label: Verse 324
units.deva:
यथापकृष्टं शैवालं क्षणमात्रं न तिष्ठति ।
आवृणोति तथा माया प्राज्ञं वापि पराङ्मुखम् ॥
units.iast:
yathāpakṛṣṭaṃ śaivālaṃ kṣaṇamātraṃ na tiṣṭhati |
āvṛṇoti tathā māyā prājñaṃ vāpi parāṅmukham ||
units.translation: Just as moss, even when pushed aside, does not stay away for a moment but covers [the water] again, so māyā covers even a wise person who has turned away [from the Self].
units.editionTranslation: As sedge, even if removed, does not stay away for a moment, but covers the water again, so Maya or Nescience also covers even a wise man, if he is averse to meditation on the Self.

units.label: Verse 325
units.deva:
लक्ष्यच्युतं चेद्यदि चित्तमीषद्
बहिर्मुखं सन्निपतेत्ततस्ततः ।
प्रमादतः प्रच्युतकेलिकन्दुकः
सोपानपङ्क्तौ पतितो यथा तथा ॥
units.iast:
lakṣyacyutaṃ ced yadi cittaṃ īṣad
bahirmukhaṃ sannipatet tatas tataḥ |
pramādataḥ pracyuta-keli-kandukaḥ
sopāna-paṅktau patito yathā tathā ||
units.translation: If the mind slips even slightly from its goal and turns outward, it falls from one level to another, just as a play-ball, dropped through carelessness, falls down a flight of stairs.
units.editionTranslation: If the mind ever so slightly strays from the Ideal and becomes outgoing, then it goes down and down, just as a play-ball inadvertently dropped on the staircase bounds down from one step to another.

units.label: Verse 326
units.deva:
विषयेष्वाविशच्चेतः संकल्पयति तद्गुणान् ।
सम्यक्संकल्पनात्कामः कामात्पुंसः प्रवर्तनम् ॥
units.iast:
viṣayeṣv āviśac cetaḥ saṃkalpayati tadguṇān |
samyaksaṃkalpanāt kāmaḥ kāmāt puṃsaḥ pravartanam ||
units.translation: When the mind enters into sense-objects, it imagines their qualities. From clear imagining comes desire; from desire comes a person's action.
units.editionTranslation: The mind that is attached to the sense-objects reflects on their qualities; from mature reflection arises desire, and after desiring a man sets about having that thing.

units.label: Verse 327
units.deva:
अतः प्रमादान् न परोऽस्ति मृत्युः
विवेकिनो ब्रह्मविदः समाधौ ।
समाहितः सिद्धिमुपैति सम्यक्
समाहितात्मा भव सावधानः ॥
units.iast:
ataḥ pramādān na paro 'sti mṛtyur
vivekino brahmavidaḥ samādhau |
samāhitaḥ siddhim upaiti samyak
samāhitātmā bhava sāvadhānaḥ ||
units.translation: For the discerning knower of Brahman, there is no greater death than heedlessness in meditation. One who is absorbed attains success fully. Be absorbed and attentive.
units.editionTranslation: Hence to the discriminating knower of Brahman there is no worse death than inadvertence with regard to concentration. But the man who is concentrated attains complete success. (Therefore) carefully concentrate thy mind (on Brahman).

units.label: Verse 328
units.deva:
ततः स्वरूपविभ्रंशो विभ्रष्टस्तु पतत्यधः ।
पतितस्य विना नाशं पुनर्नारोह ईक्ष्यते ॥
units.iast:
tataḥ svarūpa-vibhraṃśo vibhraṣṭas tu pataty adhaḥ |
patitasya vinā nāśaṃ punar nāroha īkṣyate ||
units.translation: Then comes a fall from one's true nature; once fallen, one goes downward. For one who has fallen, a return to the ascent is not seen without complete ruin.
units.editionTranslation: Through inadvertence a man deviates from his real nature, and the man who has thus deviated falls. The fallen man comes to ruin, and is scarcely seen to rise again.

units.label: Verse 329
units.deva:
संकल्पं वर्जयेत्तस्मात्सर्वानर्थस्य कारणम् ।
जीवतो यस्य कैवल्यं विदेहे स च केवलः

यत् किंचित् पश्यतो भेदं भयं ब्रूते यजुःश्रुतिः ॥
units.iast:
saṃkalpaṃ varjayet tasmāt sarvānarthasya kāraṇam |
jīvato yasya kaivalyaṃ videhe sa ca kevalaḥ

yat kiṃcit paśyato bhedaṃ bhayaṃ brūte yajuḥśrutiḥ ||
units.translation: Therefore, give up intention-making, the cause of every harm. The one who is free while living remains alone when the body falls away. The Yajur Veda declares that fear arises for one who sees even the least difference.
units.editionTranslation: Therefore one should give up reflecting on the sense-objects, which is the root of all mischief. He who is completely aloof even while living, is alone aloof after the dissolution of the body. The Yajur-Veda declares that there is fear for one who sees the least bit of distinction.

units.label: Verse 330
units.deva:
यदा कदा वापि विपश्चिदेष
ब्रह्मण्य् अनन्तेऽप्य् अणुमात्रभेदम् ।
पश्यत्यथामुष्य भयं तदैव
यद्वीक्षितं भिन्नतया प्रमादात् ॥
units.iast:
yadā kadā vāpi vipaścid eṣa
brahmaṇy anante 'py aṇumātra-bhedam |
paśyaty athāmuṣya bhayaṃ tadaiva
yad vīkṣitaṃ bhinnatayā pramādāt ||
units.translation: Whenever a wise person sees even the slightest difference in infinite Brahman, fear arises for that person at once from what was seen as different through heedlessness.
units.editionTranslation: Whenever the wise man sees the least difference in the infinite Brahman, at once that which he sees as different through mistake, becomes a source of terror to him.

units.label: Verse 331
units.deva:
श्रुतिस्मृतिन्यायशतैर् निषिद्धे
दृश्येऽत्र यः स्वात्ममतिं करोति ।
उपैति दुःखोपरि दुःखजातं
निषिद्धकर्ता स मलिम्लुचो यथा ॥
units.iast:
śruti-smṛti-nyāya-śatair niṣiddhe
dṛśye 'tra yaḥ svātmamatiṃ karoti |
upaiti duḥkhopari duḥkha-jātaṃ
niṣiddha-kartā sa malimlucaḥ yathā ||
units.translation: Whoever takes as the Self the visible world here, denied by hundreds of scriptural texts, traditional teachings, and reasonings, meets suffering upon suffering, like a thief who does what is forbidden.

gloss.en: one who does what is forbidden

units.editionTranslation: He who identifies himself with the objective universe which has been denied by hundreds of Shrutis, Smritis and reasonings, experiences misery after misery, like a thief, for he does something forbidden.

units.label: Verse 332
units.deva:
सत्याभिसंधानरतो विमुक्तो
महत्त्वमात्मीयमुपैति नित्यम् ।
मिथ्याभिसन्धानरतस्तु नश्येद्
दृष्टं तदेतद्यदचौरचौरयोः ॥
units.iast:
satya-abhisandhāna-rato vimukto
mahattvam ātmīyam upaiti nityam |
mithyābhisandhāna-ratas tu naśyed
dṛṣṭaṃ tad etad yad acaura-caurayoḥ ||
units.translation: One devoted to truth and free [from ignorance] continually attains one's own greatness; but one devoted to falsehood perishes. This is seen in the case of the non-thief and the thief.

gloss.en: of the two: non-thief and thief

units.editionTranslation: He who has devoted himself to meditation on the Reality (Brahman) and is free from Nescience, attains to the eternal glory of the Atman. But he who dwells on the unreal (the universe) is destroyed. That this is so is evidenced in the case of one who is not a thief and one who is a thief.

units.label: Verse 333
units.deva:
यतिरसदनुसन्धिं बन्धहेतुं विहाय
स्वयमयमहमस्मीत्य् आत्मदृष्ट्यैव तिष्ठेत् ।
सुखयति ननु निष्ठा ब्रह्मणि स्वानुभूत्या
हरति परमविद्याकार्यदुःखं प्रतीतम् ॥
units.iast:
yatir asad-anusandhiṃ bandha-hetuṃ vihāya
svayam ayam aham asmīty ātma-dṛṣṭyaiva tiṣṭhet |
sukhayati nanu niṣṭhā brahmaṇi svānubhūtyā
harati paramavidyā-kārya-duḥkhaṃ pratītam ||
units.translation: The renunciate should leave inquiry into the unreal, the cause of bondage, and remain with the vision of the Self alone: “I myself am this.” Steadfastness in Brahman through direct experience brings happiness and removes the experienced suffering produced by ignorance.
units.editionTranslation: The Sannyasin should give up dwelling on the unreal, which causes bondage, and should always fix his thoughts on the Atman as "I myself am This". For the steadfastness in Brahman through the realisation of one’s identity with It gives rise to bliss and thoroughly removes the misery born of nescience, which one experiences (in the ignorant state).

units.label: Verse 334
units.deva:
बाह्यानुसन्धिः परिवर्धयेत्फलं
दुर्वासनाम् एव ततस्ततोऽधिकाम् ।
ज्ञात्वा विवेकैः परिहृत्य बाह्यं
स्वात्मानुसन्धिं विदधीत नित्यम् ॥
units.iast:
bāhyānusandhiḥ parivardhayet phalaṃ
durvāsanām eva tatas tato 'dhikām |
jñātvā vivekaiḥ parihṛtya bāhyaṃ
svātmānusandhiṃ vidadhīta nityam ||
units.translation: Dwelling on external things increases their fruit: harmful latent tendencies, more and more. Knowing this through discernment, one should turn away from externals and continually pursue inquiry into one's own Self.
units.editionTranslation: The dwelling on external objects will only intensify its fruits, viz. furthering evil propensities, which grow worse and worse. Knowing this through discrimination, one should avoid external objects and constantly apply oneself to meditation on the Atman.

units.label: Verse 335
units.deva:
बाह्ये निरुद्धे मनसः प्रसन्नता
मनःप्रसादे परमात्मदर्शनम् ।
तस्मिन्सुदृष्टे भवबन्धनाशो
बहिर्निरोधः पदवी विमुक्तेः ॥
units.iast:
bāhye niruddhe manasaḥ prasannatā
manaḥ-prasāde paramātma-darśanam |
tasmin sudṛṣṭe bhava-bandha-nāśo
bahir-nirodhaḥ padavī vimukteḥ ||
units.translation: When the external is restrained, the mind becomes clear; when the mind is clear, the Supreme Self is seen. When that is clearly seen, bondage to worldly existence ends. Restraining the external is the path to liberation.
units.editionTranslation: When the external world is shut out, the mind is cheerful, and cheerfulness of the mind brings on the vision of the Paramatman. When It is perfectly realised, the chain of birth and death is broken. Hence the shutting out of the external world is the stepping-stone to Liberation.

units.label: Verse 336
units.deva:
कः पण्डितः सन्सदसद्विवेकी
श्रुतिप्रमाणः परमार्थदर्शी ।
जानन्हि कुर्यादसतोऽवलम्बं
स्वपातहेतोः शिशुवन्मुमुक्षुः ॥
units.iast:
kaḥ paṇḍitaḥ san sad-asad-vivekī
śruti-pramāṇaḥ paramārtha-darśī |
jānan hi kuryād asato 'valambaṃ
sva-pāta-hetoḥ śiśuvat mumukṣuḥ ||
units.translation: Knowing this, what seeker of liberation—discerning the real from the unreal, taking scripture as authority, and seeing the highest truth—would knowingly take recourse to the unreal, like a child, for the sake of his own fall?
units.editionTranslation: Where is the man who being learned, able to discriminate the real from the unreal, believing the Vedas as authority, fixing his gaze on the Atman, the Supreme Reality, and being a seeker after Liberation, will, like a child, consciously have recourse to the unreal (the universe) which will cause his fall ?

units.label: Verse 337
units.deva:
देहादिसंसक्तिमतो न मुक्तिः
मुक्तस्य देहाद्यभिमत्यभावः ।
सुप्तस्य नो जागरणं न जाग्रतः
स्वप्नस्तयोर् भिन्नगुणाश्रयत्वात् ॥
units.iast:
dehādi-saṃsaktimato na muktiḥ
muktasya dehādy-abhimaty-abhāvaḥ |
suptasya no jāgaraṇaṃ na jāgrataḥ
svapnas tayoḥ bhinna-guṇāśrayatvāt ||
units.translation: One attached to the body and so on has no liberation; the liberated one has no identification with the body and so on. A sleeper is not awake, and the waking person does not dream, because the two rest on different qualities.

gloss.en: because they depend on; rest on

units.editionTranslation: There is no Liberation for one who has attachment to the body etc., and the liberated man has no identification with the body etc. The sleeping man is not awake, nor is the waking man asleep, for these two states are contradictory in nature.

units.label: Verse 338
units.deva:
अन्तर्बहिः स्वं स्थिरजङ्गमेषु
ज्ञात्वात्मनाधारतया विलोक्य ।
त्यक्ताखिलोपाधिरखण्डरूपः
पूर्णात्मना यः स्थित एष मुक्तः ॥
units.iast:
antarbahiḥ svaṃ sthira-jaṅgameṣu
jñātvā ātmanā ādhāratayā vilokya |
tyaktākhilopādhiḥ akhaṇḍa-rūpaḥ
pūrṇātmanā yaḥ sthita eṣa muktaḥ ||
units.translation: Knowing the Self within and without, in moving and still things, and seeing it as their support, whoever abandons all limiting adjuncts and abides as undivided, as the complete Self, is liberated.
units.editionTranslation: He is free who, knowing through his mind the Self in moving and unmoving objects and observing It as their substratum, gives up all superimpositions and remains as the Absolute and the infinite Self.

units.label: Verse 339
units.deva:
सर्वात्मना बन्धविमुक्तिहेतुः
सर्वात्मभावान् न परोऽस्ति कश्चित् ।
दृश्याग्रहे सत्युपपद्यतेऽसौ
सर्वात्मभावोऽस्य सदात्मनिष्ठया ॥
units.iast:
sarvātmanā bandha-vimukti-hetuḥ
sarvātmabhāvān na paro 'sti kaścit |
dṛśyāgrahe sati upapadyate 'sau
sarvātmabhāvo 'sya sadātma-niṣṭhayā ||
units.translation: Seeing all as the Self is the way to freedom from bondage; there is nothing higher than this state of being the Self of all. This universal Selfhood arises when the seen is no longer grasped, through constant abidance in the true Self.

gloss.en: from the state of being the Self of all
the state of being the Self of all

units.editionTranslation: To realise the whole universe as the Self is the means of getting rid of bondage. There is nothing higher than identifying the universe with the Self. One realises this state by excluding the objective world through steadfastness in the eternal Atman.

units.label: Verse 340
units.deva:
दृश्यस्याग्रहणं कथं नु घटते देहात्मना तिष्ठतो
बाह्यार्थानुभवप्रसक्तमनसस्तत्तत्क्रियां कुर्वतः ।
संन्यस्ताखिल-धर्म-कर्म-विषयैर् नित्यात्मनिष्ठापरैः
तत्त्वज्ञैः करणीयम् आत्मनि सदानन्देच्छुभिर्यत्नतः ॥
units.iast:
dṛśyasyāgrahaṇaṃ kathaṃ nu ghaṭate dehātmanā tiṣṭhataḥ
bāhyārthānubhava-prasakta-manasaḥ tat-tat-kriyāṃ kurvataḥ |
saṃnyastākhila-dharma-karma-viṣayair nityātmaniṣṭhāparaiḥ
tattvajñaiḥ karaṇīyam ātmani sadānandecchubhir yatnataḥ ||
units.translation: How can non-apprehension of the seen world be possible for one who remains identified with the body, whose mind is attached to experiencing external objects, and who performs the corresponding actions? It should be practiced diligently in the Self by knowers of truth who have renounced all duties, actions, and objects, are devoted solely to the eternal Self, and seek abiding bliss.

gloss.en: identified with the body as self

units.editionTranslation: How is the exclusion of the objective world possible for one who lives identified with the body, whose mind is attached to the perception of external objects, and who performs various acts for that end ? This exclusion should be carefully practised by sages who have renounced all kinds of duties and actions and objects, who are passionately devoted to the eternal Atman, and who wish to possess an undying bliss.

units.label: Verse 341
units.deva:
सर्वात्मसिद्धये भिक्षोः कृतश्रवणकर्मणः ।
समाधिं विदधात्येषा शान्तो दान्त इति श्रुतिः ॥
units.iast:
sarvātma-siddhaye bhikṣoḥ kṛta-śravaṇa-karmaṇaḥ |
samādhiṃ vidadhāty eṣā śrutiḥ śānto dānta iti ||
units.translation: This scripture prescribes meditation for the mendicant who has completed the practice of hearing, for realizing the Self of all: “peaceful, self-controlled.”
units.editionTranslation: To the Sannyasin who has gone through the act of hearing, the Shruti passage, "Calm, self-controlled." Etc., prescribes Samadhi for realising the identity of the universe with the Self.

units.label: Verse 342
units.deva:
आरूढशक्तेरहमो विनाशः
कर्तुं न शक्यः सहसापि पण्डितैः ।
ये निर्विकल्पाख्यसमाधिनिश्चलाः
तानन्तरानन्तभवा हि वासनाः ॥
units.iast:
ārūḍhaśakter ahamo vināśaḥ
kartuṃ na śakyaḥ sahasā api paṇḍitaiḥ |
ye nirvikalpākhya-samādhi-niścalāḥ
tān antarā ananta-bhavā hi vāsanāḥ ||
units.translation: When ego has grown strong, its destruction cannot be accomplished suddenly, even by the learned. Apart from those steady in the absorption called nirvikalpa, latent tendencies from countless births remain.
units.editionTranslation: Even wise men cannot suddenly destroy egoism after it has once become strong, barring those who are perfectly calm through the Nirvikalpa Samadhi. Desires are verily the effect of innumerable births.

units.label: Verse 343
units.deva:
अहंबुद्ध्यैव मोहिन्या योजयित्वावृतेर्बलात् ।
विक्षेपशक्तिः पुरुषं विक्षेपयति तद्गुणैः ॥
units.iast:
ahaṃ-buddhyaiva mohinyā yojayitvā āvṛter balāt |
vikṣepa-śaktiḥ puruṣaṃ vikṣepayati tadguṇaiḥ ||
units.translation: By the force of the veiling power, the projecting power joins a person to the deluding ego-thought and distracts him through its qualities.
units.editionTranslation: The projecting power, through the aid of the veiling power, connects a man with the siren of an egoistic idea, and distracts him through the attributes of that.

units.label: Verse 344
units.deva:
विक्षेपशक्तिविजयो विषमो विधातुं
निःशेषमावरणशक्तिनिवृत्त्यभावे ।
दृग्दृश्ययोः स्फुटपयोजलवद्विभागे
नश्येत्तदावरणम् आत्मनि च स्वभावात्

निःसंशयेन भवति प्रतिबन्धशून्यो
विक्षेपणं न हि तदा यदि चेन्मृषार्थे ॥
units.iast:
vikṣepa-śakti-vijayo viṣamo vidhātuṃ
niḥśeṣam āvaraṇa-śakti-nivṛtty-abhāve |
dṛg-dṛśyayoḥ sphuṭa-payo-jalavat-vibhāge
naśyet tad-āvaraṇam ātmani ca svabhāvāt ||
niḥsaṃśayena bhavati pratibandha-śūnyo
vikṣepaṇaṃ na hi tadā yadi cen mṛṣārthe ||
units.translation: Conquering the projecting power is difficult until the veiling power has been completely removed. When seer and seen are clearly distinguished, like milk and water, that veil over the Self disappears by its nature. Then projection is surely free of obstruction, if the object is known to be unreal.
units.editionTranslation: It is extremely difficult to conquer the projecting power unless the veiling power is perfectly rooted out. And that covering over the Atman naturally vanishes when the subject is perfectly distinguished from the objects, like milk from water. But the victory is undoubtedly (complete and) free from obstacles when there is no oscillation of the mind due to the unreal sense-objects.

units.label: Verse 345
units.deva:
सम्यग्विवेकः स्फुटबोधजन्यो
विभज्य दृग्दृश्यपदार्थतत्त्वम् ।
छिनत्ति मायाकृतमोहबन्धं
यस्माद्विमुक्तस्तु पुनर्न संसृतिः ॥
units.iast:
samyag-vivekaḥ sphuṭa-bodha-janyaḥ
vibhajya dṛg-dṛśya-padārtha-tattvam |
chinatti māyā-kṛta-moha-bandhaṃ
yasmād vimuktas tu punar na saṃsṛtiḥ ||
units.translation: Clear discrimination, born of direct understanding, distinguishes the true nature of the seer and the seen, and cuts the bond of delusion made by māyā. Once freed from it, one does not return to saṃsāra.
units.editionTranslation: Perfect discrimination brought on by direct realisation distinguishes the true nature of the subject from that of the object, and breaks the bond of delusion created by Maya; and there is no more transmigration for one who has been freed from this.

units.label: Verse 346
units.deva:
परावरैकत्वविवेकवह्निः
दहत्यविद्यागहनं ह्यशेषम् ।
किं स्यात्पुनः संसरणस्य बीजं
अद्वैतभावं समुपेयुषोऽस्य ॥
units.iast:
parāvaraikatva-viveka-vahniḥ
dahaty avidyā-gahanaṃ hy aśeṣam |
kiṃ syāt punaḥ saṃsaraṇasya bījaṃ
advaita-bhāvaṃ samupeyuṣo 'sya ||
units.translation: The fire of discernment of the oneness of the higher and lower burns the dense forest of ignorance completely. For one who has attained nonduality, what seed of transmigration could remain?
units.editionTranslation: The knowledge of the identity of the Jiva and Brahman entirely consumes the impenetrable forest of Avidya or Nescience. For one who has realised the state of Oneness, is there any seed left for future transmigration ?

units.label: Verse 347
units.deva:
आवरणस्य निवृत्तिर्भवति हि सम्यक्पदार्थदर्शनतः ।
मिथ्याज्ञानविनाशस्तद्विक्षेपजनितदुःखनिवृत्तिः ॥
units.iast:
āvaraṇasya nivṛttir bhavati hi samyak-padārtha-darśanataḥ |
mithyā-jñāna-vināśas tad-vikṣepa-janita-duḥkha-nivṛttiḥ ||
units.translation: The veil is indeed removed through clear seeing of reality. From this follows the destruction of false knowledge and the cessation of suffering produced by its projection.
units.editionTranslation: The veil that hides Truth vanishes only when the Reality is fully realised. (Thence follow) the destruction of false knowledge and the cessation of misery brought about by its distracting influence.

units.label: Verse 348
units.deva:
एतत्त्रितयं दृष्टं सम्यग्रज्जुस्वरूपविज्ञानात् ।
तस्माद्वस्तुसतत्त्वं ज्ञातव्यं बन्धमुक्तये विदुषा ॥
units.iast:
etat-tritayaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ samyag-rajju-svarūpa-vijñānāt |
tasmād vastu-satattvaṃ jñātavyaṃ bandha-muktaye viduṣā ||
units.translation: This triad is seen when the true nature of a rope is rightly known. Therefore, to be free from bondage, the wise person should know the true reality of things.
units.editionTranslation: These three are observed in the case of a rope when its real nature is fully known. Therefore the wise man should know the real nature of things for the breaking of his bonds.

units.label: Verses 349–350
units.deva:
अयोऽग्नियोगाद् इव सत्समन्वयान्
मात्रादिरूपेण विजृम्भते धीः ।
तत्कार्यमेतद्द्वितयं यतो मृषा
दृष्टं भ्रमस्वप्नमनोरथेषु ॥

ततो विकाराः प्रकृतेरहंमुखा
देहावसाना विषयाश्च सर्वे ।
क्षणेऽन्यथाभावितया ह्यमीषाम्
असत्त्वमात्मा तु कदापि नान्यथा ॥
units.iast:
ayo 'gni-yogād iva sat-samanvayān
mātrādi-rūpeṇa vijṛmbhate dhīḥ |
tat-kāryam etad dvitayaṃ yato mṛṣā
dṛṣṭaṃ bhrama-svapna-manoratheṣu ||

tato vikārāḥ prakṛter ahaṃ-mukhā
dehāvasānā viṣayāś ca sarve |
kṣaṇe 'nyathābhāvitayā hy amīṣām
asattvam ātmā tu kadāpi nānyathā ||
units.translation: Like iron glowing through contact with fire, the intellect manifests in the form of subtle elements and the rest through association with Being. This pair, its product, is false, as seen in delusion, dream, and imagination. From this, the modifications of prakṛti—from ego to body—and all objects are unreal, since they change from moment to moment; the Self, however, never changes.
units.editionTranslation: Like iron manifesting as sparks through contact with fire, the Buddhi manifests itself as knower and known through the inherence of Brahman. As these two (knower and known), the effects of the Buddhi, are observed to be unreal in the case of delusion, dream and fancy, similarly, the modifications of the Prakriti, from egoism down to the body and all sense-objects are also unreal. Their unreality is verily due to their being subject to change every moment. But the Atman never changes.

units.label: Verse 351
units.deva:
नित्याद्वयाखण्डचिदेकरूपो
बुद्ध्यादिसाक्षी सदसद्विलक्षणः ।
अहंपदप्रत्ययलक्षितार्थः
प्रत्यक् सदानन्दघनः परात्मा ॥
units.iast:
nityādvaya-akhaṇḍa-cid-eka-rūpo
buddhyādi-sākṣī sat-asat-vilakṣaṇaḥ |
ahaṃ-pada-pratyaya-lakṣitārthaḥ
pratyak sadānanda-ghanaḥ parātmā ||
units.translation: The Supreme Self is eternal, nondual, indivisible consciousness, one in nature: the witness of the intellect and the rest, distinct from being and non-being, the meaning indicated by the notion of “I,” inward, a mass of ever-present bliss.
units.editionTranslation: The Supreme Self is ever of the nature of eternal, indivisible knowledge, one without a second, the Witness of the Buddhi and the rest, distinct from the gross and subtle, the implied meaning of the term and idea "I", the embodiment of inward, eternal bliss.

units.label: Verse 352
units.deva:
इत्थं विपश्चित्सदसद्विभज्य
निश्चित्य तत्त्वं निजबोधदृष्ट्या ।
ज्ञात्वा स्वमात्मानमखण्डबोधं
तेभ्यो विमुक्तः स्वयम् एव शाम्यति ॥
units.iast:
itthaṃ vipaścit sat-asat vibhajya
niścitya tattvaṃ nija-bodha-dṛṣṭyā |
jñātvā svam ātmānam akhaṇḍa-bodhaṃ
tebhyo vimuktaḥ svayam eva śāmyati ||
units.translation: In this way, the wise one distinguishes the real from the unreal and determines the truth through direct insight. Knowing one's own Self as undivided awareness and freed from those [notions], one becomes peaceful.
units.editionTranslation: The wise man, discriminating thus the real and the unreal, ascertaining the Truth through his illuminative insight, and realising his own Self which is Knowledge Absolute, gets rid of the obstructions and directly attains Peace.

units.label: Verse 353
units.deva:
अज्ञानहृदयग्रन्थेर्निःशेषविलयस्तदा ।
समाधिनाविकल्पेन यदाद्वैतात्मदर्शनम् ॥
units.iast:
ajñāna-hṛdaya-granther niḥśeṣa-vilayas tadā |
samādhinā avikalpena yadā advaita-ātma-darśanam ||
units.translation: Then the heart-knot of ignorance is dissolved completely, when the nondual Self is seen through thought-free samādhi.
units.editionTranslation: When the Atman, the One without a second, is realised by means of the Nirvikalpa Samadhi, then the heart’s knot of ignorance is totally destroyed.

units.label: Verse 354
units.deva:
त्वमहमिदमितीयं कल्पना बुद्धिदोषात्
प्रभवति परमात्मन्यद्वये निर्विशेषे ।
प्रविलसति समाधावस्य सर्वो विकल्पो
विलयनमुपगच्छेद्वस्तुतत्त्वावधृत्या ॥
units.iast:
tvam aham idam iti iyaṃ kalpanā buddhi-doṣāt
prabhavati paramātmany advaye nirviśeṣe |
pravilasati samādhāv asya sarvo vikalpo
vilayanam upagacched vastu-tattvāvadhṛtyā ||
units.translation: This imagination—“you,” “I,” and “this”—arises from a defect of the intellect even in the nondual, undifferentiated Supreme Self. When that [Self] shines in samādhi, every thought-construct dissolves through firm discernment of reality.
units.editionTranslation: Such imaginations as "thou", "I" or "this" take place through the defects of the Buddhi. But when the Paramatman, the Absolute, the One without a second, manifests Itself in Samadhi, all such imaginations are dissolved for the aspirant, through the realisation of the truth of Brahman.

units.label: Verse 355
units.deva:
शान्तो दान्तः परमुपरतः क्षान्तियुक्तः समाधिं
कुर्वन्नित्यं कलयति यतिः स्वस्य सर्वात्मभावम् ।
तेनाविद्यातिमिरजनितान्साधु दग्ध्वा विकल्पान्
ब्रह्माकृत्या निवसति सुखं निष्क्रियो निर्विकल्पः ॥
units.iast:
śānto dāntaḥ param uparataḥ kṣānti-yuktaḥ samādhiṃ
kurvan nityaṃ kalayati yatiḥ svasya sarvātma-bhāvam |
tenāvidyā-timira-janitān sādhu dagdhvā vikalpān
brahmākṛtyā nivasati sukhaṃ niṣkriyo nirvikalpaḥ ||
units.translation: Calm, self-controlled, fully withdrawn, and patient, the renunciate continually practices samādhi and contemplates his own nature as the Self of all. Thoroughly burning the thought-constructs born of ignorance's darkness, he dwells happily as Brahman, inactive and free of thought.

gloss.en: nature as the Self of all

units.editionTranslation: The Sannyasin, calm, self-controlled, perfectly retiring from the sense-world, forbearing, and devoting himself to the practice of Samadhi, always reflects on his own self being the Self of the whole universe. Destroying completely by this means the imaginations which are due to the gloom of ignorance, he lives blissfully as Brahman, free from action and the oscillations of the mind.

units.label: Verse 356
units.deva:
समाहिता ये प्रविलाप्य बाह्यं
श्रोत्रादि चेतः स्वमहं चिदात्मनि ।
त एव मुक्ता भवपाशबन्धैः
नान्ये तु पारोक्ष्यकथाभिधायिनः ॥
units.iast:
samāhitā ye pravilāpya bāhyaṃ
śrotrādi cetaḥ svaṃ aham cidātmani |
ta eva muktā bhava-pāśa-bandhaiḥ
nānye tu pārokṣya-kathābhidhāyinaḥ ||
units.translation: Only those who, absorbed, dissolve the external, the ear and other senses, the mind, and their own ego into the Self of consciousness are freed from the bonds of saṃsāra; not others who speak only of indirect knowledge.
units.editionTranslation: Those alone are free from the bondage of transmigration who, attaining Samadhi, have merged the objective world, the sense-organs, the mind, nay, the very ego, in the Atman, the Knowledge Absolute – and none else, who but dabble in second-hand talks.

units.label: Verse 357
units.deva:
उपाधिभेदात्स्वयम् एव भिद्यते
चोपाध्यपोहे स्वयम् एव केवलः ।
तस्मादुपाधेर्विलयाय विद्वान्
वसेत्सदाकल्पसमाधिनिष्ठया ॥
units.iast:
upādhi-bhedāt svayam eva bhidyate
ca upādhi-apohe svayam eva kevalaḥ |
tasmād upādher vilayāya vidvān
vaset sadā akalpa-samādhi-niṣṭhayā ||
units.translation: Because of differences in limiting adjuncts, [the Self] appears divided by itself; when the adjuncts are removed, it is itself alone. Therefore, to dissolve the adjuncts, the wise person should remain steadily established in non-conceptual samādhi.
units.editionTranslation: Through the diversity of the supervening conditions (Upadhis), a man is apt to think of himself as also full of diversity; but with the removal of these he is again his own Self, the immutable. Therefore the wise man should ever devote himself to the practice of Nirvikalpa Samadhi, for the dissolution of the Upadhis.

units.label: Verse 358
units.deva:
सति सक्तो नरो याति सद्भावं ह्येकनिष्ठया ।
कीटको भ्रमरं ध्यायन् भ्रमरत्वाय कल्पते ॥
units.iast:
sati sakto naro yāti sadbhāvaṃ hy eka-niṣṭhayā |
kīṭako bhramaraṃ dhyāyan bhramaratvāya kalpate ||
units.translation: A person attached to Being reaches the state of Being through one-pointed steadfastness, just as a worm, meditating on a bee, is transformed into bee-nature.
units.editionTranslation: The man who is attached to the Real becomes Real, through his one-pointed devotion. Just as the cockroach thinking intently on the Bhramara is transformed into a Bhramara.

units.label: Verse 359
units.deva:
क्रियान्तरासक्तिमपास्य कीटको
ध्यायन्नलित्वं ह्यलिभावमृच्छति ।
तथैव योगी परमात्मतत्त्वं
ध्यात्वा समायाति तदेकनिष्ठया ॥
units.iast:
kriyāntarāsaktim apāsya kīṭako
dhyāyan alitvaṃ hy ali-bhāvam ṛcchati |
tathaiva yogī paramātma-tattvaṃ
dhyātvā samāyāti tad-eka-niṣṭhayā ||
units.translation: Letting go of attachment to other activities, the worm, meditating on the bee, indeed reaches the state of a bee. In the same way, the yogin reaches the truth of the Supreme Self by meditating on it with one-pointed steadfastness.
units.editionTranslation: Just as the cockroach, giving up the attachment to all other actions, thinks intently on the Bhramara and becomes transformed into that worm, exactly in the same manner the Yogi, meditating on the truth of the Paramatman, attains to It through his one-pointed devotion to that.

units.label: Verse 360
units.deva:
अतीव सूक्ष्मं परमात्मतत्त्वं
न स्थूलदृष्ट्या प्रतिपत्तुमर्हति ।
समाधिनात्यन्तसुसूक्ष्मवृत्त्या
ज्ञातव्यमार्यैर् अतिशुद्धबुद्धिभिः ॥
units.iast:
atīva sūkṣmaṃ paramātma-tattvaṃ
na sthūla-dṛṣṭyā pratipattum arhati |
samādhinā atyanta-su-sūkṣma-vṛttyā
jñātavyam āryair atiśuddha-buddhibhiḥ ||
units.translation: The truth of the Supreme Self is exceedingly subtle and cannot be grasped by gross perception. It is to be known through samādhi by noble people of exceptionally pure intellect, with a very subtle mental movement.
units.editionTranslation: The truth of the Paramatman is extremely subtle, and cannot be reached by the gross outgoing tendency of the mind. It is only accessible to noble souls with perfectly pure minds, by means of Samadhi brought on by an extraordinary fineness of the mental state.

units.label: Verse 361
units.deva:
यथा सुवर्णं पुटपाकशोधितं
त्यक्त्वा मलं स्वात्मगुणं समृच्छति ।
तथा मनः सत्त्वरजस्तमोमलं
ध्यानेन सन्त्यज्य समेति तत्त्वम् ॥
units.iast:
yathā suvarṇaṃ puṭapākaśodhitaṃ
tyaktvā malaṃ svātmaguṇaṃ samṛcchati |
tathā manaḥ sattvarajastamomalaṃ
dhyānena santyajya sameti tattvam ||
units.translation: Just as gold purified by crucible heating, having cast off its impurity, attains its own natural quality, so the mind, by meditation, abandoning the impurity of sattva, rajas, and tamas, reaches Reality.

gloss.en: purified by heating in a crucible
the impurity of sattva, rajas, and tamas

units.editionTranslation: As gold purified by thorough heating on the fire gives up its impurities and attains to its own lustre, so the mind, through meditation, gives up its impurities of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, and attains to the reality of Brahman.

units.label: Verse 362
units.deva:
निरन्तराभ्यासवशात्तदित्थं
पक्वं मनो ब्रह्मणि लीयते यदा ।
तदा समाधिः सविकल्पवर्जितः
स्वतोऽद्वयानन्दरसानुभावकः ॥
units.iast:
nirantarābhyāsavaśāt tad itthaṃ
pakvaṃ mano brahmaṇi līyate yadā |
tadā samādhiḥ savikalpavarjitaḥ
svato 'dvayānandarasānubhāvakaḥ ||
units.translation: Through the force of uninterrupted practice, when the mind has thus ripened and dissolves in Brahman, then samādhi free from thought-constructs arises, itself experiencing the taste of nondual bliss.

gloss.en: through the force of uninterrupted practice
experiencing the taste of nondual bliss

units.editionTranslation: When the mind, thus purified by constant practice, is merged in Brahman, then Samadhi passes on from the Savikalpa to the Nirvikalpa stage, and leads directly to the realisation of the Bliss of Brahman, the One without a second.

units.label: Verse 363
units.deva:
समाधिनानेन समस्तवासना-
ग्रन्थेर्विनाशोऽखिलकर्मनाशः ।
अन्तर्बहिः सर्वत एव सर्वदा
स्वरूपविस्फूर्तिरयत्नतः स्यात् ॥
units.iast:
samādhinānena samastavāsanā-
granthervināśo'khilakarmanāśaḥ |
antarbahiḥ sarvata eva sarvadā
svarūpavisphūrtirayatnataḥ syāt ||
units.translation: Through this samādhi, the knot of all latent tendencies is destroyed, all karma is destroyed, and the manifestation of one’s own nature occurs effortlessly, everywhere, within and without, always.

gloss.en: of the knot of all latent tendencies
the manifestation of one’s own nature

units.editionTranslation: By this Samadhi are destroyed all desires which are like knots, all work is at an end, and inside and out there takes place everywhere and always the spontaneous manifestation of one’s real nature.

units.label: Verse 364
units.deva:
श्रुतेः शतगुणं विद्यान्मननं मननादपि ।
निदिध्यासं लक्षगुणमनन्तं निर्विकल्पकम् ॥
units.iast:
śruteḥ śataguṇaṃ vidyān mananaṃ mananād api |
nididhyāsaṃ lakṣaguṇam anantaṃ nirvikalpakam ||
units.translation: One should know reflection to be a hundredfold greater than hearing, deep contemplation a hundred-thousandfold greater even than reflection, and nirvikalpa samādhi to be boundless.
units.editionTranslation: Reflection should be considered a hundred times superior to hearing, and meditation a hundred thousand times superior even to reflection, but the Nirvikalpa Samadhi is infinite in its results.

units.label: Verse 365
units.deva:
निर्विकल्पकसमाधिना स्फुटं
ब्रह्मतत्त्वमवगम्यते ध्रुवम् ।
नान्यथा चलतया मनोगतेः
प्रत्ययान्तरविमिश्रितं भवेत् ॥
units.iast:
nirvikalpakasamādhinā sphuṭaṃ
brahmatattvamavagamyate dhruvam |
nānyathā calatayā manogateḥ
pratyayāntaravimiśritaṃ bhavet ||
units.translation: Through nirvikalpa samādhi, the truth of Brahman is clearly and certainly realized. Otherwise, because the mind is restless in its movement, [that realization] would be mixed with other cognitions.
units.editionTranslation: By the Nirvikalpa Samadhi the truth of Brahman is clearly and definitely realised, but not otherwise, for then the mind, being unstable by nature, is apt to be mixed up with other perceptions.

units.label: Verse 366
units.deva:
अतः समाधत्स्व यतेन्द्रियः सन्
निरन्तरं शान्तमनाः प्रतीचि ।
विध्वंसय ध्वान्तमनाद्यविद्यया
कृतं सदेकत्वविलोकनेन ॥
units.iast:
ataḥ samādhatsva yatendriyaḥ san
nirantaraṃ śāntamanāḥ pratīci |
vidhvaṃsaya dhvāntamanādyavidyayā
kṛtaṃ sadekatvavilokanena ||
units.translation: Therefore, with the senses controlled and the mind always peaceful, concentrate on the inner Self. Destroy the darkness created by beginningless ignorance by seeing the oneness of Existence.
units.editionTranslation: Hence with the mind calm and the senses controlled always drown the mind in the Supreme Self that is within, and through the realisation of thy identity with that Reality destroy the darkness created by Nescience, which is without beginning.

units.label: Verse 367
units.deva:
योगस्य प्रथमद्वारं वाङ्निरोधोऽपरिग्रहः ।
निराशा च निरीहा च नित्यमेकान्तशीलता ॥
units.iast:
yogasya prathamadvāraṃ vāṅnirodho'parigrahaḥ |
nirāśā ca nirīhā ca nityamekāntaśīlatā ||
units.translation: The first gate of yoga is restraint of speech and non-possessiveness, freedom from expectation and striving, and a constant disposition toward solitude.
units.editionTranslation: The first steps to Yoga are control of speech, non-receiving of gifts, entertaining of no expectations, freedom from activity, and always living in a retired place.

units.label: Verse 368
units.deva:
एकान्तस्थितिरिन्द्रियोपरमणे हेतुर्दमश्चेतसः
संरोधे करणं शमेन विलयं यायादहंवासना ।
तेनानन्दरसानुभूतिरचला ब्राह्मी सदा योगिनः
तस्माच्चित्तनिरोध एव सततं कार्यः प्रयत्नो मुनेः ॥
units.iast:
ekāntasthitirindriyoparamaṇe hetur damaś cetasaḥ
saṃrodhe karaṇaṃ śamena vilayaṃ yāyād ahaṃvāsanā |
tenānandarasānubhūtiracalā brāhmī sadā yoginaḥ
tasmāc cittanirodha eva satataṃ kāryaḥ prayatno muneḥ ||
units.translation: Abiding in solitude is a cause of sense-withdrawal; self-restraint is the means for restraining the mind. Through tranquility the ego-tendency should dissolve; thereby the yogi always has an unshaken experience of the essence of Brahman-bliss. Therefore, the sage should continually strive for restraint of mind alone.

gloss.en: for the withdrawal of the senses
experience of the essence of bliss

units.editionTranslation: Living in a retired place serves to control the sense-organs, control of the senses helps to control the mind, through control of the mind egoism is destroyed; and this again gives the Yogi an unbroken realisation of the Bliss of Brahman. Therefore the man of reflection should always strive only to control the mind.

units.label: Verse 369
units.deva:
वाचं नियच्छात्मनि तं नियच्छ
बुद्धौ धियं यच्छ च बुद्धिसाक्षिणि ।
तं चापि पूर्णात्मनि निर्विकल्पे
विलाप्य शान्तिं परमां भजस्व ॥
units.iast:
vācaṃ niyacchātmani taṃ niyaccha
buddhau dhiyaṃ yaccha ca buddhisākṣiṇi |
taṃ cāpi pūrṇātmani nirvikalpe
vilāpya śāntiṃ paramāṃ bhajasva ||
units.translation: Restrain speech in the mind; restrain that [mind] in the intellect; restrain the intellect in the witness of the intellect. Having dissolved that too in the complete, thought-free Self, seek supreme peace.

gloss.en: in the inner self; here, the mind
in the witness of the intellect

units.editionTranslation: Restrain speech in the Manas, and restrain Manas in the Buddhi; this again restrain in the witness of Buddhi, and merging that also in the Infinite Absolute Self, attain to supreme Peace.

units.label: Verse 370
units.deva:
देहप्राणेन्द्रियमनोबुद्ध्यादिभिरुपाधिभिः ।
यैर् यैर् वृत्तेः समायोगस्तत्तद्भावोऽस्य योगिनः ॥
units.iast:
dehaprāṇendriyamanobuddhyādibhirupādhibhiḥ |
yair yair vṛtteḥ samāyogastattadbhāvo 'sya yoginaḥ ||
units.translation: With whichever limiting adjuncts—the body, vital breath, senses, mind, intellect, and the rest—the mind’s mode is associated, the yogi takes on that corresponding state.

gloss.en: with limiting adjuncts such as body, vital breath, senses, mind, intellect, and the rest

units.editionTranslation: The body, Pranas, organs, manas, Buddhi and the rest – with whichsoever of these supervening adjuncts the mind is associated, the Yogi is transformed, as it were, into that.

units.label: Verse 371
units.deva:
तन्निवृत्त्या मुनेः सम्यक् सर्वोपरमणं सुखम् ।
संदृश्यते सदानन्दरसानुभवविप्लवः ॥
units.iast:
tannivṛttyā muneḥ samyak sarvoparamaṇaṃ sukham |
saṃdṛśyate sadānandarasānubhavaviplavaḥ ||
units.translation: Through the cessation of that, the sage clearly sees the bliss of complete cessation of everything as a flood of experience of the essence of eternal bliss.

gloss.en: a flood of experience of the essence of eternal bliss

units.editionTranslation: When this is stopped, the man of reflection is found to be easily detached from everything, and to get the experience of an abundance of everlasting Bliss.

units.label: Verse 372
units.deva:
अन्तस्त्यागो बहिस्त्यागो विरक्तस्यैव युज्यते ।
त्यजत्यन्तर्बहिःसङ्गं विरक्तस्तु मुमुक्षया ॥
units.iast:
antastyāgo bahistyāgo viraktasyaiva yujyate |
tyajatyantarbahiḥsaṅgaṃ viraktastu mumukṣayā ||
units.translation: Inner and outer renunciation are fitting only for the dispassionate person; the dispassionate person gives up inner and outer attachment out of the desire for liberation.

gloss.en: out of the desire for liberation

units.editionTranslation: It is the man of dispassion (Vairagya) who is fit for this internal as well as external renunciation; for the dispassionate man, out of the desire to be free, relinquishes both internal and external attachment.

units.label: Verse 373
units.deva:
बहिस्तु विषयैः सङ्गं तथान्तरहमादिभिः ।
विरक्त एव शक्नोति त्यक्तुं ब्रह्मणि निष्ठितः ॥
units.iast:
bahistu viṣayaiḥ saṅgaṃ tathāntarahamādibhiḥ |
virakta eva śaknoti tyaktuṃ brahmaṇi niṣṭhitaḥ ||
units.translation: Only the dispassionate person, established in Brahman, can give up outer attachment to sense-objects and inner attachment to ego and the rest.
units.editionTranslation: It is only the dispassionate man who, being thoroughly grounded in Brahman, can give up the external attachment to the sense-objects and the internal attachment for egoism etc.

units.label: Verse 374
units.deva:
वैराग्यबोधौ पुरुषस्य पक्षिवत्
पक्षौ विजानीहि विचक्षण त्वम् ।
विमुक्तिसौधाग्रलताधिरोहणं
ताभ्यां विना नान्यतरेण सिध्यति ॥
units.iast:
vairāgyabodhau puruṣasya pakṣivat
pakṣau vijānīhi vicakṣaṇa tvam |
vimuktisaudhāgralatādhirohaṇaṃ
tābhyāṃ vinā nānyatareṇa sidhyati ||
units.translation: O discerning one, know dispassion and knowledge to be a person’s two wings, like a bird’s. Climbing the creeper atop liberation’s palace is not accomplished by either one alone.

gloss.en: climbing the creeper atop liberation’s palace

units.editionTranslation: Know, O wise man, dispassion and discrimination to be like the two wings of a bird in the case of an aspirant. Unless both are there, none can, with the help of either one, reach the creeper of Liberation that grows, as it were, on the top of an edifice.

units.label: Verse 375
units.deva:
अत्यन्तवैराग्यवतः समाधिः
समाहितस्यैव दृढप्रबोधः ।
प्रबुद्धतत्त्वस्य हि बन्धमुक्तिः
मुक्तात्मनो नित्यसुखानुभूतिः ॥
units.iast:
atyantavairāgyavataḥ samādhiḥ
samāhitasyaiva dṛḍhaprabodhaḥ |
prabuddhatattvasya hi bandhamuktiḥ
muktātmano nityasukhānubhūtiḥ ||
units.translation: For one with extreme dispassion there is samādhi; only for one whose mind is collected is there firm awakening. The one awakened to Reality is free from bondage; the liberated Self experiences eternal bliss.

gloss.en: for one whose mind is collected

units.editionTranslation: The extremely dispassionate man alone has Samadhi, and the man of Samadhi alone gets steady realisation; the man who has realised the Truth is alone free from bondage, and the free soul only experiences eternal Bliss.

units.label: Verse 376
units.deva:
वैराग्यान् न परं सुखस्य जनकं पश्यामि वश्यात्मनः
तच्चेच्छुद्धतरात्मबोधसहितं स्वाराज्यसाम्राज्यधुक् ।
एतद्द्वारमजस्रमुक्तियुवतेर्यस्मात्त्वमस्मात्परं
सर्वत्रास्पृहया सदात्मनि सदा प्रज्ञां कुरु श्रेयसे ॥
units.iast:
vairāgyān na paraṃ sukhasya janakaṃ paśyāmi vaśyātmanaḥ
taccecchuddhatarātmabodhasahitaṃ svārājyasāmrājyadhuk |
etaddvāramajasramuktiyuvateryasmāttvamasmātparaṃ
sarvatrāspṛhayā sadātmani sadā prajñāṃ kuru śreyase ||
units.translation: For one whose mind is controlled, I see no greater source of happiness than dispassion. If joined with clearer knowledge of the Self, it bestows self-sovereignty and supreme dominion. Since this is the doorway to the everlasting maiden of liberation, for your highest good, go beyond [all else], remain desireless everywhere, and keep your awareness always in the Self.

gloss.en: for one whose mind is controlled
joined with clearer knowledge of the Self
of the everlasting maiden of liberation

units.editionTranslation: For the man of self-control I do not find any better instrument of happiness than dispassion, and if that is coupled with a highly pure realisation of the Self, it conduces to the suzerainty of absolute Independence; and since this is the gateway to the damsel of everlasting liberation, therefore for thy welfare, be dispassionate both internally and externally, and always fix thy mind on the eternal Self.

units.label: Verse 377
units.deva:
आशां छिन्द्धि विषोपमेषु विषयेष्वेषैव मृत्योः कृतिस्
त्यक्त्वा जातिकुलाश्रमेष्वभिमतिं मुञ्चातिदूरात्क्रियाः ।
देहादावसति त्यजात्मधिषणां प्रज्ञां कुरुष्वात्मनि
त्वं द्रष्टास्यमनोऽसि निर्द्वयपरं ब्रह्मासि यद्वस्तुतः ॥
units.iast:
āśāṃ chinddhi viṣopameṣu viṣayeṣveṣaiva mṛtyoḥ kṛtis
tyaktvā jātikulāśrameṣvabhimatiṃ muñcātidūrātkriyāḥ |
dehādāvasati tyajātmadhiṣaṇāṃ prajñāṃ kuruṣvātmani
tvaṃ draṣṭāsyamano'si nirdvayaparaṃ brahmāsi yadvastutaḥ ||
units.translation: Cut off desire for sense-objects that are like poison; this alone is the work of death. Abandon pride in caste, family, and life-stage, and cast actions far away. Give up the notion that the body and such things are the Self, and establish your awareness in the Self. In reality, you are the Witness, beyond mind; you are nondual, supreme Brahman.

gloss.en: in the body and the rest
the notion of [them as] the Self

units.editionTranslation: Sever thy craving for the sense-objects, which are like poison, for it is the very image of death, and giving up thy pride of caste, family and order of life, fling actions to a distance. Give up thy identification with such unreal things as the body, and fix thy mind on the Atman. For thou art really the Witness, Brahman, unshackled by the mind, the One without a second, and Supreme.

units.label: Verse 378
units.deva:
लक्ष्ये ब्रह्मणि मानसं दृढतरं संस्थाप्य बाह्येन्द्रियं
स्वस्थाने विनिवेश्य निश्चलतनुश्चोपेक्ष्य देहस्थितिम् ।
ब्रह्मात्मैक्यमुपेत्य तन्मयतया चाखण्डवृत्त्यानिशं
ब्रह्मानन्दरसं पिबात्मनि मुदा शून्यैः किमन्यैर् भृशम् ॥
units.iast:
lakṣye brahmaṇi mānasaṃ dṛḍhataraṃ saṃsthāpya bāhyendriyaṃ
svasthāne viniveśya niścalatanuścopekṣya dehasthitim |
brahmātmaikyamupetya tanmayatayā cākhaṇḍavṛttyāniśaṃ
brahmānandarasaṃ pibātmani mudā śūnyaiḥ kimanyair bhṛśam ||
units.translation: Fix the mind very firmly on Brahman, the goal, and place the external senses in their own proper places. With the body still, disregard its condition. Having attained the unity of Brahman and Self and become absorbed in That, continually drink with joy in the Self the essence of Brahman’s bliss through unbroken awareness. What great use are other empty things?

gloss.en: the unity of Brahman and Self

units.editionTranslation: Fixing the mind firmly on the Ideal, Brahman, and restraining the external organs in their respective centres; with the body held steady and taking no thought for its maintenance; attaining identity with Brahman and being one with It – always drink joyfully of the Bliss of Brahman in thy own Self, without a break. What is the use of other things which are entirely hollow ?

units.label: Verse 379
units.deva:
अनात्मचिन्तनं त्यक्त्वा कश्मलं दुःखकारणम् ।
चिन्तयात्मानमानन्दरूपं यन्मुक्तिकारणम् ॥
units.iast:
anātmacintanaṃ tyaktvā kaśmalaṃ duḥkhakāraṇam |
cintayātmānamānandarūpaṃ yanmuktikāraṇam ||
units.translation: Having abandoned thought of the non-Self, the defilement that causes sorrow, contemplate the Self, whose nature is bliss and which is the cause of liberation.
units.editionTranslation: Giving up the thought of the non-Self which is evil and productive of misery, think of the Self, the Bliss Absolute, which conduces to Liberation.

units.label: Verse 380
units.deva:
एष स्वयंज्योतिरशेषसाक्षी
विज्ञानकोशे विलसत्यजस्रम् ।
लक्ष्यं विधायैनमसद्विलक्षणम्
अखण्डवृत्त्यात्मतयानुभावय ॥
units.iast:
eṣa svayaṃjyotiraśeṣasākṣī
vijñānakośe vilasatyajasram |
lakṣyaṃ vidhāyainamasadvilakṣaṇam
akhaṇḍavṛttyātmatayānubhāvaya ||
units.translation: This self-luminous witness of all shines continually in the intellect-sheath. Make this, which is distinct from the unreal, your goal; realize it as your own Self through unbroken awareness.
units.editionTranslation: Here shines eternally the Atman, the Self-effulgent Witness of everything, which has the Buddhi for Its seat. Making this Atman which is distinct from the unreal, the goal, meditate on It as thy own Self, excluding all other thought.

units.label: Verse 381
units.deva:
एतमच्छीन्नया वृत्त्या प्रत्ययान्तरशून्यया ।
उल्लेखयन्विजानीयात्स्वस्वरूपतया स्फुटम् ॥
units.iast:
etamacchīnnayā vṛttyā pratyayāntaraśūnyayā |
ullekhayanvijānīyātsvasvarūpatayā sphuṭam ||
units.translation: Keeping this in view through an unbroken mental mode, free of any other cognition, one should clearly know it as one’s own true nature.
units.editionTranslation: Reflecting on this Atman continuously and without any foreign thought intervening, one must distinctly realise It to be one’s real Self.

units.label: Verse 382
units.deva:
अत्रात्मत्वं दृढीकुर्वन्नहमादिषु संत्यजन् ।
उदासीनतया तेषु तिष्ठेत्स्फुटघटादिवत् ॥
units.iast:
atrātmatvaṃ dṛḍhīkurvannahamādiṣu saṃtyajan |
udāsīnatayā teṣu tiṣṭhetsphuṭaghaṭādivat ||
units.translation: Firmly establish the sense of Self here, abandoning identification with ego and the rest; remain indifferent toward them, as toward a broken pot and the like.

gloss.en: as with a broken pot and the like

units.editionTranslation: Strengthening one’s identification with This, and giving up that with egoism and the rest, one must live without any concern for them, as if they were trifling things, like a cracked jar or the like.

units.label: Verse 383
units.deva:
विशुद्धमन्तःकरणं स्वरूपे
निवेश्य साक्षिण्य् अवबोधमात्रे ।
शनैः शनैर् निश्चलतामुपानयन्
पूर्णं स्वमेवानुविलोकयेत्ततः ॥
units.iast:
viśuddhamantaḥkaraṇaṃ svarūpe
niveśya sākṣiṇy avabodhamātre |
śanaiḥ śanair niścalatāmupānayan
pūrṇaṃ svamevānuvilokayettataḥ ||
units.translation: Having placed the purified inner instrument in its own nature and in the Witness, which is pure awareness alone, and gradually brought it to stillness, one should then behold one’s own complete Self.
units.editionTranslation: Fixing the purified mind in the Self, the Witness, the Knowledge Absolute, and slowly making it still, one must then realise one’s own infinite Self.

units.label: Verse 384
units.deva:
देहेन्द्रियप्राणमनोऽहम् आदिभिः
स्वाज्ञानकॢप्तैर् अखिलैर् उपाधिभिः ।
विमुक्तमात्मानमखण्डरूपं
पूर्णं महाकाशमिवावलोकयेत् ॥
units.iast:
dehendriyaprāṇamano'ham ādibhiḥ
svājñānakḷptair akhilair upādhibhiḥ |
vimuktamātmānamakhaṇḍarūpaṃ
pūrṇaṃ mahākāśamivāvalokayet ||
units.translation: Behold the Self as complete and indivisible, free from all limiting adjuncts—body, senses, vital breath, mind, ego, and the rest—created by your own ignorance, like the vast sky.

gloss.en: with body, senses, vital breath, mind, ego, and the rest

units.editionTranslation: One should behold the Atman, the Indivisible and Infinite, free from all limiting adjuncts such as the body, organs, Pranas, Manas and egoism, which are creations of one’s own ignorance – like the infinite sky.

units.label: Verse 385
units.deva:
घटकलशकुसूलसूचिमुख्यैः
गगनमुपाधिशतैर् विमुक्तमेकम् ।
भवति न विविधं तथैव शुद्धं
परमहमादिविमुक्तमेकम् एव ॥
units.iast:
ghaṭakalaśakusūlasūcimukhyaiḥ
gaganamupādhiśatair vimuktamekam |
bhavati na vividhaṃ tathaiva śuddhaṃ
paramahamādivimuktamekam eva ||
units.translation: The sky, freed from hundreds of limiting adjuncts—pot, jar, grain-bin, needle, and the like—remains one, not many. In the same way, the pure Supreme, free from ego and the rest, is one alone.

gloss.en: such as pot, jar, grain-bin, and needle
freed from ego and the rest

units.editionTranslation: The sky, divested of the hundreds of limiting adjuncts such as a jar, a pitcher, a receptacle for grains or a needle, is one, and not diverse; exactly in a similar way the pure Brahman, when divested of egoism etc., is verily One.

units.label: Verse 386
units.deva:
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्बपर्यन्ता मृषामात्रा उपाधयः ।
ततः पूर्णं स्वमात्मानं पश्येदेकात्मना स्थितम् ॥
units.iast:
brahmādistambaparyantā mṛṣāmātrā upādhayaḥ |
tataḥ pūrṇaṃ svamātmānaṃ paśyedekātmanā sthitam ||
units.translation: From Brahmā down to a blade of grass, the limiting adjuncts are nothing but unreal. Therefore one should see one’s own complete Self as established in the one Self.

gloss.en: extending from Brahmā down to a blade of grass

units.editionTranslation: The limiting adjuncts from Brahma down to a clump of grass are all wholly unreal. Therefore one should realise one’s own Infinite Self as the only Principle.

units.label: Verse 387
units.deva:
यत्र भ्रान्त्या कल्पितं तद्विवेके
तत्तन्मात्रं नैव तस्माद्विभिन्नम् ।
भ्रान्तेर्नाशे भाति दृष्टाहितत्त्वं
रज्जुस्तद्वद्विश्वम् आत्मस्वरूपम् ॥
units.iast:
yatra bhrāntyā kalpitaṃ tad viveke
tat-tan-mātraṃ naiva tasmād vibhinnam |
bhrānter nāśe bhāti dṛṣṭā hi tattvaṃ
rajjuḥ tadvat viśvam ātmasvarūpam ||
units.translation: Whatever is imagined through delusion in something is, upon discrimination, only that itself and not at all different from it. When delusion is destroyed, the truth that was seen shines forth, as with a rope; likewise, the universe is the very nature of the Self.
units.editionTranslation: That in which something is imagined to exist through error, is, when rightly discriminated, that thing itself, and not distinct from it. When the error is gone, the reality about the snake falsely perceived becomes the rope. Similarly the universe is in reality the Atman.

units.label: Verse 388
units.deva:
स्वयं ब्रह्मा स्वयं विष्णुः स्वयमिन्द्रः स्वयं शिवः ।
स्वयं विश्वमिदं सर्वं स्वस्मादन्यन् न किंचन ॥
units.iast:
svayaṃ brahmā svayaṃ viṣṇuḥ svayamindraḥ svayaṃ śivaḥ |
svayaṃ viśvamidaṃ sarvaṃ svasmādanyan na kiṃcana ||
units.translation: The Self itself is Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, and Śiva; the Self itself is this whole universe. Nothing whatsoever is other than the Self.
units.editionTranslation: The Self is Brahma, the Self is Vishnu, the Self is Indra, the Self is Shiva; the Self is all this universe. Nothing exists except the Self.

units.label: Verse 389
units.deva:
अन्तः स्वयं चापि बहिः स्वयं च
स्वयं पुरस्तात् स्वयम् एव पश्चात् ।
स्वयं ह्यावाच्यां स्वयमप्युदीच्यां
तथोपरिष्टात्स्वयमप्यधस्तात् ॥
units.iast:
antaḥ svayaṃ cāpi bahiḥ svayaṃ ca
svayaṃ purastāt svayam eva paścāt |
svayaṃ hyāvācyāṃ svayamapyudīcyāṃ
tathopariṣṭātsvayamapyadhastāt ||
units.translation: The Self itself is within and without, in front and behind, in the south and also in the north; likewise, the Self itself is above and below.
units.editionTranslation: The Self is within, and the Self is without; the Self is before and the Self is behind; the Self is in the south, and the Self is in the north; the Self likewise is above as also below.

units.label: Verse 390
units.deva:
तरङ्गफेनभ्रमबुद्बुदादि
सर्वं स्वरूपेण जलं यथा तथा ।
चिद् एव देहाद्यहमन्तमेतत्
सर्वं चिद् एवैकरसं विशुद्धम् ॥
units.iast:
taraṅgaphenabhramabudbudādi
sarvaṃ svarūpeṇa jalaṃ yathā tathā |
cid eva dehādyahamantametat
sarvaṃ cid evaikarasaṃ viśuddham ||
units.translation: Just as waves, foam, whirlpools, bubbles, and the like are, in essence, water, so too all this, from the body up to the ego, is consciousness alone. Everything is consciousness alone, of one essence and pure.

gloss.en: waves, foam, whirlpools, bubbles, and the like

units.editionTranslation: As the wave, the foam, the whirlpool, the bubble, etc., are all in essence but water, similarly the Chit (Knowledge Absolute) is all this, from the body up to egoism. Everything is verily the Chit, homogeneous and pure.

units.label: Verse 391
units.deva:
सदेवेदं सर्वं जगदवगतं वाङ्मनसयोः
सतोऽन्यन्नास्त्य् एव प्रकृतिपरसीम्नि स्थितवतः ।
पृथक् किं मृत्स्नायाः कलशघटकुम्भाद्यवगतं
वदत्येष भ्रान्तस्त्वमहमिति मायामदिरया ॥
units.iast:
sadevedaṃ sarvaṃ jagadavagataṃ vāṅmanasayoḥ
sato'nyannāsty eva prakṛtiparasīmni sthitavataḥ |
pṛthak kiṃ mṛtsnāyāḥ kalaśaghaṭakumbhādyavagataṃ
vadatyeṣa bhrāntastvamahamiti māyāmadirayā ||
units.translation: All this world, known through speech and mind, is Existence alone. For one established beyond Nature’s limit, nothing at all is other than Existence. Are jars, pots, pitchers, and the like known to be separate from clay? The deluded one, intoxicated by Māyā’s wine, says, “you” and “I.”

gloss.en: jar, pot, pitcher, and the like

units.editionTranslation: All this universe known through speech and mind is nothing but Brahman; there is nothing besides Brahman, which exists beyond the utmost range of the Prakriti. Are the pitcher, jug, jar, etc., known to be distinct from the clay of which they are composed ? It is the deluded man who talks of "thou" and "I", as an effect of the wine of Maya.

units.label: Verse 392
units.deva:
क्रियासमभिहारेण यत्र नान्यदिति श्रुतिः ।
ब्रवीति द्वैतराहित्यं मिथ्याध्यासनिवृत्तये ॥
units.iast:
kriyāsamabhihāreṇa yatra nānyaditi śrutiḥ |
bravīti dvaitarāhityaṃ mithyādhyāsanivṛttaye ||
units.translation: Through a repeated series of verbs such as “where there is nothing else,” scripture declares the absence of duality in order to remove false superimposition.

gloss.en: through a repeated series of verbs
for the removal of false superimposition

units.editionTranslation: The Shruti, in the passage, "Where one sees nothing else", etc., declares by an accumulation of verbs the absence of duality, in order to remove the false superimpositions.

units.label: Verse 393
units.deva:
आकाशवन्निर्मलनिर्विकल्पं
निःसीमनिःस्पन्दननिर्विकारम् ।
अन्तर्बहिःशून्यमनन्यमद्वयं
स्वयं परं ब्रह्म किमस्ति बोध्यम् ॥
units.iast:
ākāśavan nirmala-nirvikalpaṃ
niḥsīma-niḥspandana-nirvikāram |
antarbahiḥśūnyam ananyam advayaṃ
svayaṃ paraṃ brahma kim asti bodhyam ||
units.translation: Like space, [Brahman is] pure and free from thought-constructs, limitless, motionless, changeless, empty of inside and outside, without another, nondual—the Self itself, the Supreme Brahman. Is there anything else to be known?
units.editionTranslation: The Supreme Brahman is, like the sky, pure, absolute, infinite, motionless and changeless, devoid of interior or exterior, the One Existence, without a second, and is one’s own Self. Is there any other object of knowledge ?

units.label: Verse 394
units.deva:
वक्तव्यं किमु विद्यतेऽत्र बहुधा ब्रह्मैव जीवः स्वयं
ब्रह्मैतज्जगदाततं नु सकलं ब्रह्माद्वितीयं श्रुतिः ।
ब्रह्मैवाहमिति प्रबुद्धमतयः संत्यक्तबाह्याः स्फुटं
ब्रह्मीभूय वसन्ति सन्ततचिदानन्दात्मनैतद्ध्रुवम् ॥
units.iast:
vaktavyaṃ kimu vidyate'tra bahudhā brahmaiva jīvaḥ svayaṃ
brahmaitajjagadātataṃ nu sakalaṃ brahmādvitīyaṃ śrutiḥ |
brahmaivāhamiti prabuddhamatayaḥ saṃtyaktabāhyāḥ sphuṭaṃ
brahmībhūya vasanti santatacidānandātmanaitaddhruvam ||
units.translation: What more is there to say here at length? The individual self is Brahman alone; this entire, extended universe is Brahman, indeed all of it; scripture says Brahman is nondual. Those of awakened understanding, knowing “I am Brahman alone” and having clearly renounced external things, abide as Brahman, with continuous consciousness and bliss as their nature. This is certain.

gloss.en: with continuous consciousness and bliss as their nature

units.editionTranslation: What is the use of dilating on this subject ? The Jiva is no other than Brahman; this whole extended universe is Brahman Itself; the Shruti inculcates the Brahman without a second; and it is an indubitable fact that people of enlightened minds who know their identity with Brahman and have given up their connection with the objective world, live palpably unifold with Brahman as Eternal Knowledge and Bliss.

units.label: Verse 395
units.deva:
जहि मलमयकोशेऽहंधियोत्थापिताशां
प्रसभमनिलकल्पे लिङ्गदेहेऽपि पश्चात् ।
निगमगदितकीर्तिं नित्यमानन्दमूर्तिं
स्वयमिति परिचीय ब्रह्मरूपेण तिष्ठ ॥
units.iast:
jahi malamayakośe'haṃdhiyotthāpitāśāṃ
prasabhamanilakalpe liṅgadehe'pi paścāt |
nigamagaditakīrtiṃ nityamānandamūrtiṃ
svayamiti paricīya brahmarūpeṇa tiṣṭha ||
units.translation: Destroy the desire raised by egoic thought in the impurity-filled sheath; then forcibly destroy it also in the subtle body, which is like wind. Recognize as your own Self the eternal embodiment of bliss whose glory the Vedas proclaim, and abide as Brahman.
units.editionTranslation: (First) destroy the hopes raised by egoism in this filthy gross body, then do the same forcibly with the air-like subtle body; and realising Brahman, the embodiment of eternal Bliss – whose glories the Scriptures proclaim – as thy own Self, live as Brahman.

units.label: Verse 396
units.deva:
शवाकारं यावद्भजति मनुजस्तावदशुचिः
परेभ्यः स्यात्क्लेशो जननमरणव्याधिनिलयः ।
यदात्मानं शुद्धं कलयति शिवाकारमचलम्
तदा तेभ्यो मुक्तो भवति हि तदाह श्रुतिर् अपि ॥
units.iast:
śavākāraṃ yāvadbhajati manujastāvadaśuciḥ
parebhyaḥ syātkleśo jananamaraṇavyādhinilayaḥ |
yadātmānaṃ śuddhaṃ kalayati śivākāramacalam
tadā tebhyo mukto bhavati hi tadāha śrutir api ||
units.translation: As long as a person identifies with the corpse-like body, the person is impure and suffers from others, as well as from birth, death, and disease. When one regards the Self as pure, auspicious in nature, and unmoving, one becomes free from these; scripture too declares this.

gloss.en: the abode of birth, death, and disease

units.editionTranslation: So long as man has any regard for this corpse-like body, he is impure, and suffers from his enemies as also from birth, death and disease; but when he thinks of himself as pure, as the essence of good and immovable, he assuredly becomes free from them; the Shrutis also say this.

units.label: Verse 397
units.deva:
स्वात्मन्यारोपिताशेषाभासवस्तुनिरासतः ।
स्वयमेव परं ब्रह्म पूर्णमद्वयमक्रियम् ॥
units.iast:
svātmany āropitāśeṣābhāsavastu-nirāsataḥ |
svayam eva paraṃ brahma pūrṇam advayam akriyam ||
units.translation: By removing all apparent things superimposed on the Self, the Supreme Brahman alone—complete, nondual, and actionless—remains as itself.
units.editionTranslation: By the elimination of all apparent existences superimposed on the soul, the supreme Brahman, Infinite, the One without a second and beyond action, remains as Itself.

units.label: Verse 398
units.deva:
समाहितायां सति चित्तवृत्तौ
परात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे ।
न दृश्यते कश्चिदयं विकल्पः
प्रजल्पमात्रः परिशिष्यते यतः ॥
units.iast:
samāhitāyāṃ sati cittavṛttau
parātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe |
na dṛśyate kaścidayaṃ vikalpaḥ
prajalpamātraḥ pariśiṣyate yataḥ ||
units.translation: When the mind’s activity is absorbed in the Supreme Self, Brahman free from thought-constructs, none of this differentiation is seen; it remains only as idle talk.
units.editionTranslation: When the mind-functions are merged in the Paramatman, the Brahman, the Absolute, none of this phenomenal world is seen, whence it is reduced to mere talk.

units.label: Verse 399
units.deva:
असत्कल्पो विकल्पोऽयं विश्वमित्येकवस्तुनि ।
निर्विकारे निराकारे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥
units.iast:
asatkalpo vikalpo'yaṃ viśvamityekavastuni |
nirvikāre nirākāre nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ ||
units.translation: This notion, “the universe,” is as good as unreal in the one Reality. How could there be difference in that which is changeless, formless, and without qualities?
units.editionTranslation: In the One Entity (Brahman) the conception of the universe is a mere phantom. Whence can there be any diversity in That which is changeless, formless and Absolute ?

units.label: Verse 400
units.deva:
द्रष्टृदर्शनदृश्यादिभावशून्यैकवस्तुनि ।
निर्विकारे निराकारे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥
units.iast:
draṣṭṛdarśanadṛśyādibhāvaśūnyaikavastuni |
nirvikāre nirākāre nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ ||
units.translation: In the one Reality, free from the distinctions of seer, seeing, seen, and the rest, changeless, formless, and without qualities, where could difference be?

gloss.en: free from the distinctions of seer, seeing, seen, and the rest

units.editionTranslation: In the One Entity devoid of the concepts of seer, seeing and seen – which is changeless, formless and Absolute – whence can there be any diversity ?

units.label: Verse 401
units.deva:
कल्पार्णव इवात्यन्तपरिपूर्णैकवस्तुनि ।
निर्विकारे निराकारे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥
units.iast:
kalpārṇava ivātyantaparipūrṇaikavastuni |
nirvikāre nirākāre nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ ||
units.translation: How could there be difference in the one Reality, utterly full like the ocean of cosmic dissolution, changeless, formless, and without distinctions?
units.editionTranslation: In the One Entity which is changeless, formless and Absolute, and which is perfectly all-pervading and motionless like the ocean after the dissolution of the universe, whence can there be any diversity ?

units.label: Verse 402
units.deva:
तेजसीव तमो यत्र प्रलीनं भ्रान्तिकारणम् ।
अद्वितीये परे तत्त्वे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥
units.iast:
tejasīva tamo yatra pralīnaṃ bhrāntikāraṇam |
advitīye pare tattve nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ ||
units.translation: Where the cause of delusion is dissolved like darkness in light, in the nondual, supreme, distinctionless Reality, whence could difference be?
units.editionTranslation: Where the root of delusion is dissolved like darkness in light – in the supreme Reality, the One without a second, the Absolute – whence can there be any diversity ?

units.label: Verse 403
units.deva:
एकात्मके परे तत्त्वे भेदवार्ता कथं वसेत् ।
सुषुप्तौ सुखमात्रायां भेदः केनावलोकितः ॥
units.iast:
ekātmake pare tattve bhedavārtā kathaṃ vaset |
suṣuptau sukhamātrāyāṃ bhedaḥ kenāvalokitaḥ ||
units.translation: How can talk of difference remain in the supreme Reality, which is one in nature? Who has perceived difference in deep sleep, where there is bliss alone?
units.editionTranslation: How can the talk of diversity apply to the Supreme Reality which is one and homogeneous ? Who has ever observed diversity in the unmixed bliss of the state of profound sleep ?

units.label: Verse 404
units.deva:
न ह्यस्ति विश्वं परतत्त्वबोधात्
सदात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे ।
कालत्रये नाप्यहिरीक्षितो गुणे
न ह्यम्बुबिन्दुर्मृगतृष्णिकायाम् ॥
units.iast:
na hyasti viśvaṃ paratattvabodhāt
sadātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe |
kālatraye nāpyahirīkṣito guṇe
na hyambubindurmṛgatṛṣṇikāyām ||
units.translation: In the knowledge of the Supreme Reality, the universe is not present in Brahman—the changeless Self that is Existence. At no time is a snake seen in a rope, nor is a drop of water seen in a mirage.

gloss.en: through knowledge of the Supreme Reality
in the Self that is Existence
in the three periods of time

units.editionTranslation: Even before the realisation of the highest Truth, the universe does not exist in the Absolute Brahman, the Essence of Existence. In none of the three states of time is the snake ever observed in the rope, nor a drop of water in the mirage.

units.label: Verse 405
units.deva:
मायामात्रमिदं द्वैतमद्वैतं परमार्थतः ।
इति ब्रूते श्रुतिः साक्षात्सुषुप्तावनुभूयते ॥
units.iast:
māyāmātramidaṃ dvaitamadvaitaṃ paramārthataḥ |
iti brūte śrutiḥ sākṣātsuṣuptāvanubhūyate ||
units.translation: Scripture directly declares, “This duality is only Māyā; nonduality is the ultimate reality.” This is experienced in deep sleep.
units.editionTranslation: The Shrutis themselves declare that this dualistic universe is but a delusion from the standpoint of Absolute Truth. This is also experienced in the state of dreamless sleep.

units.label: Verse 406
units.deva:
अनन्यत्वमधिष्ठानादारोप्यस्य निरीक्षितम् ।
पण्डितैरज्जुसर्पादौ विकल्पो भ्रान्तिजीवनः ॥
units.iast:
ananyatvam adhiṣṭhānād āropyasya nirīkṣitam |
paṇḍitair rajju-sarpādau vikalpo bhrānti-jīvanaḥ ||
units.translation: The wise have seen that what is superimposed is not different from its substratum, as in a rope mistaken for a snake; the imagined distinction lives by delusion.
units.editionTranslation: That which is superimposed upon something else is observed by the wise to be identical with the substratum, as in the case of the rope appearing as the snake. The apparent difference depends solely on error.

units.label: Verse 407
units.deva:
चित्तमूलो विकल्पोऽयं चित्ताभावे न कश्चन ।
अतश्चित्तं समाधेहि प्रत्यग्रूपे परात्मनि ॥
units.iast:
citta-mūlo vikalpo 'yaṃ cittābhāve na kaścana |
ataś cittaṃ samādhehi pratyag-rūpe parātmani ||
units.translation: This imagined distinction is rooted in the mind; when the mind is absent, there is nothing at all. Therefore steady the mind in the Supreme Self, whose nature is inward.
units.editionTranslation: This apparent universe has its root in the mind, and never persists after the mind is annihilated. Therefore dissolve the mind by concentrating it on the Supreme Self, which is thy inmost Essence.

units.label: Verse 408
units.deva:
किम् अपि सततबोधं केवलानन्दरूपं
निरुपममतिवेलं नित्यमुक्तं निरीहम् ।
निरवधिगगनाभं निष्कलं निर्विकल्पं
हृदि कलयति विद्वान् ब्रह्म पूर्णं समाधौ ॥
units.iast:
kim api satata-bodhaṃ kevalānanda-rūpaṃ
nirupamam ativelaṃ nitya-muktaṃ nirīham |
niravadhi-gaganābhaṃ niṣkalaṃ nirvikalpaṃ
hṛdi kalayati vidvān brahma pūrṇaṃ samādhau ||
units.translation: In samādhi, the wise person contemplates in the heart the complete Brahman: something beyond description, constant awareness, of pure-bliss nature, incomparable, beyond measure, eternally free, without desire, like the boundless sky, partless, and free from thought-constructs.
units.editionTranslation: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is something of the nature of eternal Knowledge and absolute Bliss, which has no exemplar, which transcends all limitations, is ever free and without activity, and which is like the limitless sky, indivisible and absolute.

units.label: Verse 409
units.deva:
प्रकृतिविकृतिशून्यं भावनातीतभावं
समरसम् असमानं मानसं बन्धदूरम् ।
निगमवचनसिद्धं नित्यमस्मत्प्रसिद्धं
हृदि कलयति विद्वान् ब्रह्म पूर्णं समाधौ ॥
units.iast:
prakṛti-vikṛti-śūnyaṃ bhāvanātīta-bhāvaṃ
samarasam asamānaṃ mānasaṃ bandha-dūram |
nigama-vacana-siddhaṃ nityam asmat-prasiddhaṃ
hṛdi kalayati vidvān brahma pūrṇaṃ samādhau ||
units.translation: In samādhi, the wise person contemplates in the heart the complete Brahman: free from Prakṛti and its modifications, with a nature beyond thought, of one essence, peerless, present to the mind and far from bondage, established by Vedic statements, eternal, and well-known to us.

gloss.en: free from Prakṛti and its modifications

units.editionTranslation: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is devoid of the ideas of cause and effect, which is the Reality beyond all imaginations, homogeneous, matchless, beyond the range of proofs, established by the pronouncements of the Vedas, and ever familiar to us as the sense of the ego.

units.label: Verse 410
units.deva:
अजरममरमस्ताभाववस्तुस्वरूपं
स्तिमितसलिलराशिप्रख्यमाख्याविहीनम् ।
शमितगुणविकारं शाश्वतं शान्तमेकं
हृदि कलयति विद्वान् ब्रह्म पूर्णं समाधौ ॥
units.iast:
ajaram amaram astābhāva-vastu-svarūpaṃ
stimita-salila-rāśi-prakhyam ākhyā-vihīnam |
śamita-guṇa-vikāraṃ śāśvataṃ śāntam ekam
hṛdi kalayati vidvān brahma pūrṇaṃ samādhau ||
units.translation: In samādhi, the wise person contemplates in the heart the complete Brahman: ageless and immortal, whose nature is Reality free from disappearance and non-being, resembling a still mass of water, without a name, with the guṇa-modifications quieted, eternal, peaceful, and one.

gloss.en: whose nature is Reality free from disappearance and non-being
resembling a still mass of water

units.editionTranslation: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is undecaying and immortal, the positive Entity which precludes all negations, which resembles the placid ocean and is without a name, in which there are neither merits nor demerits, and which is eternal, pacified and One.

units.label: Verse 411
units.deva:
समाहितान्तःकरणः स्वरूपे
विलोकयात्मानमखण्डवैभवम् ।
विच्छिन्द्धि बन्धं भवगन्धगन्धितं
यत्नेन पुंस्त्वं सफलीकुरुष्व ॥
units.iast:
samāhitāntaḥkaraṇaḥ svarūpe
vilokayātmānam akhaṇḍa-vaibhavam |
vicchinddhi bandhaṃ bhava-gandha-gandhitam
yatnena puṃstvaṃ saphalīkuruṣva ||
units.translation: With your inner instrument composed, behold the Self in its own nature, whose glory is undivided. Cut the bond scented with worldly existence, and through effort make your human birth fruitful.
units.editionTranslation: With the mind restrained in Samadhi, behold in thy self the Atman, of infinite glory, cut off thy bondage strengthened by the impressions of previous births, and carefully attain the consummation of thy birth as a human being.

units.label: Verse 412
units.deva:
सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्तं सच्चिदानन्दमद्वयम् ।
भावयात्मानम् आत्मस्थं न भूयः कल्पसेऽध्वने ॥
units.iast:
sarvopādhi-vinirmuktaṃ sac-cid-ānandam advayam |
bhāvayātmānam ātmasthaṃ na bhūyaḥ kalpase 'dhvane ||
units.translation: Contemplate the Self, abiding in itself, freed from every limiting adjunct, Being-Consciousness-Bliss, and nondual; you will no longer be set upon the road of becoming.

gloss.en: you are set; you become fit

units.editionTranslation: Meditate on the Atman, which resides in thee, which is devoid of all limiting adjuncts, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, and thou shalt no more come under the round of births and deaths.

units.label: Verse 413
units.deva:
छायेव पुंसः परिदृश्यमानम् आभासरूपेण फलानुभूत्या ।
शरीरमाराच्छववन्निरस्तं पुनर्न संधत्त इदं महात्मा ॥
units.iast:
chāyeva puṃsaḥ paridṛśyamānam ābhāsa-rūpeṇa phalānubhūtyā |
śarīram ārāt śava-vad nirastaṃ punar na saṃdhatta idaṃ mahātmā ||
units.translation: Though, through the experience of its results, this body appears like a person's shadow, the great one does not take it up again after casting it far away like a corpse.

gloss.en: in the form of an appearance

units.editionTranslation: After the body has once been cast off to a distance like a corpse, the sage never more attaches himself to it, though it is visible as an appearance, like the shadow of a man, owing to the experience of the effects of past deeds.

units.label: Verse 414
units.deva:
सततविमलबोधानन्दरूपं समेत्य
त्यज जडमलरूपोपाधिमेतं सुदूरे ।
अथ पुनरपि नैष स्मर्यतां वान्तवस्तु
स्मरणविषयभूतं कल्पते कुत्सनाय ॥
units.iast:
satata-vimala-bodhānanda-rūpaṃ sametya
tyaja jaḍa-mala-rūpa-upādhim etaṃ sudūre |
atha punar api naiṣa smaryatāṃ vānta-vastu
smaraṇa-viṣaya-bhūtaṃ kalpate kutsanāya ||
units.translation: Having attained the Self whose nature is constant, pure awareness and bliss, abandon far away this limiting adjunct, inert and impure in nature. Do not remember it again: a vomited thing, when made an object of memory, serves only to disgust.

gloss.en: whose nature is constant, pure awareness and bliss
the limiting adjunct, inert and impure in nature

units.editionTranslation: Realising the Atman, the eternal, pure Knowledge and Bliss, throw far away this limitation of a body, which is inert and filthy by nature. Then remember it no more, for something that has been vomited excites but disgust when called in memory.

units.label: Verse 415
units.deva:
समूलमेतत्परिदाह्य वह्नौ
सदात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे ।
ततः स्वयं नित्यविशुद्धबोधा-
नन्दात्मना तिष्ठति विद्वरिष्ठः ॥
units.iast:
samūlam etat paridāhya vahnau
sadātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe |
tataḥ svayaṃ nitya-viśuddha-bodhā-
nandātmanā tiṣṭhati vidvariṣṭhaḥ ||
units.translation: Having burned all this, root and all, in the fire of the Real Self—nondual Brahman—the foremost among the wise then remains as the Self of eternal, pure awareness and bliss.

gloss.en: as the Self of eternal, pure awareness and bliss

units.editionTranslation: Burning all this, with its very root, in the fire of Brahman, the Eternal and Absolute Self, the truly wise man thereafter remains alone, as the Atman, the eternal, pure Knowledge and Bliss.

units.label: Verse 416
units.deva:
प्रारब्धसूत्रग्रथितं शरीरं
प्रयातु वा तिष्ठतु गोरिव स्रक् ।
न तत् पुनः पश्यति तत्त्ववेत्ता आनन्दात्मनि
ब्रह्मणि लीनवृत्तिः ॥
units.iast:
prārabdha-sūtra-grathitaṃ śarīraṃ
prayātu vā tiṣṭhatu gor iva srak |
na tat punaḥ paśyati tattva-vettā ānanda-ātmani
brahmaṇi līna-vṛttiḥ ||
units.translation: The body, woven from the threads of prārabdha, may depart or remain, like a garland on a cow. The knower of Truth, whose mind is absorbed in Brahman, the Self of Bliss, no longer regards it.

gloss.en: woven from the threads of already-begun karma

units.editionTranslation: The knower of Truth does no more care whether this body, spun out by the threads of Prarabdha work, falls or remains – like the garland on a cow – for his mind-functions are at rest in the Brahman, the Essence of Bliss.

units.label: Verse 417
units.deva:
अखण्डानन्दमात्मानं विज्ञाय स्वस्वरूपतः ।
किमिच्छन् कस्य वा हेतुर्देहं पुष्णाति तत्त्ववित् ॥
units.iast:
akhaṇḍānandam ātmānaṃ vijñāya sva-svarūpataḥ |
kim icchan kasya vā hetor dehaṃ puṣṇāti tattvavit ||
units.translation: Having known the Self as his own nature, undivided Bliss, what could the knower of Truth desire, and for whose sake would he nourish the body?
units.editionTranslation: Realising the Atman, the Infinite Bliss, as his very Self, with what object, or for whom, should the knower of Truth cherish the body.

units.label: Verse 418
units.deva:
संसिद्धस्य फलं त्वेतज्जीवन्मुक्तस्य योगिनः ।
बहिरन्तः सदानन्दरसास्वादनम् आत्मनि ॥
units.iast:
saṃsiddhasya phalaṃ tu etaj jīvan-muktasya yoginaḥ |
bahir antaḥ sadā ānanda-rasa-āsvādanam ātmani ||
units.translation: For the perfected yogi who is liberated while living, this is the fruit: tasting within and without the ever-present essence of bliss in the Self.
units.editionTranslation: The Yogi who has attained perfection and is liberated-in-life gets this as result – he enjoys eternal Bliss in his mind, internally as well as externally.

units.label: Verse 419
units.deva:
वैराग्यस्य फलं बोधो बोधस्योपरतिः फलम् ।
स्वानन्दानुभवाच्छान्तिरेषैवोपरतेः फलम् ॥
units.iast:
vairāgyasya phalaṃ bodho bodhasyoparatiḥ phalam |
svānandānubhavāc chāntir eṣaivoparateḥ phalam ||
units.translation: The fruit of dispassion is knowledge; the fruit of knowledge is withdrawal. Peace comes from experiencing one's own bliss: that alone is the fruit of withdrawal.
units.editionTranslation: The result of dispassion is knowledge, that of Knowledge is withdrawal from sense-pleasures, which leads to the experience of the Bliss of the Self, whence follows Peace.

units.label: Verse 420
units.deva:
यद्युत्तरोत्तराभावः पूर्वपूर्वं तु निष्फलम् ।
निवृत्तिः परमा तृप्तिरानन्दोऽनुपमः स्वतः ॥
units.iast:
yady uttarottarābhāvaḥ pūrva-pūrvaṃ tu niṣphalam |
nivṛttiḥ paramā tṛptir ānando 'nupamaḥ svataḥ ||
units.translation: If each later stage is absent, each earlier stage is fruitless. Withdrawal, supreme contentment, and incomparable bliss come naturally.

gloss.en: the absence of each successive stage

units.editionTranslation: If there is an absence of the succeeding stages, the preceding ones are futile. (When the series is perfect) the cessation of the objective world, extreme satisfaction, and matchless bliss follow as a matter of course.

units.label: Verse 421
units.deva:
दृष्टदुःखेष्वनुद्वेगो विद्यायाः प्रस्तुतं फलम् ।
यत्कृतं भ्रान्तिवेलायां नाना कर्म जुगुप्सितम्
